A UK minister has been accused of telling “fibs” after saying GB Energy was “never meant” to employ 1,000 people in Aberdeen.

Martin McCluskey said the UK Government was aiming to employ 300 direct employees at its headquarters.

The SNP described the remark as “shameful” and accused Labour of breaking its promises.

GB Energy chairman Jürgen Maier told MPs after the 2024 election that GB Energy could create more than 1,000 more jobs at the HQ in the north east, although he said the target could take decades to hit.

open image in gallery (second left to right) Anas Sarwar, Sir Keir Starmer, Ed Miliband and Martin McCluskey at the Port of Greenock while on the general election campaign trail in 2024 (Stefan Rousseau/PA) ( PA Archive )

He later said the publicly-owned company would only create “200 or 300 jobs in Aberdeen by 2031”.

Asked about the 1,000 jobs figure, Mr McCluskey, minister of energy and jobs, told Times Radio the UK Government was aiming “towards about 300 direct employees” before adding “but it was never meant to be direct employees”.

Jack Middleton, SNP MSP for Aberdeen Central, said: “Never mind creating 1,000 jobs in Aberdeen, the Labour Party is destroying 1,000 energy jobs a month through their hated tax on Scotland’s energy.

“This is shameful stuff because not only have the Labour Party broken their 1,000 jobs promise, they actually committed to 70,000 jobs meanwhile energy bills are set to be £1,000 higher than they pledged too.

“No wonder Martin McCluskey is telling fibs – his Government shut down Grangemouth and is ruining Scotland’s premier offshore industry.

“It’s no wonder people in energy-rich Scotland are concluding we need a fresh start with independence to put Scotland’s energy in Scotland’s hands.”

News.title: Fiji declares national crisis as HIV epidemic escalates
News.content:
“The rollout has been slow and frustrating, and Fiji will pay for it in terms of lives lost,” said Prof Lisa Maher, an epidemiologist at the Kirby Institute in Sydney who is supporting Fiji’s response. “This is the only thing that will turn the epidemic around and stop people dying, and stop onward transmission of HIV to the general population.”

But the emergency declaration should provide political cover to introduce the needle and syringe programme, with a Cabinet subcommittee now created to remove barriers to action.

“The government is signalling that it is prepared to act in this particularly important and controversial area,” said Prof Maher. “It’s not coincidental that the draft bill [to legalise the distribution of needles and syringes for certain groups] now looks likely to go before parliament, after being blocked for 10 months… So it’s not just symbolic.”

Dr Jason Mitchell, head of Fiji’s HIV taskforce, added: “Since the government announced [the crisis], it has followed with some very rapid actions in progressing the needle and syringe programme. So that is being fast tracked through the necessary channels, and the government is determined to get that out in the next couple of weeks.

“We’ve gotten to the point where we really needed to take some really strong action,” he told The Telegraph. “This is the government realising that there have been challenges, and they need to step it up.”

It is hoped that the declaration will also turbocharge other elements of the response – for instance the scale-up of the post-exposure prophylaxis (Prep) scheme, which was introduced in May – as the virus gains a foothold in the broader population.

Although there has been a major focus on testing, treatment and education, UNAIDS still estimates that only 39 per cent of an estimated 9,100 people living with HIV in 2025 knew their positive status. Just 22 per cent were accessing antiretroviral treatment, and 117 people died in 2025, compared to 25 in 2021.

News.title: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing
News.content:
There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

News.title: Banton shows his worth as England cruise to series victory against Sri Lanka
News.content:
A patchy Test team and a one-day international side learning on the job should not obscure the fact that under Harry Brook, England have built a formidable T20 outfit.

Missing a slew of first-choice players, they dispatched Sri Lanka with a game to spare and an emphatic show of their depth in the format, with Sonny Baker and Tom Banton – two men still finding their feet in the side – to the fore. England have now won 20 of the 23 completed T20s since Brook took over last year, and six matches in a row this summer. It is easily their best format and, as Liam Dawson said, they have “match-winners throughout” and plenty of “freak” performers.

In this six-wicket win, Baker’s one for 15 limited England’s target to a paltry 146, which Banton, a natural opener who is being recommissioned in the middle order, helped knock off with 47 balls remaining. “Tonight was a special performance, very clinical,” said Brook.

News.title: Interest rate increase ‘likely’, warns Bank of England
News.content:
Andrew Bailey has said that interest rates are likely to rise if the Middle East war rages on, warning inflation is now on course to hit 4pc.

The Bank of England opted to hold borrowing costs at 3.75pc on Thursday, the sixth time in a row it has left them unchanged.

However, the Governor said a “material” increase in energy prices since July would push up inflation to twice the Bank’s 2pc target.

He warned the outlook for inflation “continues to be on the upside” and criticised the “seeming loss of urgency to find solutions” to the war in Iran.

Oil prices are back above $100 a barrel and analysts expect average gas and electricity bills to rise above £2,000 this winter as the conflict continues.

Mr Bailey said: “So far, higher global energy costs have had a limited effect on price and wage setting in the UK.

“But the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2pc target.”

Investors expect the Bank to raise interest rates as soon as November, which has pushed average mortgage rates to their highest level in three years.

The average five-year fixed mortgage deal has risen to 5.87pc, according to Moneyfacts, which is the highest level since November 2023 and up from 4.95pc before the Iran war.

Thursday’s rate hold leaves the Bank out of step with central banks around the world after the US Federal Reserve and European Central Bank voted to raise borrowing costs this month.

However, economists said there had been a change in tone from policymakers over the threat posed by energy prices and whether this would feed into the wider economy.

The Bank of England predicted that inflation would hit 4pc early next year, just as most workers are negotiating pay rises.

Paul Dales, chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said: “It seems as though a majority of the MPC is on the cusp of wanting to tighten policy.”

In a warning on the impending pain facing households, Mr Bailey told the Chancellor that energy bills would rise by 24pc early next year under the Ofgem price cap.

This will push up annual average bills by £413 to £2,136, which the Governor blamed on the war in the Middle East.

The Governor is required to write a formal letter to the Chancellor every time inflation is more than a percentage point above its 2pc target.

Official data showed inflation rose to 3.1pc in August.

Mr Bailey said: “The energy price shock has been the most important factor driving recent short-term movements in inflation.”

Despite expectations of higher rates, the FTSE 100 rose on Thursday at its steepest pace since July, climbing more than 1pc, as the Bank of England eased the pressure on the UK bond market.

Policymakers also confirmed a Telegraph report that the Bank will stop selling the long-dated bonds it amassed during the financial crisis and lockdown.

The Bank will continue actively selling £20bn of government bonds per year until the rest of the stockpile is wound down to zero in 2034.

The announcement triggered a sharp fall in the cost of borrowing for the Treasury, with the yield on 30-year UK gilts falling at the fastest pace since May.

News.title: Next-generation antivenom fights India’s deadliest snakes
News.content:
The process to make antivenom has barely changed in a century: snakes are milked, their venom is injected into horses, and their antibodies are harvested to form the basis of the product. The resulting treatments are difficult to administer, can trigger severe side effects, and the quality varies from batch to batch.

“The big four snakes contribute to 70 per cent of poisonous bites [in India]… so 30 per cent of poisonous snakes are not covered, even to begin with,” said Dr Yogesh Jain, a public health physician in Chhattisgarh state and a member of The Global Snakebite Taskforce.

“But there are huge quality and efficacy issues even against these 70 per cent of bites. We’re relying on a 100-year-old technique of getting antivenoms, and at least 50,000 people are dying every year,” he told The Telegraph.

“There’s a real need for new technology. We don’t have a safe and appropriate antivenom for the largest majority of people in rural India.”

Now, scientists are hopeful that they have developed a potential alternative.

In the latest study, published last week, researchers showed that an experimental antivenom cocktail with five components protected mice against lethal doses of antivenom in Indian cobras, even when delayed by up to 20 minutes – a scenario that mimics the real-world lag between a bite and treatment.

“If you go 10 years back, people didn’t think you could make sufficiently simple products with new, modern biotechnology that could cover all these different snake venoms,” said Prof Andreas Laustsen-Kiel, head of the Section of Biologics Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark and co-author of the paper.

“People simply believed it was too complex, too expensive to manufacture, and so on… But the data we are gathering is convincing enough to say this is something that could make a huge dent in the lost lives and limbs snakebite causes every year.”

The antivenom itself was based on lab-made nanobodies – antibodies derived from a group of animals including camels, llamas and some species of shark. Scientists believe their structure means they could be a more potent, more precise, more temperature-stable alternative to man-made monoclonal antibodies – and cheaper to manufacture.

“The latest study builds on an earlier discovery of nanobodies that can protect across a broad spectrum of African snakes,” said Prof Nicholas Casewell, director of the Centre for Snakebite Research and Interventions at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, who has previously collaborated with Prof Laustsen-Kiel.

“In this paper they have iterated and demonstrated that a narrow number of nanobodies can protect against Indian cobras and king cobras. This demonstration brings the nanobody technology closer to market,” he added.

But that is likely still years away, depending on how much funding the researchers can attract. The next steps – a larger animal study, scaling up manufacture, and launching human trials – are expensive.

“If money was no issue, we could probably be testing in humans in 1.5 to three years from now,” said Prof Laustsen-Kiel. “But since money is a big issue, it is more likely that human trials won’t be able to start until 2.5 to four years from now.

“But I really think that this [study shows] there’s no doubt that biotech can deliver better antivenoms. The question is whether people are willing to fund it,” he said.

News.title: Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans
News.content:
The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears.



Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta buries hatchet with Fabian Hurzeler after managers clashed during fiery Brighton vs Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA has buried the hatchet with Fabian Hurzeler after their spat last season.

The two managers clashed after Arsenal beat Brighton 1-0 in March at the Amex on their way to winning the Premier League.



Hurzeler had a pop at the Gunners’ style of play and said afterwards that “only one team tried to play football” during the game.

But Arteta stressed all is forgiven now as the two sides prepare to meet again this weekend.



The Arsenal boss said: “That’s all done. That’s all in the past.

“I have huge respect for Fabian and what he has done, and what Brighton has done as a club. It’s just remarkable. Tomorrow is going to be a beautiful game to watch, I am sure.”

A trip to Brighton on Saturday means that Viktor Gyokeres could face his former club.

The striker, however, is likely to be on the bench as he is struggling for form and Kai Havertz has three goals in six games.

Arteta, however, is not worried by Gyokeres’ slow start and has backed him to good.

He said: “Especially in the Premier League, he hasn’t played that many minutes.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“But last week he played in Napoli, and he had a good game. I think that’s about moments as well.

“We need to give him all the support and confidence that he needs to deliver because we know the player that we have, the capacity that he has to score goals and what he can give to the team.

“The team is doing certain different things this season as well. It’s a bit of both, but it’s nothing unique for Viktor; it’s for everybody.

“That’s a constant evolution, player and team. And for sure our job, especially my job, is to try to fit that in and find those connections and that level of confidence for the player to give his best for the team.



“Especially for a striker, you know what, they need minutes and they need goals. That’s what really boosts their energy, and we have a game tomorrow and hopefully he can deliver that.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta hands Arsenal major injury boost with four stars all pushing to play vs Brighton after missing Ipswich game
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA says Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie are all pushing to play against Brighton this weekend.

The quartet are struggling for fitness and were not part of Arsenal’s squad for their 4-2 win at Ipswich in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.



Timber was left out as he is still building up his minutes after undergoing groin surgery in the summer.

Hincapie has a muscular issue, while White’s groin is troubling him and Mosquera has a hamstring injury.



But Arteta has hinted that the quartet could all feature when the Gunners travel to the Amex on Saturday.

The Arsenal boss said: “All good. We have another training session this afternoon, so very positive about everybody.

“We have another session, they are willing to be part of it and we have another session to try to make sure they are fit.”

Arsenal are taking on Brighton as they look to extend their perfect start to the new season.

The Premier League champions have won all seven of their matches in all competitions and stretching that run to eight would equal a club record set 123 years ago.

Arteta said on Friday morning: “We’ve got a really tough opponent tomorrow so we’re going to have to earn the right to win the game.



“But certainly that will be the mindset of the players and the team.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We know how complicated it is to win a football match at this level. So to win seven, it tells the story.

“After the World Cup, especially, there were a lot of unknowns about how the players and the team were going to react.

“We didn’t have any time with them to work together. But I said from day one, I think the attitude and what I was seeing, I was really impressed with.

“Then you have to put it down to performances. We had a bit of luck as well, for sure, to win four matches. And we are here. And then we want to make another one for sure tomorrow.”

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney lands major new BBC show as Man Utd legend warns A-list guests ‘I don’t like losing’
Sports.content:
Next

WAYNE ROONEY has landed a major new BBC show and he’s already warned his celebrity guests he hates losing.

The Manchester United and England legend will star in a new weekly show called Can You Beat Wayne Rooney?



Rooney will take on famous faces from sport, entertainment and popular culture in a battle of football knowledge.

The show will be hosted by comedian Alex Brooker and will launch this autumn.



Fans will be able to watch it on BBC Sport’s Football YouTube channel and BBC iPlayer, while it will also be available on BBC Sounds and major podcast platforms.

Each episode will see Rooney answer football questions against a different guest.



But the questions won’t just test his knowledge, they will also bring back stories from his incredible career.

That means fans can expect plenty of memories from his Manchester United days, England career, famous goals, team-mates and big matches.

And Rooney has admitted his competitive side will come out.

He said: “Anyone who knows me knows I’m competitive, whether it’s on a football pitch, playing paddle or on a golf course and even rowing on the Hudson River.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Every guest will turn up thinking they can beat me and, honestly, I don’t like losing.

“A single question can take you straight back to a dressing room, a match or a moment you haven’t thought about in years.

“We’ve got some great guests lined up, plenty of laughs and some fantastic football conversations.”

Brooker said: “Wayne is an absolute winner, he hates losing. I can’t wait to see every guest arrive trying to take him down and Wayne determined not to let it happen.



“Add in the incredible stories that come from the questions and you’ve got something football fans are going to love. It’s going to be a lot of fun.”

The new series will be produced in Manchester by Persephonica, the company behind Games Gone and The Steve Bracknall Podcast.

It comes after Rooney answered Erling Haaland‘s challenge to fulfil his World Cup rowing pledge and take to New York’s Hudson River following Norway‘s dramatic victory over Brazil.

Now Rooney has another challenge on his hands, and he’ll be desperate to make sure none of his guests get the better of him.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel recalls Cole Palmer and Alexander-Arnold as NINE players from World Cup miss out including Arsenal ace

COLE PALMER and Trent Alexander-Arnold have returned to the England set-up as Thomas Tuchel named his first squad since their World Cup heartache.

The Chelsea and Real Madrid stars both missed out on the tournament in the USA, Mexico and Canada.



Palmer was snubbed after a mixed season with Chelsea in 2025-26.

But he has gained the backing of Tuchel after a strong start to the current campaign under Xabi Alonso.





Palmer has four goals and two assists in all competitions and will have a chance to impress alongside Chelsea team-mate and pal Morgan Rogers.

Alexander-Arnold was also a surprise omission from the World Cup squad despite lacking options at right-back.

This season he has three starts under Jose Mourinho at Madrid. He has played a total of 310 minutes and has registered one assist so far.

Both will go straight into a new-look group preparing for Nations League games against Spain, Croatia and Czechia.



Liverpool starlet Rio Ngumoha, 18, and Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, 23, have also been selected after helping England with their World Cup preparations.

Ngumoha has already made three appearances for the Reds under boss Andoni Iraola and has looked lively.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And Scott has started all five of Bournemouth’s games so far, scoring once and also assisting in their 2-1 Europa League win over Real Sociedad.



Other new faces in the squad are Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, Newcastle’s Lewis Hall, Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly.

A handful of Tuchel’s World Cup stars weren’t available for this international break, including John Stones, who picked up an thigh injury for Inter Milan.

And his club team-mate Djed Spence also wasn’t picked as he is yet to play a game for Inter so far due to fitness issues.

The same is true for Newcastle centre-back Dan Burn, while Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins – who both play in the Saudi Pro League – are out.

Goalkeeper Dean Henderson wasn’t available for selection either after suffering an ankle blow.



Replacing him is Brighton shot-stopper Jason Steele.

Reece James was missing from the squad announcement too in a surprise call.

There is also no place for Jordan Henderson – now at Chelsea – after he was controversially named in the World Cup squad.



Manchester United star Kobbie Mainoo keeps his place in the team, as does Arsenal’s Eberechi Eze despite only playing 68 minutes in the Premier League so far.

But Eze’s club team-mate Noni Madueke does miss out after also failing to start a game for the Gunners in the Prem this season.

Harry Maguire continues to be snubbed by Tuchel after claiming he was “shocked and gutted” to miss the World Cup – and there is no Phil Foden either.



Tuchel explained his picks on Friday morning as he said he was “happy” to have Alexander-Arnold back with him.

He added: “It’s an opportunity for Trent. He had a good start to the season.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI usually loves seeing his team-mates take bold and adventurous risks.

The camera then panned to a sheepish Kai Havertz, caught putting the bottle of Heinz down on the table before mixing the red sauce in.

Sports.title: Doyle: Arapaho can strike gold in Newbury's Mill Reef Stakes
Sports.content:
Our ambassador Hollie Doyle previews a busy Saturday which features the Group Two Mill Reef Stakes at Newbury – live on Sky Sports Racing.

Dods gelding to strike gold in Mill Reef

Michael Dods has been bullish about his unbeaten gelding Arapaho Gold, who can make it five wins out of five in the Dubai Duty Free Mill Reef Stakes (2.12) at Newbury on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Racing.

The impressive Gimcrack winner - according to the Darlington trainer the best juvenile he's ever had - boasts by far the best form in the race and proved his liking for this course and distance when he won the Listed Rose Bowl earlier in the season.

Image: Arapaho Gold, ridden by Connor Beasley, on the way to winning the Al Basti Equiworld Dubai Gimcrack at York

Godolphin's Nabati looked most progressive until coming unstuck in the Listed Flying Scotsman Stakes at Doncaster only last week. Charlie Appleby is backing him up quickly with something to prove at this level.

Starlust to capitalise on drop in grade

I'm keeping a close eye on the revitalised Breeders' Cup winner Starlust in the Dubai International Airport World Trophy Stakes (1.02) at Newbury.

Ralph Beckett's sprinter, who stole the glory in Del Mar two years ago before an unsuccessful stint at stud, has run two big figures at the top level in the Nunthorpe and the Flying Five in Ireland last weekend so poses a threat to all in this lower grade.

Back on an easier track, he can get his head back in front at the possible expense of Shagraan, who can outrun his odds in the first-time cheekpieces. Clive Cox's gelding was second in this race last year and will enjoy the underfoot conditions.

Legend can bounce back to winning form

Roaring Legend proved he retains plenty of ability when going down narrowly to last weekend's Mallard winner Valedictory at Newmarket in the summer and can go one better in the Dubai Duty Free Autumn Cup Handicap (1.37) at Newbury.

Olly Murphy's eight-year-old is a fresh horse - a comment that applies to Alan King's Insanity. I've always liked this gelding who is well handicapped on the pick of his more recent form.

Primo Lara has Ryan Moore up which will attract plenty of market interest but this looks much tougher than the all-weather race he won at Kempton earlier this month.

Newbury a hot date for Boyfriend

Richard Hannon holds the key to the Dubai Duty Free Handicap (2.47) at Newbury with the consistent Boyfriend and stable companion Stem.

The former was quite unlucky at Salisbury when things got quite congested but he stayed on well and might have gone closer with a clear run. Compensation way well await.

Stem produced a good run at Sandown last time and has won at Newbury before, while Jane Chapple-Hyam's Balzac posted a much-improved run at Ascot after being gelded and looks another big player.

Haggas grey has strong Gold Cup chance

Binhareer is a stakes horse in the making so I'm expecting big things from him in the Ladbrokes Ayr Gold Cup (3.40) at Ayr on Saturday.

William Haggas' grey ran a super race in the Group Three Hackwood Stakes at Newbury in July off an unchanged rating of 103 and my husband Tom Marquand is looking forward to getting back on him in handicap company.

A course and distance winner in easy ground last year, he's on top of my shortlist along with Far Above Dream who went agonisingly close in a hot handicap at York last time. That form was franked when the third Coul Angel bolted up at the Curragh last week.

At a bigger price, I wouldn't rule out Richard Spencer's Run Boy Run, who won the race 12 months ago off a lower rating and could be dangerous in first-time blinkers if he's drawn on the right side in stall 23.

Hats off to Sam in Silver Cup

I'd love to see Sam England win the Ladbrokes Ayr Silver Cup Handicap (2.30) with the in-form Trilby who is another strong chance for Tom (Marquand).

He won well at Beverley before staying on nicely at Haydock, hitting the line really hard, and the quicker they go the better for the six-year-old who is on a nice mark despite his five-pound penalty.

Wathnan Racing's Deep Havana also shoulders a penalty but won well at Thirsk off a long lay-off and can improve on that, while Julie Camacho's Havana Blue should play a leading role after winning so impressively at Ascot.

Getting back on simulator my biggest milestone

I'm delighted to report that in the past two weeks I've really turned the corner in my recovery from the broken leg I sustained at Bath in May.

For a while I wasn't seeing the progress I was hoping for which was quite worrying - my knee and ankle just weren't working together - but I'm starting to see good results now which is very satisfying.

The biggest milestone was getting back on the simulator a few weeks ago. Initially I couldn't even get my foot up in the iron but it feels good to be taking such a big step back towards riding again.

Even from the outset I was determined not to let myself lose too much condition, hoping that I would be able to regain fitness faster once I started to increase my rehab, which has been quite exhausting.

I've been doing an hour in the gym every day at Oaksey House in Lambourn, followed by physio sessions and work in the hydro pool. I've also been back on the exercise bike which has been great for boosting my cardio.

I'm definitely ticking every box and seeing the results of my hard work so I'm hoping to be back doing what I love in a matter of weeks, rather than months.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

Sports.title: Will Carrick navigate choppy waters to steer Man Utd ship back on course?
Sports.content:
Manchester United's Carabao Cup second-round loss at Grimsby last season was a result that many will remember.

It was a defeat which became synonymous with former Manchester United head coach Ruben Amorim's time in charge.

That was a very bad night for United, and although Wednesday's defeat at home to Brighton did not feel as significant, there were similarities for the man who succeeded Amorim, Michael Carrick.

Fulham

Manchester United Sunday 20th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Man Utd's captain for the loss, Youri Tielemans, admitted afterwards that once they went 2-0 down, his side stopped playing - and that was pretty evident by their performance.

You could sense at Old Trafford from 20 minutes onwards that Brighton were in the ascendancy and the game was only going to go one way. Despite bringing on Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, United failed to make an impression.

That is what will truly worry head coach Carrick.

After the few defeats Carrick has suffered since his return to the club in January, he has always backed his players or found positive qualities in the performances, but there was no such redemption to be found against Brighton.

Predictable problems and defensive worries

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton

When Carrick and his staff first came in, they deservedly received a lot of praise.

Defensively they looked tight and compact and that led to impressive wins against Manchester City and Arsenal.

The likes of Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate and Jonny Evans made an immediate improvement to the defensive unit.

But, equally, questions have to be raised now about the frailties that same defence is showing this season. Carrick's side have conceded two goals in three of their four Premier League games.

The defence was exposed once again in the Brighton loss. Yes, one goal was a goalkeeping error by Karl Darlow, but aside from the goals conceded, the shape and understanding of the back four lacked any sort of coherence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Dave Reed analyses Man Utd's running stats

Left-back predictably is an issue for Carrick. He has yet to acknowledge the area as a specific weakness as per his style when engaging in the media, but it is a significant problem - one the United hierarchy knew about going into the summer's transfer window.

Luke Shaw, United's only senior left-back at the club, has missed the last three games through a minor injury, but considering his age and injury track record - despite his excellent availability last season - it was naive not to strengthen in that area.

Carrick has experimented with Noussair Mazraoui in that position but he seems to have fallen down the pecking order, as the less experienced Patrick Dorgu was preferred for the Manchester derby loss.

Young left-back Harry Amass does not seem to be fancied in the position long-term either - so how will United remedy the position for the rest of the season?

An awkward discussion over Carrick's future

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carrick responds to the Old Trafford boos after Manchester United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton

It seems ridiculous to even discuss Carrick's job security after only a few weeks of the new season.

Man Utd have still accumulated the most points across the league since his return in January.

However, as Carrick admitted himself, a few moments such as Ainsley Maitland-Niles' equaliser for Everton, City's controversial VAR goal and now a shocking collapse against Brighton, have made it all feel very different.

If United lose at Fulham on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, there will be inevitable and uncomfortable discussions around whether Carrick can lead United out of the storm they currently find themselves in.

That may be for another day, but the United head coach does deserve sympathy for the squad he has been dealt.

The lack of sales and outgoings this summer at United handicapped them in being able to further reinforce the squad. But does that excuse them ignoring key areas to strengthen?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp rips into Manchester United for the way they defended in their 3-2 loss to Brighton in the Carabao Cup third round

The left-back area, as mentioned, should have been strengthened. Knowing Benjamin Sesko was still nursing a shin injury all summer, perhaps United should have brought in a temporary No 9 to share the load rather than playing Mbeumo and Cunha out of position. Both players have failed to discover the form they showed under Carrick last season.

But, ultimately, until United are able to be in a position where they can really reshape their team in one window, they will continue to be caught in this cycle of strengthening just enough with players left over from previous regimes.

That perhaps is why you could hear boos at Old Trafford after the Brighton loss. Not just aimed at that performance, but perhaps a familiar feeling of a cycle beginning again, a deja vu of seasons past and another false dawn after a promising start under a new United head coach.

Again, it feels too soon for that just yet, and Carrick deserves time after what he delivered last season, but these are the waters he has to navigate, and ultimately, he will be the one judged.

But if he can stop the spiral, even without a win against Fulham with a positive performance, time may allow him to be able to steer the ship back on course.

Sports.title: Merson: 'Huge game' between Spurs and Aston Villa is a 'momentum swinger'
Sports.content:
In his latest Sky Sports column, Paul Merson looks ahead to Saturday's "huge" game between Tottenham and Aston Villa.

Both teams are winless in the Premier League, with Spurs looking for their first league goal of the season.

Read below for the Magic Man's thoughts on the "momentum swinger" game at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, as he also assesses Arsenal's chances of defending their Premier League title.

Mindset and confidence are Spurs' key problems

"The first 15, 20 minutes I thought they [Spurs] were outstanding [vs Everton].

"I thought the way they passed it, moved it, it caused problems for Everton. But they didn't get that goal. And when they don't get that goal, then that mindset sets in again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League clash between Tottenham and Everton

"I think they'd still be playing now [without scoring], wouldn't they? That is the problem. They need to score early. And confidence is the thing as well.

"I say any footballer, I don't care if you're under-10s or professional, if you can bottle one thing, it's confidence.

"And at the moment, they just haven't got that confidence and the belief. And that's the problem, that belief."

Are Villa genuine relegation contenders?

"No. I think they [Villa] have too many good players, if I'm being honest. I think it was a terrible result against Nottingham Forest. It was worrying.

"They were dominating but couldn't score a goal. But I'd be shocked if they got relegated.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Aston Villa's match against Nottingham Forest in the Premier League

"They've got too many good players, and they've got one of the best managers in the business. They're just having a little bit of a time at the moment.

"I do think this is a big game this weekend [vs Tottenham], though. It's a huge game. Down at the bottom, if you're down there, you're down there.

"I don't worry about Tottenham or Villa, but I think it's a big game for both teams because it's a momentum swinger.

"You win it, then you can kick on after the international break. It's a big football match."

Arsenal will defend title comfortably

"I think they [Arsenal] will win the Premier League by double digits. I think they'll win it easy.

"I look at Arsenal's fixtures: Man City away, Man Utd away, Chelsea away, Liverpool away. After those four games, I don't know who's beating Arsenal.

"They're just a hard, hard team to beat. I don't see them losing a lot of football matches this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League clash between Sunderland and Arsenal

"The shackles are off a bit. No one can call Arsenal bottle jobs any more. So the pressure is off.

"And they just play with that feeling like they've had an email through and told them, 'you know what the score is going to be already'.

"I just watched them against Villa, and you watch them against Sunderland, and there's no panic.

"They play; it's patient. They will score in the end and the opposition won't. That is the way they are at the moment."

Sports.title: Nasser: Pietersen could be key for 'second coming' of Banton
Sports.content:
Nasser Hussain has lauded the "second coming" of England batter Tom Banton and says the appointment of new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen could be key to his development in the middle order.

Banton top-scored for England with an unbeaten 52 off 24 balls in an impressive innings, combining well with skipper Harry Brook (23 off 8) after Jos Buttler (30 off 16) had become the first player to make 15,000 T20 runs - as the home side sauntered past Sri Lanka's modest 145-9 with 7.5 overs to spare.

The half-century was Banton's third since re-entering the white-ball set-up as a middle-order batter, having played as an opener in his early career - a transition Hussain lauded on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The pick of the action from Cardiff as England dashed to a target of 146 against Sri Lanka to wrap up a T20 series win with a game to spare

"Banton has been really good in his second coming [after moving from opener to the middle order]," said Hussain.

"Everyone talks about what [white-ball mentor] Kevin Pietersen can do for Harry Brook, but I think Pietersen could be good for Banton.

"KP raved about Banton when he came through at Somerset but then he fell away and KP made a couple of comments saying he had to work hard.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jos Buttler makes history in the T20 format by passing the 15,000 career runs milestone - the first to do so

"He has worked hard and we are now seeing the rewards of that. KP will now be saying, 'keep improving'. That's what great players do."

Sky Sports Cricket's Kumar Sangakkara also praised Banton's development, adding: "He was just exceptional. Anything that was pitched full, he cleared his front leg. Anything that was on the stumps, straight down the ground.

"Even with pace, he's got that power and that timing to really make a difference. I think he was exceptional. His development, especially against spin, has been brilliant for England."

Hussain: Dawson changed course of match

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Two in two for Liam Dawson following Jamie Overton's superb catch for the first, Kamil Mishara then chips the first ball he faces straight back to the bowler

Hussain was also complimentary of Liam Dawson's performance after the spinner took 3-32 in Sri Lanka's innings, including a crucial two wickets in two balls when the tourists' openers were going well - an impact that Hussain felt changed the course of the match.

"England just outplayed Sri Lanka in every department," Hussain added. "At 55-0 after five [overs], you thought Sri Lanka are actually going to put on a showing here and maybe test England.

"But it was Liam Dawson with two in an over [that changed the course of the match] - and on a ground where sometimes bowling spin isn't easy and sides often leave out their spinner.

"He's a very smart cricketer. He's a very tough cricketer and he's been around a long time. And he'll know what sort of lengths and lines to bowl on this particular ground. So that was brilliant from Dawson."

'Sri Lanka way off it'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara analyse what has gone wrong for Sri Lanka

The defeat was Sri Lanka's 14th in succession against England in T20 internationals - a record which was indicative to Hussain of a larger malaise in comparison to past sides.

"Sri Lanka are just way off the side that I've seen over the years - just way off," he said.

"It's a massive drop off in the batting in particular. I've watched some of their greats and they're just strokers of the ball. They stroke the ball for six, for four - but what I see at the moment is people trying to over hit.

"On good pitches, last game, this game, the moment there was a bit of pace, they're losing their shape.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jofra Archer flattens the middle stump to help wrap up Sri Lanka's innings

"In every metric today, England completely outplayed them. There were 50 dot balls. Ten sixes England scored, [and Sri Lanka scored] two sixes, even with these straight boundaries.

"A coach or a director of cricket or whoever will look at and sit back and go, that wasn't good enough - and when you're playing against England, those metrics have to be closer together.

"They are miles apart."

Sports.title: Allen stars as Bills open new stadium with win over Lions
Sports.content:
Josh Allen quickly put his stamp on the Buffalo Bills' new Highmark Stadium as he threw three touchdown passes and ran for two scores as the Bills beat the Detroit Lions 41-31 on Thursday night.

It was Allen's fourth career five-TD outing, and followed a four-touchdown outing (two passing, two rushing) in Buffalo's 36-31 season-opening win at Houston.

The $2.1bn stadium that officially opened last month was built across the street from the Bills' former home.

Allen followed the pre-game fireworks celebration with more fireworks of his own by overseeing touchdown drives on each of Buffalo's first four possessions.

He scored the first regular-season TD in the stadium on a 1-yard run 5:51 into the opening quarter. He followed that with a 43-yard scoring pass to a wide-open Josh Palmer. Tight ends Dalton Kincaid, with a 16-yard catch, and Dawson Knox, with a 1-yarder, also scored for Buffalo in the first half.

Allen finished 20 of 31 for 248 yards, and added 72 yards rushing. James Cook had 134 yards rushing and put the game away with a 1-yard TD run with 2:50 left.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen's best plays from his five touchdown game against the Detroit Lions in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season

Allen's two rushing TDs upped his career total to 83, moving him into a tie for 18th on the NFL list with Jim Taylor. He also picked up his 90th regular-season victory, in becoming one of just four quarterbacks to reach that milestone through their first nine seasons.

The Lions were undone by an injury depleted defense, and a banged-up offensive line that had difficulty opening holes for Jahmyr Gibbs and protecting Jared Goff.

After rallying from a 21-0 deficit to cut Buffalo's lead to 34-24, the Lions offense stalled midway through the fourth quarter. Backed up at their own 10, the Lions went three-and-out and forced to punt after Goff had two passes tipped by Deone Walker, and Gibbs was stopped for no gain.

Goff finished 26 of 38 for 327 yards and four touchdowns, with Amon-Ra St. Brown having nine catches for 142 yards and two scores. Gibbs also scored on an 11-yard catch but was limited to 52 yards rushing. Sam LaPorta also scored on a 1-yard catch.

St. Brown and Gibbs have now scored in the same game 22 times to move into a tie for fourth place in matching the Cleveland receiver/running back combo of Paul Warfield and Leroy Kelly.

The Lions' defense got off to a dreadful start in allowing Bills to score 27 points and gain 299 yards in the first half alone.

Sports.title: Fiercest rivalry in football? Millwall and West Ham face off after 14-year wait
Sports.content:
One of football's fiercest rivalries is back.

The infamous 'Dockers derby' has over 125 years of history but the 100th match-up between Millwall and West Ham on Saturday lunchtime is one of the most hotly anticipated.

They say absence makes the heart grow fonder but after a 14-year wait since these two London clubs last faced off, expect that gap to only ramp up the atmosphere and intensity before and after the first whistle blows at 12.30pm at the Den, live on Sky Sports.

Last season ended in disappointment for both sides, with West Ham relegated from the Premier League and Millwall beaten in the Championship play-offs. But a consolation for both sets of supporters was the prospect of this first showdown since February 2012.

West Ham won that day at Upton Park and the visitors will be favourites to take the three points again when they visit their injury-hit hosts.

Nuno Espirito Santo's group may have been beaten by Premier League Fulham in the Carabao Cup in midweek but, with six changes made to the starting XI for that tie, that result is not a great guide for what to expect from the Hammers on Saturday.

Instead, look to their stunning run in the Championship over their past four league games. They've scored 16 times across that winning streak, with captain Jarrod Bowen looking a class apart at this level, with four goals and two assists in the run.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hal Robson-Kanu and Bristol Rovers' boss Steve Evans discuss whether anyone can stop West Ham this season after The Hammers' impressive start to the Championship.

If table-topping West Ham are turning on the style, Millwall are scrapping, with double-figures in the treatment room.

A 2-2 draw at Middlesbrough was ultimately a positive point on Tuesday - but the concession of a two-goal lead was perhaps a reflection of a team suffering fatigue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Millwall.

The Lions battled to the final whistle to hold on for a draw but the physical demands of covering for their absent team-mates has taken a toll on the players who have been repeatedly asked to go again.

There was similar spirit shown against Newcastle last week in the 1-0 Carabao Cup loss but keeping teams at bay in the Championship has been an issue in recent weeks with Millwall shipping 13 goals across their past five league games, with the solitary clean sheet against Bolton the exception.

The free-scoring Hammers will be optimistic of opening up that defence again.

Millwall with the rivalry edge overall Millwall have won 38 games to West Ham’s 34, with 27 draws in their past 99 meetings.

But this game is the epitome of a 'formbook-out-of-the-window' fixture.

Millwall hold a narrow winning record across the 99 previous clashes and home advantage could also be significant. Millwall fans will hold memories of the 4-1 thrashing of West Ham in March 2004 when they head to the Den on Saturday. You have to go back to December 1988 for West Ham's last win at Millwall.

But expect the unexpected. Red cards in three of the past six meetings highlights how the atmospheres generated by these two fan groups can translate onto the pitch and bring unpredictability to these occasions.

It all adds to the anticipation, with the 100th chapter of the story of this famous fixture ready to be written.
