Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Bees sense chance to sting Blues’ backline

Chelsea have not won this west London derby since Brentford’s first Premier League season. Each visit since October 2021’s 1-0 win, Ben Chilwell the scorer, has been a draw. This season has continued the divergence between the clubs’ respective approaches, Brentford’s solidity and continuity contrasting with Chelsea attempting their latest reboot. Kevin Schade, after two well-taken goals at Bournemouth, will fancy facing a defence not yet attuned to Xabi Alonso’s configurations. Only one team has won a Premier League title with a defensive trio: Chelsea’s last title team, in 2016-17 under Antonio Conte. Alonso’s attack has been rather more successful, presenting another challenge for Jannik Schuster. Replacing Nathan Collins, the 20-year-old central defender had a tough examination from Bournemouth’s Evanilson on his first Premier League start, emerging with credit. For Chelsea, João Pedro has three goals and three assists, but doubts surrounding his fitness could lead to Danny Welbeck’s first league start. John Brewin

Brentford v Chelsea, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Spurs and Villa meet in desperation derby

What happens when a very stoppable force meets an extremely movable object? We will be tuning into events at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday to find out as 19th-placed Aston Villa arrive in north London. The teams have scored one goal between them in the league and are desperately hoping for a first Premier League win. The return of Pedro Porro is big for Roberto De Zerbi and that should bring the Archie Gray Experiment at right-back to a merciful end. No Premier League starting XI feels less settled than Spurs – most players look as if they are a mistake or two from being dropped – which has culminated in a side that seems governed by fear and continuously prefers to take the safe option. After coming off the bench against Everton and Liverpool in the past week, the injury-plagued James Maddison will be itching to start and take some sort of initiative for Tottenham. Michael Butler

Tottenham v Aston Villa, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Mateus Fernandes will hope Spurs can get their first league win of the season against Aston Villa. Photograph: Alex Morton/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

3 Hürzeler’s scoring express meets champions

When Fabian Hürzeler spoke about Brighton’s success being founded on them being “well structured” after their stirring comeback against Manchester United at Old Trafford on Wednesday, he could have been referring to Malick Yalcouyé. The 20-year-old Ivorian moved to the south coast in 2024 after spending just a few months with IFK Gothenburg in Sweden but had to wait until this season to make his senior debut for Brighton after being sent on loan to Sturm Graz in Austria and then Swansea last season. With Jack Hinshelwood sidelined by injury until after the international break, Yalcouyé has taken his chance in the No 10 role and already found the net twice in the Premier League as Brighton have made a brilliant start. Arsenal are up next for the division’s top scorers – who have 13 goals from their opening four matches – and Mikel Arteta should be wary of the threat posed by Yalcouyé and co as the champions prepare for a fourth away game in succession. Ed Aarons

Brighton v Arsenal, Saturday 3pm

4 Mykolenko form a boost for Moyes

Vitalii Mykolenko’s early-season improvement has gone largely unheralded – and it probably always will be among his detractors – but at a time when David Moyes needs experienced players to step up and defy the constraints of a small squad, the Everton left-back has produced. Having signed a new three-year contract in the summer, and seemingly bulked up, the Ukraine international has kept his critics quiet with several impressive displays for a defence that has four clean sheets in six matches. There remains a problematic lack of cover at left-back after the decision to loan Adam Aznou to Málaga for the season but Mykolenko, the better defender, has eased the concerns that surrounded his position before the new campaign. Ipswich’s new forward recruits, Emersonn and Zian Flemming, will test Everton’s solidity but Moyes’s side will have made an encouraging start should they sign off with a win before the extended international break. Andy Hunter

Everton v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

5 Jaissle refuses to delete Newcastle blueprint

As befits a lover of direct football, Matthias Jaissle likes to get straight to the point. On Thursday he was asked whether, in the light of Monday night’s 4-1 thrashing at Leeds and a raft of injuries, he was tempted to perhaps switch to a back five or modify his beloved “vertical” approach when Hull visit Tyneside on Saturday. The reply proved unequivocal. “No,” said a manager unafraid to answer questions with a single word. Instead Jaissle expects his young team to retain faith in a wider vision as Newcastle – who signed eight players aged 24 and under this summer – adapt to life after Bruno Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon. “It’s a brave journey the club is going on and I’m fully committed in that,” the German said. “If there’s one setback, we shouldn’t delete our journey or our vision. We’re fully committed. We’re fully aligned. We anticipated that something like that against Leeds would happen. It’s on us to respond. But while still believing. We don’t change.” Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Hull, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen ‘We’re fully aligned,’ says Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

6 Delap hopes to impress as Wood regent

Many scoffed at the £45m that was paid for Liam Delap in the summer but Nottingham Forest feels like the perfect place for the striker to regain his form. Forest previously thrived with the now injured Chris Wood as their arrowhead and Delap is something of a younger regent for the New Zealander – powerful, instinctive and willing to bring others into play. During Saturday’s win at Villa, Morgan Gibbs-White and Delap looked as if they already have an understanding and both will be keen to capitalise against a Coventry side that have conceded eight goals in the past two games. After a nervy campaign last season, Forest feel back in the ascendancy and will have been delighted that plans to increase the City Ground’s capacity from 31,000 to 52,500, at an estimated cost of £790m, were approved by the local council on Wednesday. MB

Nottingham Forest v Coventry, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Iraola faces test on south-coast return

After watching Bournemouth make their European bow from afar in San Sebastián, a city Andoni Iraola knows inside out, the Basque head coach will return to his previous club on Sunday. Iraola – whose assistants Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper played for Bournemouth, the former captaining the club into the Premier League in 2015 – led the Dorset club into the Europa League by recording their best-ever finish, sixth. His body of work on the south coast earned him the Liverpool opportunity and a warm welcome is a guarantee. Despite the Cherries’ slow start under Iraola’s successor, Marco Rose, they will pose tricky opposition. The German spent a couple of hours in Iraola’s company before officially starting in June and both will be braced for an all-action contest. Eddie Howe failed to beat Bournemouth in the eight league games he managed against them with Newcastle and Iraola and his staff will expect a tough test. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Liverpool, Sunday 2pm

8 Calvert-Lewin: man on a mission

Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be a man on a mission against Crystal Palace at Elland Road on Saturday. Daniel Farke’s centre-forward hopes to become the first Leeds player to score in six consecutive home league games since Arthur Hydes back in 1932. Managers often, quite rightly, say players matter more than formations but, in Calvert-Lewin’s case, Farke’s switch to 3-5-2 late last November proved a road to Damascus moment. Until then he had struggled as the team’s lone striker but, once he was paired with Noah Okafor or Lukas Nmecha, the goals started to flow. Granted, Leeds sometimes play 3-4-3 or, occasionally, revert to a back four but Calvert-Lewin has emphasised the importance of attacking partnerships. After collecting eight points from their opening four games, Farke’s team have registered the best beginning to a top-tier campaign of any Leeds team since David O’Leary’s class of 2001-02. Will it continue at Palace’s expense? Is Hydes’ record under threat? Might 3-5-2 be the answer to ending more strikers’ goal droughts? Louise Taylor

Leeds v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm

9 Le Bris plots party crash in Manchester

Manchester City’s maximum 12 points from their first four Premier League games featured 1-0 wins (over Coventry and Manchester United), a 2-1 victory (Bournemouth), and a 4-1 success (Crystal Palace). Conceding only two goals while scoring eight is an impressive record that is only marginally bettered by the champions, Arsenal (one conceded, eight scored in their 12-point tally), and it seems a rosy augury that Enzo Maresca’s team will be genuine title contenders this season. Régis Le Bris, though, plots to halt City’s perfect start, and can draw on guiding Sunderland to a share of the points last season against the FA Cup holders, though that was at the Stadium of Light. In the corresponding fixture at the Etihad Stadium, City cruised to a 3-0 win. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Sunderland, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Enzo Le Fée reacts after scoring against AZ on Sunderland’s midweek European return. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Bobb needs to provide more end product

Oscar Bobb came off the bench against West Ham and fired Fulham into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup with a clinical late winner at the London Stadium on Tuesday night. It was a fine piece of individual play from the Norway winger but he needs to do it more often. The goal was Bobb’s first since joining Fulham last January and a player of his ability should be producing more of an end product. The 23-year-old is a clever dribbler and looked ready to establish himself at Manchester City before a serious injury curtailed his development. The talent is clear. Bobb had a good World Cup and should be full of confidence when Fulham, still seeking their first win in the league this season, host Manchester United. Jacob Steinberg

Sports.title: Todd Boehly exits Chelsea diminished after having his fingers burned
Sports.content:
Not since a doomed foray into the thorny world of the transfer market has Todd Boehly had any real influence over the day-to-day at Chelsea. The American exits football as a diminished figure four years on, along with his fellow investor Mark Walter, and the first thing to say is that little will change in the Stamford Bridge boardroom just because Boehly has left the scene.

Clearlake Capital, the US private equity firm founded by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, was already the majority owner and guiding force. The trio of Boehly, Walter and the Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss had an equal share of a 38.5% stake but have drifted into irrelevance since the BlueCo consortium bought Chelsea from Roman Abramovich for £2.5bn in 2022.

Clearlake, with Eghbali taking a prominent role, called the shots long before Wednesday night’s confirmation that it has full control after buying out Boehly and Walter.

This split has been in the works for a while. It is two years since cracks within the ownership group spilled into public. There was talk of Boehly losing faith in his working relationship with Clearlake. Boehly wanted a resolution. People close to Boehly said he had investors ready to provide capital for a full takeover, although that drew eye-rolling from Clearlake.

Its response was to consider buying Boehly out. Another suggestion from Clearlake was for Boehly to step down as chair and accept changes to governance that would leave the billionaire in little more than a ceremonial role.

No love lost there, then, although there was no immediate sign of movement from either side. A truce followed and Clearlake continued down its path. Eghbali is hugely influential. It is only over the past year that Chelsea fans unhappy with the club’s difficulties in the post-Abramovich era have really started to home in on Clearlake.

Feliciano, who recently became an investor in the Major League Baseball team the San Diego Padres, operates more in the background. Eghbali is more widely seen and was repeatedly targeted with abusive chants by supporters earlier this year.

There was a time when Boehly was the public face of the takeover. Clearlake stood back and watched when Boehly appointed himself interim sporting director after key personnel left in the wake of Abramovich’s departure. How hard could it be? Pretty hard actually. Boehly attracted publicity and was in the limelight. Agents found him personable but wondered whether he knew anything about football.

There was a sense that Boehly’s naivety could be exploited. Chelsea ended up splurging some £300m on a bunch of misfits. The signing of Raheem Sterling on a £325,000-a-week contract became a cautionary tale. Chelsea did not easily shake off the cost of such failures and the sense of chaos grew when Thomas Tuchel was sacked and replaced by Graham Potter at the start of the 2022-23 season.

Boehly has since explained he signed Marc Cucurella from Brighton because he heard that Manchester City wanted the Spain left-back. There is presumably more to thriving as a sporting director than copying your rival’s work.

Boehly had his fingers burned. He became a joke figure, the face of Chelsea’s excess, and made himself unpopular on a wider scale by glibly wondering at a business conference why the Premier League had no All-Star game. Saying Chelsea would beat Real Madrid 3-0 before a Champions League quarter-final in 2023 predictably backfired.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea have only qualified for the Champions League once under Todd Boehly’s tenure. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

It is said that Boehly’s plan was never to become so involved and he always planned to step aside once experts were in place. Chelsea’s strategy has certainly changed since that first window. They have gone from having one interim sporting director to appointing five permanent ones in Paul Winstanley, Laurence Stewart, Sam Jewell, Joe Shields and Dave Fallows. They have handed out long, incentivised contracts and targeted young players.

Eghbali has driven the vision. It has been a bumpy ride at times. Chelsea have qualified for the Champions League once under this ownership. Managers have come and gone. Clearlake sources say important lessons have been absorbed this year. Last summer’s business was better. Chelsea brought in a serious manager, Xabi Alonso, and signed established talent.

Boehly has stood back and watched. Talk of buyouts went quiet until the summer just gone. The spark, it is said, was Walter seeking to liquidate assets to deal with financial issues in the US. The writing was on the wall when he sold his LA Lakers stake.

Boehly and Walter are said to have made a modest profit on their investment in Chelsea. Jonathan Goldstein, a Boehly ally, has also left the board. Wyss has invested in a Clearlake vehicle and has not left the building.

Little will change. Day-to-day operations, leadership and strategy remain the same. The big issue is the stadium question. The exit of Boehly and Walter could lead to movement.

The Guardian first reported in September 2024 that Chelsea were in talks over leaving Stamford Bridge for Earls Court. The Earls Court Development Committee’s separate proposal for the site has not progressed since receiving planning permission. Chelsea’s interest remains, although they have not ruled out finding a way to make the more complicated plan of redeveloping Stamford Bridge work.

Whatever happens will take place without Boehly. Eghbali and Feliciano said in their statement that Boehly “will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family”.

That was a generous take.

Sports.title: Kluivert and Rayan rock Real Sociedad as Bournemouth win on European bow
Sports.content:
The first goal that AFC Bournemouth ever scored in Europe could be heard out on the Bay of Biscay. A tradition from Real Sociedad’s old Atotxa ground, once lost but now recovered at Anoeta, dictates that a single flare is set off every time the visitors score while two are lit when the home team do; that way those out to sea know the score. And so it was that at 21.41 on a Thursday night in September 2026, Justin Kluivert found the net and a man named Juan Iturralde ran out into the street to let everyone know what had happened.

Back in Dorset and high in Anoeta, where 2,000 Bournemouth fans sang their way through this most special of occasions, they knew. They had waited their whole lives for this and it was a nice way to mark the history they made, their arrival announced to Europe with fireworks and a 2-1 victory in San Sebastián, the city where it all began for Andoni Iraola, the manager who brought them here.

Iturralde ran into the night three times – he went once more when Rayan made it 2-0 after 20 minutes and again when Sergio Gómez made it 2-1 on 57 – and might have gone more too. After a superb first half, Bournemouth had to hang on, sometimes desperately, in the second. For a while it had seemed a lead would slip away from their grasp for the fifth time in six games this season, but Djordje Petrovic came to their rescue with two astonishing saves from Orri Óskarsson in the final, dramatic minutes. It had been some battle and they had given everything.

That resistance hadn’t appeared necessary an hour or so earlier. Bournemouth had waited 127 years for a first European game and considerably less for their first goal. They had been playing 10 minutes and 43 seconds and when it came they celebrated it twice. A lovely shift of the body from Evanilson started it, the Brazilian receiving and releasing Adrien Truffert. The cross was perfectly placed, bent behind the defensive line for Kluivert to score.

High in the north-east corner Bournemouth’s fans went up but down in the south-west corner the flag did too, it didn’t take the video assistant referee long to prove that was wrong, and allowing them to do it all again while Iturralde set off into the street. Truffert was on the run again soon after, Alex Scott’s glorious long, looped, curling ball dropping into just the right place for Rayan to head the second.

View image in fullscreen Justin Kluivert fires Bournemouth into an early lead. Photograph: Robin Jones/AFC Bournemouth/Getty Images

There was an ease about the way Scott had completed the pass – an almost gentle turn of the ankle, the ball delivered as if by hand – and about the way he played. Amid the speed and intensity he glided. Around him, teammates flew everywhere, Marcus Tavernier especially, and Real Sociedad could not keep up. Three times they threatened from dead balls too: Evanilson headed the first off the post, António Silva headed the second wide and Óskarsson just about headed away a third. Songs from the corner sung to a backdrop of frustrated whistles from the rest of Anoeta.

From the home fans there was relief when half-time arrived without the lead being extended. There was also a reaction, a dash from Ander Barrenetxea signalling their intent and an increase in volume. Petrovic made a superb save from Beñat Turrientes on 56 minutes and almost immediately Real Sociedad pulled one back. Gómez’s curling cross bent all the way through, past the outstretched legs and into the far corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was a different game and a different place now, Real Sociedad’s version of Bad Moon Rising interrupted by an “huuy!” when Gonçalo Guedes’s effort was pushed past the post by Petrovic. Already this season Bournemouth had lost leads against Manchester City, Everton, Newcastle and Brentford, most of them late, and a familiar feeling only increased as Gómez’s fantastic ball sent Guedes through on the left, only for the Portuguese winger to try to cut inside rather than shoot. From the loose ball, Mikel Oyarzabal’s subtle, clipped shot floated onto the top of the bet.

Gómez was not their only problem. Luka Sucic shot wide on 81 minutes and then Gómez slipped Óskarsson in for what should have been the equaliser. Petrovic though saved that and, somehow, stopped the Iceland striker from five yards in the final minute.

Ultimately, the fireworks were finally over on Bournemouth’s famous night as a European journey that was once unimaginable was heard across the sea.

Sports.title: Pino kickstarts Crystal Palace’s Europa League rout of Lech Poznan to ease Sage’s worries
Sports.content:
It was worth the wait for Crystal Palace. After being denied their rightful place in the Europa League last season, Pierre Sage’s side made the perfect debut by brushing aside Lech Poznan with a victory that will take some of the heat off their new manager.

The Frenchman has big shoes to fill in replacing Oliver Glasner after his predecessor won three trophies in the space of 12 months and there had been some talk of disquiet behind the scenes following his decision to drop the teenager Jaydee Canvot at the weekend. But while Palace face a testing trip to face in-form Leeds on Sunday, having conceded 11 goals from their opening four Premier League matches, they were given a big helping hand by their opponents here well before Radoslaw Murawski was sent off late on for a reckless foul on Canvot.

The result was never in doubt after Poznan gifted Yéremy Pino a goal direct from their own throw-in, with Chris Richards and a Jørgen Strand Larsen penalty making the points safe by half-time. Eddie Nketiah rounded off the win with a late fourth and Sage was delighted to have shared in Palace’s historic moment before a meeting with his former club Lyon next month.

“I saw a lot of videos about the fans, especially during the journey in the Conference League last year,” he said. “They were incredible and I want to share the same thing with them this year.”

It’s a measure how quickly things have moved on in south London that Palace didn’t even have the chance to stage a parade to celebrate their Conference League triumph. But after a difficult start to the new campaign, the captain Dean Henderson had urged supporters to “park the negativity” when he signed a contract extension on Wednesday.

View image in fullscreen Jørgen Strand Larsen makes it 3-0 from the penalty spot. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA

Poznan’s European campaign started on 21 July and the Polish champions were backed by a vociferous travelling support. They were almost able to celebrate a goal inside the opening two minutes but the captain Mikael Ishak fluffed his lines as Palace showed their defensive frailties again.

As well as some noise around Sage following Saturday’s defeat by promoted Ipswich, there have been concerns about the atmosphere at Selhurst Park after the disbanding of influential supporters’ group the Holmesdale Fanatics. But after Terry Yegbe’s disastrous throw-in helped Palace take the lead, they were treated to two more goals before the break.

Richards headed in a deep corner from Adam Wharton and Strand Larsen dispatched a spot-kick after Pino was brought down by Murawski. There could have been another in spectacular fashion after Yegbe hammered the ball into his own net just before half-time but thankfully for him the assistant flagged for offside against Strand Larsen.

The Poznan fans decided that was the moment to perform the dance they have made famous. After their side’s poor first-half performance, it was no wonder that they preferred to turn their backs. At least they could amuse themselves by letting off a series of flares in the second half just as Pino came close to adding his second of the night.

Ismaïla Sarr’s first appearance of the season was greeted with the odd boo after his hopes of a move to Liverpool were dashed in the transfer window. But the reception for the Senegal forward was largely positive as Nketiah also came off the bench to complete the job on a night that Palace will hope can kickstart life under Sage.

Sports.title: Europa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled Celtic
Sports.content:
Celtic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Just weeks on from crashing out of the Champions League qualifiers to the Austrian side Lask, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic’s defensive flaws were exposed once more.

Martin O’Neill’s team also suffered a chastening 3-0 defeat by their rivals Rangers in the League Cup last weekend and failed to deliver on their manager’s promise to respond, with a home league derby against the Gers looming. Bamidele Yusuf opened the scoring for the visitors before Mika Baur equalised late in the first half. However, Kristoffer Zachariassen quickly put Ferencvaros back in front before Daniel Arzani’s sensational strike, on his return to Celtic Park, capped a fine night for Ferencvaros.

“We’re naturally disappointed getting beaten,” said O’Neill. “We started off very brightly. We had a number of balls that were flashed across the goal and no one there to put the ball in the net for us.

“Their first proper attempt, really, on goal yielded a goal for them. We came back into the game, got the equaliser just before half-time and then conceded a really poor goal. We’re hit on the break for the third goal. While we had a number of balls flashed across the box, even in the last 20 minutes, we didn’t get there to the front post a number of times that could’ve kept it alive and we’re beaten in the game.

“It’s a huge frustration, obviously, but it’s also psychologically quite damning as well. It’s not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers].

“Tonight was, I think, a European lesson for us in many aspects. We’ll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.”

Juventus hammered the Dutch side NEC Nijmegen 5-0 at home with help from two ⁠errors by the goalkeeper Nikolas Polster and Marseille lost 4-1 at Besiktas as the first ⁠round of Europa ⁠League matches wrapped up.

View image in fullscreen Nick Woltemade of Juventus battles for the ball during the victory against NEC. Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPA

The first howler from Polster allowed Nicolás González to nip in ahead of him ⁠and steal the ball to give Juve the lead in the ninth minute. A goal from Kerim Alajbegovic and a penalty ⁠from Nick Woltemade sent them in 3-0 up at the break.

Zeki Celik made it 4-0 in the 75th ‌minute before Polster again ‌came out of his goal and failed to clear the ball; this ‌time it was Randal Kolo Muani who rolled it into the empty net to complete the rout.

Marseille’s disastrous start to the season continued as they followed up three straight defeats in Ligue 1 with a comprehensive beating at the hands of Besiktas, with the Turkish side scoring three ‌goals without reply in the second half.

Earlier in the evening, the Greek side OFI Crete beat Germany’s Hoffenheim 2-0 at home, while RB Salzburg picked up a 1-0 win away to Levski Sofia in Bulgaria.

Sports.title: Floyd Samba’s debut double lifts Manchester City to Carabao Cup win over Norwich
Sports.content:
Floyd Samba lit up this tie with a debut that will have the 17-year-old grinning for a while after a superb goal in each half ensured Manchester City advanced to face Brighton in the last 16 in their defence of the Carabao Cup.

Samba has an older brother by a year, Tyrone, who is also in the academy. Their father, Christopher, is a former Blackburn and QPR defender.

With a game featuring speed, awareness and a poacher’s eye, he hopes to make a case for regular first-team game time. Given the elite-level forward competition this will be tough, but tonight was a fine calling card.

Samba said: “A debut like that is mind blowing. I couldn’t believe it – that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me.”

For Enzo Maresca, a sixth successive win maintains a 100% record for his nascent project (barring the Community Shield) and points to how the manager is shrugging off doubts about succeeding Pep Guardiola.

Of Samba, he said: “Satisfying for the two goals, the entire performance he was good. He didn’t play [before] as a 9, we tried in the last two or three days. He is very good at finishing so it was a very good game for him. He is not a 9 for sure but he was good.”

View image in fullscreen Ryan McAidoo (left) congratulates Floyd Samba after he scored Manchester City’s fourth goal against Norwich. Photograph: Nigel French /Apl/Sportsphoto

City host Sunderland here on Sunday. Defeat Régis Le Bris’ side and Maresca will enjoy his three-week international break. You would not bet against them doing so – City are improving with each outing, as they did against Norwich.

Many opponents are blown away at the Etihad, so for the 14th-placed Championship side to initially tap the ball about was impressive.

Maresca’s formation was fluid and reaped a first dividend when Nico O’Reilly’s cross was fumbled by the visiting goalkeeper, Daniel Grimshaw. The ball dropped to Allan and he delivered it back across for Samba to cutely head home.

City doubled their lead when Samba laid the ball off to Ayyoub Bouaddi, the midfielder hit the ball to Rayan Cherki and, as Grimshaw advanced, he beat the keeper to his right.

Watching from the touchline, Philippe Clement hoped his side were not about to crumble as the first half neared its end. He was relieved when Samba, running in, was thwarted by a Grimshaw dive at his feet.

Yet his men ended the period chasing City: an exhausting task that showed the control the hosts exerted. In a sparsely attended tie, this was precisely what Maresca wished – it meant that his main man, Cherki could be rested, as Ryan McAidoo replaced him for the second half.

Bournemouth v Aston Villa Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Soon, Allan joined Samba in registering on his City bow. From the left, the Brazilian zigzagged in, beat Sam Field once, cut back to beat him again, then found the far corner with a lethal strike.

Maresca will have been displeased after the restart to see a Norwich raid that swooped down the left and had the ball bouncing to Kellen Fisher in the area, but the right-back missed the target.

Fisher’s profligacy was punished when Samba made himself a cert for the player-of-the-match award with a second. He collected the ball inside Norwich’s area and shaped a sweet finish into the far right corner, the helpless Grimshaw watching it sail by.

Maresca was delighted with this and also the wider picture of how his side executed the gameplan. With each win he oversees, the Italian’s authority and stature grow, his appointment appearing ever shrewder.

The game’s closing stages were lit up by McAidoo’s sharp finish: an apt end to an impressive City victory.

Clement said: “After 20 minutes Manchester City started to get a bit annoyed because they could not create anything but then you get the first goal against and we need to defend better. In the second half we were more dangerous – I saw several good individual performances, but it is hard to take – six shots on target, five goals.”

Sports.title: FA chair Hewitt demands Infantino release records of failed World Cup plan
Sports.content:
The Football Association’s chair, Debbie Hewitt, has written to Gianni Infantino demanding that Fifa releases all documents relating to his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan and the decision to lift the USA striker Folarin Balogun’s suspension during last summer’s tournament.

The Guardian revealed last month that Hewitt and other members of the Fifa council were lobbying for an independent review of the proposed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) sell-off and the Balogun controversy. Their requests have been formalised in a letter sent to the Fifa president and his deputy, Mattias Grafström.

The letter, first reported by the Times, has been sent in advance of the Fifa council meeting in Zurich on 15 October. That is due to be the first time since the FFE plan emerged in July that Infantino will meet the other 36 members of the group that acts as Fifa’s board of directors.

A number of members of the council, which comprises 28 representatives of the six confederations, eight vice-presidents and Infantino, attempted last month to call an extraordinary general meeting to hold Infantino to account over FFE and Balogun.

The rebels were unable to get the 19 votes required to trigger such a meeting, however, and Hewitt’s call for the release of documents and an independent review is also likely to fail.

Infantino has not had any contact with the Fifa council since writing to it to withdraw FFE at the start of August and has been lobbying for support before next year’s presidential election, making visits to the Caribbean, South America, Morocco and Qatar.

Balogun’s ban was lifted after a phone call from Donald Trump to Infantino despite the player being shown a straight red card for serious foul play in the USA’s World Cup last-32 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. That allowed him to play against Belgium in the last 16, a match the USA lost 4-1.

View image in fullscreen Debbie Hewitt is taking the lead in holding Gianni Infantino to task despite the risk that it could affect the UK’s chances of hosting the 2035 Women’s World Cup. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images/PA

Fifa has said it followed due process, with the decision taken independently by its ethics committee, but has yet to publish a written report on the hearing. A request from the Royal Belgian FA for an explanation went unanswered.

Hewitt’s letter is understood to make reference to other governance issues at Fifa, particularly its response to the crisis caused by the FFE controversy this summer.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The FA’s willingness to take the lead in holding Infantino to task comes with some risk because the UK is the currently sole bidder for the 2035 Women’s World Cup. A decision on the hosts of that tournament and the 2031 edition is due to be made at an extraordinary Fifa congress on 23 November.

The deadline for candidates to stand in March’s presidential election is five days earlier. Infantino is the only candidate to publicly reveal his intention to stand, with Uefa and Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – working to find someone to stand against him.

The FA sent a letter of endorsement for Infantino’s fourth term as president before the World Cup but, along with several other European countries, has since withdrawn its backing.

Sports.title: England squad announcement: Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominic Calvert-Lewin recalled with Alex Scott included
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has handed Trent Alexander-Arnold a recall to the England squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures.

The right-back star fell out of favour under Tuchel following his move to Real Madrid and was subsequently left out of the World Cup squad.



5 Trent Alexander-Arnold is back with the Three Lions for the upcoming fixtures Credit: AFP

The former Liverpool ace has encountered a difficult start to the season but now has the opportunity to reignite his international career.

His last appearance in an England shirt came 15 months ago in the World Cup qualifying win in Andorra.

Who has been named in the England squad?

In total, there are eight new names included in Tuchel's Nations League squad from the one that travelled to the World Cup.



There is a recall for Alex Scott, while in-form Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin is named in the squad.

Bournemouth midfielder Scott received his first senior call up last November for the World Cup qualifiers against Serbia and Albania, but was unable to muster up his first international minutes.



Scott has been in blistering form for Bournemouth and starred in Thursday's Europa League win at Real Sociedad.

The 23-year-old has long remained in Tuchel’s plans and was part of England’s pre-World Cup training camp in the USA.



Meanwhile, Calvert-Lewin's call-up caps off a fine week for the striker after his goalscoring exploits for Leeds in their 4-1 win over Newcastle on Monday.

There is also a recall for Chelsea’s Cole Palmer after his omission from England’s 26-man World Cup squad.

Like Scott, the attacking midfielder has been rewarded for his promising start to the season.

5 Alex Scott will be hopeful of making his long-awaited England debut Credit: Getty



5 Cole Palmer is back in the England squad after missing out on the World Cup Credit: Getty

5

Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha has also got the nod from Tuchel while Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly, Newcastle's Lewis Hall and veteran Brighton goalkeeper Jason Steele are all included.

Notable absentees

Tuchel has once again overlooked Manchester City's Phil Foden.

The 26-year-old was another of the high-profile names to have missed out on Tuchel's World Cup squad and international exodus shows no signs of easing.



Morgan Gibbs-White has also been left out of the the Nations League squad.

The Nottingham Forest midfielder has not featured for the Three Lions since the 5-0 friendly win over Wales last October.

England take on world champions Spain at Wembley before trips to Czechia and Croatia.

England’s upcoming Nations League fixtures Spain (H) Saturday, September 26 - 7.45pm Croatia (A) Saturday, October 3 - 5pm Czechia (H) Tuesday, October 6 - 7.45pm Czechia (A) Tuesday, September 29 - 7.45pm

Tuchel’s side then round off the inflated international spell with a home game against Czechia.



It is Tuchel’s first gathering with his squad since their disappointing World Cup exit in July.

England were knocked out of the tournament at the semi-final stage, losing to Argentina 2-1 despite having led until the final ten minutes of the match.

They did, however, finish on a high note by beating pre-tournament favourites France 6-4 in the third place play-off match in Miami.

It marked England's best performance in a men’s World Cup since the victorious tournament of 1966.



But as with every post-tournament squad, a new cycle emerges with fresh faces aiming to force their way into the squad.

5 Tuchel's side face an immediate test of their credentials against world champions Spain next weekend Credit: Getty

Unlike Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp, Tuchel has opted against an inflated squad, instead opting for his customary 26 call-ups.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill interview with female reporter hints Celtic career is coming to an end
Sports.content:
Martin O’Neill interview with female reporter hints Celtic career is coming to an end

Martin O'Neill has been criticised for his uncharacteristic response in a frosty post-match interview following Celtic's latest defeat.

The Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at Celtic Park by Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday night.



3 O'Neill refused to explain his decision to change goalkeepers against Ferencvaros Credit: Getty

It marked a second successive defeat following their 3-0 loss at Rangers in the Scottish League Cup on Sunday.

O'Neill's frustrations were on display following the match as he spoke to TNT Sports' Connie McLaughlin.

The 74-year-old refused to explain his decision to change goalkeepers from the weekend.



Instead, O'Neill claimed he would answer the question on Celtic TV in a blunt response.

Viljami Sinisalo had come into the side to replace Sam Johnstone, who started the Old Firm derby.



What did Martin O'Neill say?

When asked by McLaughlin, O'Neill replied: "No, I won’t talk to you about the thinking behind that there. Sinisalo was always going to play that game as well too.

"Believe it or not Connie, my job is not to explain every single situation to you, much as you are going to ask and I’m delighted you are."



McLaughlin continued to probe, adding: "The reason I do that is that the fans outside will be asking the same question and it's my job to do the same?"

However, O'Neill bit back, responding: "I'll tell the fans then," to which McLaughlin said: "Well, this is your chance to do that then."

The Celtic boss refused to budge, though, stating: "Well, why don't I just tell the fans through Celtic TV."

3 Ferencvaros secured a comfortable 3-1 win over Celtic on Thursday night Credit: AFP



Their defeat to Ferencvaros followed a devastating exit from the Champions League last month.

Despite leading 3-0 from their play-off first leg against LASK, Celtic were beaten on aggregate following a 5-1 defeat after extra-time in Austria.

What did Alan Brazil say about Martin O'Neill's interview?

Alan Brazil has concerns O'Neill's outburst could mark the beginning of the end for his latest Celtic tenure.

However, the talkSPORT co-host stopped short of saying his time at the club is coming to an end.



Reacting to the interview on Friday's Breakfast show, Brazil admitted: "Martin’s been brilliant.

"His record at Celtic is magnificent and I’m not saying it’s coming to an end, I’m not saying that, but that really surprised me last night."

3 O'Neill's comments were 'surprising', says talkSPORT's Brazil Credit: Getty

Brazil added: "I understand Martin’s hurting and he’s annoyed, but there’s other ways of getting around that question."



Since returning to the club in January, O'Neill has won 29 of his 38 matches in all competitions, losing just six times.

O'Neill's current deal runs to the end of this season after he was rewarded for winning a league and cup double last term.

Following a spell as caretaker boss between October and December he returned to Celtic Park for a second stint as permanent manager.

Despite their European woes, his side have won all six of their Scottish Premiership matches so far this season.



However, that record will be put to the test against Rangers on Sunday as the sides meet at Parkhead.

Sports.title: Jamie O’Hara: Tottenham could win the Bundesliga and would challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona for LaLiga title
Sports.content:
Jamie O’Hara: Tottenham could win the Bundesliga and would challenge Real Madrid and Barcelona for LaLiga title

Jamie O'Hara believes that Tottenham Hotspur could win the Bundesliga and compete with Real Madrid and Barcelona for the LaLiga title.

The wild claim came after a clean sweep of wins for Premier League teams in Europe to show just how strong the English top-flight is.

4 Tottenham are without a goal in the Premier League, but to O'Hara, European leagues wouldn't be a problem Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Last week, the Champions League returned, and there were wins for Arsenal, Manchester City, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Manchester United.

The Europa League took centre stage this week with Sunderland, Bournemouth and Crystal Palace winning with relative comfort.

Spurs are yet to score in the Premier League this season and are coming into the year off the back of consecutive 17th place finishes.

However, due to the strength of the Premier League, O'Hara believes Spurs win the Bundesliga, Ligue 1 and would then compete for the LaLiga title.

It's fair to say that Jason Cundy couldn't believe what he was hearing.

Speaking on The Sports Bar, O'Hara said: "The Premier League is like a super league. No one can compete."

Cundy then asked O'Hara where he thinks Spurs would finish in the Bundesliga.

"I would say second, but it would be a title challenge with Bayern Munich," O'Hara responded.

"It would be PSG and Tottenham fighting it out, and LaLiga would be a three-horse race. I am saying Tottenham because I am a Tottenham fan, but I also think Bournemouth would be the same.

"Spurs could 100 per cent win the Bundesliga. You have only got to beat Bayern Munich, that's it. In LaLiga, it's a three-horse race, and that is how strong the Premier League is.

4 Cundy was left a little bit in disbelief at what he was hearing

Cundy then wanted to know what happened to Atletico Madrid, who knocked Spurs out of the Champions League last season.

O'Hara responded: "They are guff. They are not good. They are only good because they are playing in a crap league.

"We 100 per cent finish third in LaLiga. I don't think it is ridiculous what I've said.

"The Premier League is too strong for every other league. I watched AC Milan the other night, and they are absolute garbage.

"I am telling you, we would bop teams in Europe. Europe is guff. They are nowhere near good enough.

"It's just pointless. The Europa League is boring. The English teams get to the final."

4 Cundy's reactions were top drawer as O'Hara continued to make his point

Spending power

The financial might of the Premier League can be shown in the summer transfer spend.

And it isn't a new trend either as all top-flight teams splash the cash to try and achieve their aims in the Premier League.

But when you look at the actual numbers, they are quite staggering.

Over the past five seasons, the net spend of the Premier League is £5.5billion.

Compared to that, we have Serie A and LaLiga with net spend of £815m and £121m.

4 Bournemouth claimed their first-ever win in Europe, winning 2-1 at Real Sociedad Credit: Getty

Money makes the difference

There is no surprise that Premier League teams in Europe swat other sides away when you see the difference in transfer spend.

Then when you add in the revenue difference as well, the gap is likely to only widen.

The Conference League's inception was meant to give some teams from lesser countries a chance to win a trophy.

But from five seasons, three Premier League teams have won. It has given West Ham United and Crystal Palace moments they'll always treasure, while Leicester City and Aston Villa also went deep into the competition.

Last year, Villa claimed Europa League glory while Nottingham Forest got to the semi-final, only to lose to the Villans.

The evidence is there that the Premier League is growing stronger and stronger, and if you put teams from the top-flight in those leagues, they would almost certainly do well.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho handed major career warning in brutal dressing down from Troy Deeney
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney believes Alejandro Garnacho must look in the mirror to find out the culprit for his recent struggles.

Garnacho joined Aston Villa this summer, marking his third club in as many years, previously being at Chelsea and Manchester United.



3 Garnacho has played just 31 minutes for Villa this season Credit: Getty

However, the Argentinian winger's stint in the West Midlands has not quite gone to plan, having failed to start in any of his three appearances for the club.

Unai Emery reveals Alejandro Garnacho is 'behind' his teammates

Garnacho was an unused substitute for Villa in their 3-1 win over Coventry City in their Carabao Cup third round tie on Wednesday.

And when asked why Garnacho didn't get any game time, Villa boss Unai Emery stated it was because he'd slipped down the pecking order behind teenage academy graduate George Hemmings and Alysson.



"Garnacho is a little behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season," Emery said.

"It is time to be patient for the time he needs."

But Deeney, speaking on talkSPORT's Premier League All Access podcast, wasn't having it.



Troy Deeney's brutal verdict on Alejandro Garnacho

"I think Unai Emery is the type of manager that hopes to get the best out of somebody for a small period of time to get them moving, and he's willing to take that risk," Deeney said.

"He (Emery) believes that the group was strong enough that Garnacho would go into that and fall into line, in terms of what everybody else does and works on.



"But ultimately, I said this when he was at Chelsea because remember, he wanted to leave Manchester United, went to Chelsea and he was going to make it better, it was all Manchester United's fault.

"He goes to Chelsea, doesn't play, moves on and now it's all Chelsea's fault.

3 The 22-year-old's stock has fallen significantly in recent seasons Credit: Getty

"At some point, it might be you.

"I don't know the kid and don't ever want to know him, doesn't look like my cup of tea. But it might be that you are the fella that's the problem.



"When you're worried about your Instagram and your six-pack and how many earrings you've got in, you just need to worry about your football.

"You're not involved in the World Cup squad and you had it all there for you, you're not involved in the national team squad because [Lionel] Messi can't stand you.

"And now, year-on-year, your standards are going lower and lower.

"Considering he came up trying to be Cristiano Ronaldo, he does the opposite. He doesn't work hard and he doesn't deliver."

3 Emery has shown he's not afraid to make tough team calls Credit: Getty



Could Alejandro Garnacho endure a similar situation to Harvey Elliott?

Given Garnacho's Villa career has endured a stuttering start, some have inevitably drawn comparisons to Harvey Elliott's situation.

Elliott joined the Villans on a season-long loan from Liverpool last year, which would have become a permanent deal for £35million had he made ten Premier League appearances.

However, Emery made clear he did not plan to trigger the obligation, which left Elliott out in the cold for practically all of last season.

Like Elliott, Garnacho's move to Villa included a conditional obligation to buy should he reach a certain amount of appearances, although it is unclear what the conditions are.



But if Garnacho cannot win Emery over, he faces a season wasted on the sidelines.

At age 22, there is still plenty of time for Garnacho to revive his career and Emery has proven capable of doing so for the likes of Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio, who both enjoyed successful loan stints under the Spaniard.

Yet if Garnacho cannot knuckle down and usurp the likes of Hemmings and Alysson, there's every chance his season is over before it began, much like Elliott.

And, according to Deeney, there'd only be one person to blame.

Sports.title: Gary O’Neil’s dad dies as Ipswich boss pays emotional tribute
Sports.content:
Graham O'Neil, the father of Ipswich Town boss Gary, has passed away.

The Tractor Boys' manager confirmed the devastating news in an Instagram post on Thursday.

2 O'Neil shared the news of his father's passing on social media Credit: Getty

Gary O'Neil's touching tribute to his father

"Thanks for everything Dad," O'Neil wrote.

"I couldn't have done any of it without you.

"You taught me football, you taught me values and you taught me how to look after everyone that's important to me.

"What an incredible example you set. I'll miss you forever mate!"

Ipswich pay tribute to O'Neil's father

Ipswich also paid tribute to Graham via a post on X.

"All at Ipswich Town are deeply saddened by the passing of Gary O'Neil's father, Graham," the post read.

"Our thoughts, condolences and love are with Gary and his family at this incredibly sad time."

Confirmation of O'Neil's father's passing came two days after Ipswich's Carabao Cup exit to Arsenal.

The Tractor Boys were beaten 4-2, although they had already conceded all four goals before the hour mark.

Anis Mehmeti pulled one back in the 62nd minute for Ipswich before Chuba Akpom added another consolation goal in second-half stoppage time.

2 As it stands, O'Neil will take charge of Ipswich against Everton on Saturday Credit: AFP

Despite the loss, O'Neil, who was in the dugout for the match, believed there were positives to take.

"I thought they had a right go and stuck at it," O'Neil said.

"It didn't feel like a 4-0 game at any point, but the quality they have meant they got into that position.

"We found a way to fight our way back into it, though. I'm disappointed that we didn't win because that's what we're here for, but there are lots of positives to take.

"We managed to get some minutes into a lot of players that need it, and we still look a threat, which is the important thing for me.

"Arsenal are a good side defensively. They don't concede many chances at all, and we were still bale to get through. We were still able to create problems for them."

O'Neil's side is next in action on Saturday away at Everton, with kick-off scheduled for 3pm.

Sports.title: Man City-bound wonderkid, 16, handed USMNT call-up in new era after World Cup humbling
Sports.content:
Man City-bound wonderkid, 16, handed USMNT call-up in new era after World Cup humbling

Teenage whiz Cavan Sullivan's stock has taken yet another sharp rise.

The 16-year-old was named in Mauricio Pochettino's United States national team squad for the upcoming international break.

3 Sullivan is the Union's third-highest goalscorer this season with nine Credit: Getty

The make-up of the 28-man roster very much signifies a new era for the USMNT, with 12 players receiving their first call-up.

Adding to the freshness of the squad is that the average age of those called up is 22 years and nine months.

That is aided by the fact six players in the squad are aged 18 or under, including Sullivan, who turns 17 on September 28.

What has Mauricio Pochettino said about the USMNT squad?

"This is the beginning of a fresh start for everyone and we are excited in these first matches to bring a group of experienced players along with some young talents who have great potential," Pochettino said.

"It will be important that they all understand our culture, our way of working, and of course the principles of how we want to play.

"Most importantly, they must show the commitment to representing the country in the way our fans deserve."

Which big US names were not included in the 28-man squad?

There are a string of notable omissions, with Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie all left out.

However, McKennie is injured while Pulisic recently returned to fitness from a leg fracture he sustained at the World Cup.

As for Balogun, he has not featured for Monaco this season following his failed deadline day move to Everton.

Despite the trio's absence from the roster, all eyes will be Sullivan to see if he makes his debut.

Mauricio Pochettino's US squad for September and October international break Goalkeepers: Chris Brady, Matt Freese, Diego Kochen, Brian Schwake Defenders: George Campbell, Sergino Dest, Alex Freeman, Peyton Miller, Neil Pierre, Chris Richards, Antonee Robinson, Miles Robinson, Auston Trusty, Frankie Westfield Midfielders: Tyler Adams, Sebastian Berhalter, Zavier Gozo, Adri Mehmeti, Yunus Musah, Brooklyn Raines, Gio Reyna, Cavan Sullivan, Malik Tillman Forwards: Mathis Albert, Cole Campbell, Justin Ellis, Julian Hall, Ricardo Pepi

3 Pochettino led the US to a round of 16 berth at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Should Pochettino hand Sullivan his first senior cap, he would not be the USMNT's youngest ever player.

That record belongs to Freddy Adu, who made his international debut against Canada in January 2026 aged 16 years and 234 days.

How has Cavan Sullivan performed this season?

Regardless, the opportunity to get in front of Pochettino will be invaluable for Sullivan, who has dazzled for the Philadelphia Union this season with nine goals and nine assists.

Impressively, Sullivan has also made 21 starts for the Union this term, underlining how he has become a trusted member of the team despite his young age.

Unfortunately Philadelphia won't have Sullivan, who operates predominantly as a right midfielder, for much longer.

As part of the deal that brought him to the club at age 14, a clause was inserted into the contract that he would join Manchester City when he turns 18.

3 Maresca is gaining one of the US' brightest prospects for nothing next season Credit: Getty

Given Sullivan is only one year out from his 18th birthday, City boss Enzo Maresca will soon have to factor in the American midfielder into his plans.

But once the move is complete, Sullivan faces a serious challenge to break into City's starting line-up.

Antoine Semenyo, who joined City from Bournemouth in January, figures as the club's first choice at right wing.

English star Phil Foden is another right wing option, although he has struggled for form and was controversially sent off in his last outing.

The USMNT face Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada in their first matches since the World Cup, which saw them exit at the last 16 with a 4-1 thumping against Belgium.

Sports.title: Michail Antonio banned from driving for six months after being found guilty of offence
Sports.content:
Michail Antonio banned from driving for six months after being found guilty of offence

Watford striker Michail Antonio has been hit with a six-month driving ban.

Antonio was charged by the Metropolitan Police after he failed to identify the driver of his Lamborghini when it was suspected to be involved in a motoring offence in London in November.

2 Antonio found himself in hot water Credit: PA

The 36-year-old told Uxbridge Magistrates' Court he was not behind the wheel that night.

Instead, Antonio said he loaned out his car to his cousin while he was away in Manchester.

Antonio claimed he did not receive the police's initial letter, which asked for the driver's identity, and suggested it got lost in the post.

The ex-West Ham ace also gave evidence he was 'shocked' to learn, back in February, that he had been charged with failing to identify the driver.

He told the court that he left his cousin to respond to the charge and believed he had provided details of the guilty driver.

Michail Antonio's punishment in full

However, Antonio was ultimately found guilty of failing to provide information regarding the identification of the driver when required.

Along with a six-month driving ban, Antonio was ordered to pay a fine and court costs which totalled £2,050.

Antonio was hit with a £1,000 fine, £650 in prosecution costs and a £400 victim surcharge.

Prior to the verdict being handed down, Antonio already had six points on his licence.

He had previously been convicted of driving without insurance in July 2025.

2 Antonio said he was visiting his children in Manchester when the incident happened Credit: Getty

The additional six points he was given on Thursday meant an automatic six-month disqualification.

Antonio also stands accused of failing to respond to West Midlands police over a speeding offence in his Lamborghini and is set to stand trial over that charge next March.

Michail Antonio's troubling few years

The 36-year-old's latest off-field woes continue what has been a tumultuous few years.

His football career changed in an instant when he crashed his Ferrari in December 2024 and broke his leg. However, the player admitted he was fortunate to be alive after the crash.

Luckily for Antonio, he was able to complete a full recovery and returned to play with Qatari side Al Sailiya.

He then joined Watford on a one-year deal in September.
