Sports.title: Premier League press conferences: Mikel Arteta defends his furious outburst after Sunderland penalty decision - and reveals talks with referee chiefs
Sports.content:
It's the final Premier League gameweek before the international break, and managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press.

Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here...

Mikel Arteta said his criticism of the referee's decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal last weekend was through a duty to 'defend my club' and confirmed they have spoken to Pro Ref.

The Spaniard was incensed after referee John Brooks awarded the Black Cats a penalty for grappling in the area between Dan Ballard and Ezri Konsa.

He was adamant that Ballard had pulled Konsa to the ground and on the day labelled Brooks' decision as 'unacceptable'.

Ahead of Arsenal's Premier League fixture against Brighton on Saturday, Arteta said: 'I am here to try and give my opinion, defend my club, give the very best to my players.

Mikel Arteta said his criticism of the referee's decision to award Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal last weekend was through a duty to 'defend my club'

'In order to do so I need to respond in the most direct and fair way. I will make mistakes sometimes but I will try and be as fair as possible.

'We have a space to talk and give our opinions. It's everybody's duty to try and improve the game.'

Arsenal have since spoken to Pro Ref about the matter.

'We discuss many topics and very important all of them. To talk to give their opinions, and everyone's duty to try and improve the game,' he said.

When pushed on what was said, Arteta replied: 'It is a conversation that will remain private.'

He was also asked whether Arsenal received a direct apology like Manchester United did soon after the Manchester derby defeat to Manchester City: 'It is not about an apology. It is about agreeing that the decision should be different or not.'

Meanwhile, Arteta is optimistic that up to four injured defenders could return for the club's trip to the Amex.

Jurrien Timber, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie all did not feature in the midweek Carabao Cup squad against Ipswich Town.

'Everyone is fine. We still have another training session this afternoon, but I'm very optimistic about all of them,' he said.

'They all want to be involved, and we'll use the final session to make sure they're ready.'

Ben White was forced off at half-time at Sunderland but Arteta indicated all is well with his right back, stating: 'All good. We have another training session.'

By Isaan Khan

Sports.title: Liverpool and Leeds legend Gary McAllister, 61, 'faces financial ruin' after being hit with bankruptcy petition - with Scot involved in tax-avoidance scheme alongside fellow ex-players
Sports.content:
Liverpool and Leeds legend Gary McAllister, 61, 'faces financial ruin' after being hit with bankruptcy petition - with Scot involved in tax-avoidance scheme alongside fellow ex-players

Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition by HM Revenue and Customs.

The Liverpool and Leeds legend, 61, has been taken to court by HMRC over an unpaid tax bill, with the amount owed yet to be disclosed.

As reported by the Telegraph, McAllister is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were subsequently ruled to be tax avoidance schemes by HMRC.

The schemes offered investors substantial tax relief by using relatively modest investments backed by significant loans.

McAllister has not been accused of deliberately evading tax. His representatives say he believed his tax adviser was handling the matter with HMRC and that he is now seeking to bring the dispute to a swift conclusion.

HMRC has spent years pursuing ex-footballers and celebrities involved in the scheme for unpaid tax.

Gary McAllister is facing the threat of financial ruin after being hit with a bankruptcy petition

A spokesman told the Telegraph: 'We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans. We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort.'

McAllister, who is widely regarded as one of Scotland's greatest ever midfielders, enjoyed a successful career before his retirement in 2004.

He played a key role during Leeds United's title-winning campaign in 1991-92, helping the Yorkshire club win the last ever English First Division before it was rebranded to the Premier League.

After four years with Coventry City in the mid-1990s, the Scottish later joined Liverpool in 2000 and won the FA Cup, UEFA Cup and League Cup over a two-year spell at Anfield.

His career came to an end at Coventry, where he took on the role of player-manager in 2002, having made more than 150 appearances for the club across two spells.

Chalking up 57 caps over his glittering career, McAllister also captained Scotland for four years and famously missed a penalty against England during his country's 2-0 defeat at the 1996 European Championship.

McAllister is one of several former footballers facing the threat of bankruptcy.

Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this month that HMRC had filed a petition with the High Court to have former Liverpool star Jamie Carragher declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill reportedly worth between £700,000 and £800,000.

The Liverpool legend is understood to have been among a number of high-profile footballers who invested in film partnerships that were later ruled to be tax avoidance schemes

Last year, it was also reported that former Liverpool defender Steve Finnan and ex-Manchester City winger Shaun Wright-Phillips were facing separate bankruptcy petitions.

David James, Wes Brown, Lee Hendrie, Trevor Sinclair and John Barnes are among the former Premier League footballers to have been declared bankrupt by HMRC since 2010.

Sports.title: Extraordinary moment Martin O'Neill shuts down female reporter in 'patronising' and 'condescending' post-match interview after Europa League defeat
Sports.content:
Extraordinary moment Martin O'Neill shuts down female reporter in 'patronising' and 'condescending' post-match interview after Europa League defeat

Martin O'Neill has come under fire for his 'patronising' and 'condescending' response to a female TV reporter after he refused to explain his team selection following Celtic's 3-1 loss in the Europa League on Thursday.

The Scottish giants were soundly beaten by Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros in a dismal start to their Europa League campaign, with O'Neill making four changes to the side that lost 3-0 to Old Firm rivals Rangers on Sunday.

Goalkeeper Viljami Sinisalo was recalled to the starting XI in place of Sam Johnstone, while Oliver Sorensen, Haissem Hassan and James Forrest were also brought in by O'Neill.

When questioned about his team selection by TNT Sports reporter Connie McLaughlin after the game, O'Neill shut down the journalist in a manner described as 'patronising' and 'condescending' by fans on social media.

'No, I won't talk to you about the thinking behind that there. Sinisalo was always going to play that game as well too,' he told McLaughlin.

'Believe it or not Connie, my job is not to explain every single situation to you, much as you are going to ask and I'm delighted you are.'

Martin O'Neill has come under fire for his 'condescending' interview with a female TV reporter

Fans were angry with O'Neill's 'patronising' manner towards reporter Connie McLaughlin

Celtic were beaten 3-1 by Hungarian outfit Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday

When McLaughlin then suggested that supporters would be asking the same question, O'Neill responded: 'I'll tell the fans through Celtic TV.'

O'Neill has since faced widespread criticism on social media, with many supporters accusing him of being 'misogynistic' as well as supercilious.

Much of the backlash appears to have stemmed from viewers mishearing him call McLaughlin 'honey' when he actually said 'Connie', and the reporter has since taken to Instagram herself in an attempt to set the record straight.

'Glad I came back from Portugal,' she joked sarcastically on her Instagram story after conducting the spiky interview, before clarifying: 'Connie not honey'.

Droves of fans still hit out at O'Neill's patronising manner on social media.

'Very condescending - this type of attitude is what we need to get out the game,' one fan posted to X.

A second added: 'Horrible little condescending man.'

'Embarrassing himself and his club here,' wrote a third.

Another supporter furiously said: 'What a horrible and odious man he's shown himself to be. Not the first time he's spoken to a female reporter like that either.'

True to his word, O'Neill later addressed his team selection on Celtic TV.

'I think, in terms of balancing things, there are one or two players who deserve an opportunity,' he said.

McLaughlin took to Instagram to clarify that O'Neill referred to her as 'Connie' and not 'honey'

Fans hit out at O'Neill on social media, describing his attitude as 'condescending' and 'odious'

'For instance, James starts tonight. He has been an impact player for us and has been really terrific in that time. We have to give him a chance now to start a game.

'Will he last out the match? We do not know. He is 35 years of age, or whatever the case may be, but he has been a great player.

'There are a couple of things we have done tonight. Some players deserve to start in the side, James being one of them. Let us go and see how it goes.'

Sports.title: Inside the Beat Luke Littler auditions: Hundreds of darts hopefuls queue for hours to get their shot at facing star live on Netflix and winning £501k... and even Fallon Sherrock turns up!
Sports.content:
Thousands – filled with hope and confidence – arrive in east London for a chance to win £501,000.

Queues develop after an 8am start in Stratford, snaking around the Olympic Park. All for their shot at beating the most famous darts player around.

The idea of Luke Littler's new big-money Netflix show is simple. Can a novice beat Littler in a leg of darts? Up to 20 will try to do just that live on Netflix on October 30 in the streaming giant's new venture Beat Luke Littler.

Anyone who can topple the reigning world champion and world No 1 will take home a life-changing £501,000. Gary Lineker is the host, with Richard Osman providing expert analysis.

But first – the preliminary rounds, the audition – before the fame. Not just anyone will get an opportunity to potentially upstage Littler.

Contestants are allowed to prepare before a producer bellows out the rules. Another asks questions on camera: 'What would you do with the money? How did you get into darts? Don't answer like this, answer like this.' That's showbiz.

Surrounded by big purple and yellow advertising reading 'Beat Luke Littler' referees set out the rules and take their positions to ensure there's no cheating the automated scoring system.

More than 3,000 hopefuls auditioned for Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' in Stratford, London

Up to 20 people will be given the chance to win £501,000 on Netflix - all they have to do is beat Littler in a leg of darts

The aim of the first stage is to complete a leg of darts in 24 throws or fewer. No ifs, no buts, no second chances. It's no easy feat. This part-timer may achieve it on a good day – locked away in his spare room while music plays on late evening. Under this sort of pressure is a different story. As expected, failure was the outcome.

But a lot of these contestants don't crumble under the pressure – they thrive off it.

'I can beat anyone on my day,' one auditionee, who wrapped up his leg in 12 darts, tells Daily Mail Sport. Wrap things up in 12 again on October 30 and he will more than likely find himself £501,000 richer.

Two or three participants make it through to the next stage. They are awarded a green sticker. 'Thanks for coming, and, if you didn't make it, don't worry - it's hard,' shouts another producer.

There are various abilities on show. Some wear jeans and get nowhere close. Others don their own personal darts shirts but struggle for a double. Others ease through – including 'Queen of the Palace' Fallon Sherrock.

For Sherrock, who has won two matches at the World Championship before – it's all part of the day job. She's probably the most famous face here. Anyone who has never held a tour card can enter – Sherrock may have won matches at the Alexandra Palace, but she's never been on the tour.

'I did it in 18,' she tells Daily Mail Sport. 'My scoring wasn't very good, but I took out a 157.

'I don't need the money, but I have always said I would like more opportunities to promote the women's game, and this is the perfect opportunity to do it. Why wouldn't you? It would be stupid for me not to do it.

'The queue was very long. We joined at 8am and got in at near enough 11am. But I can do it - and I do speak to Luke. I know him, I know his mum, his dad, Faith, and they are lovely, genuine people.'

Daily Mail Sport auditioned for the new show - but failed to make it past the first stage

Those with the skill or fortunate enough to make it to the second stage face an interview with the production team, where they will discuss their approach to the challenge, how they would prepare to face Littler, and how they'd perform under pressure.

Even fewer will then make it to the final stage. That involves a chat with an expert judging panel, including 16-time world champion Phil Taylor.

Darts mastermind Barry Hearn walks past. 'Alright, lads?' he quips to the press.

Taylor is in for the long-haul, an 11-hour day in total. 'I think someone will win it,' he says. 'They have got a chance. It's all about holding your bottle on a double.

'It's been different. I've never done anything like this before. It's similar to the X-Factor, but you have to be a bit nicer with this one. I'm not Simon Cowell.

'It's about encouraging the players, especially the youngsters coming through. It's very nerve-wracking for them. But we are looking for confidence, ability, and they have to be dedicated. It's not easy - you have to be so professional now. I was 30 when I first turned pro - some of them now are 13, 14, 15. To ask them to be professional at that age is very difficult.'

Laura Turner (left), Barry Hearn (centre) and Phil Taylor (right) are on the judging panel for the final stage of the audition process

The volume of interest in the show runs in line with the growth of the sport since Littler burst onto the scene

Littler isn't here. He's taking some time off before getting back into action with more Players Championship events and the World Grand Prix among events to come soon.

It's unclear what he really thinks about this show – nothing is really on the line for him compared to the competitors, bar maybe pride.

'If you can go out in 12 darts, and you want to beat Luke Littler in a game of 501, he has to go out in nine, or you're half a million richer,' Taylor tells Daily Mail Sport. 'That's the secret.

'Luke is very laid back, quiet, very talented. Nothing fazes him, but the one attribute he has for me is he isn't bothered about the money. It's a bonus. I was always bothered about the money when I started - I had children, a mortgage to pay.

'I have had a throw with him. Not competitive. But I would love to get my form back, I am practicing a little bit. I am a bit too old now. I love retirement - it's great being at home. I ask my wife if we should go on holiday and we don't want to go away anymore, we travelled that much. I missed my family.'

While speaking to Taylor, one or two more competitors try their luck. One owns an international flavouring company. Another is an electrician. They both have their green stickers and are waiting to speak to producers before potentially being put in front of the judges.

Simple maths says around 600 dart hopefuls will make it through the first stage here in London. That number will be whittled down to barely double figures by the time they have met the judges. The same process will happen in Manchester. Those auditions take place on Saturday at Manchester Central Convention Complex – you can visit BeatLukeLittler.com for more information on how to apply.

Leaving four hours after arriving the queues are still as long. A member of the Netflix production team tells us they think way more hopefuls have arrived than expected.

One thing is obvious: this idea, so far, is a hit. The attraction and attention runs parallel with the rise of darts since Littler burst on the scene. Next month, those that look up to the 19-year-old will have the chance to beat him and win big money. Why wouldn't you turn up?

Watch Beat Luke Littler live on Netflix on October 30

Sports.title: Inside Leicester Tigers' three-year plan to conquer the PREM: Lessons from Sandhurst, bull-fighting trips, Geoff Parling's coaching shake-up and the summit that offers major hint on Ollie Chessum's future
Sports.content:
Early last week, Leicester Tigers skipper Ollie Chessum knocked on the door of the club’s chief executive, Andrea Pinchen, to discuss the future.

‘He came into my office for a quick chat that ended up being an hour and a half long,’ Pinchen tells Daily Mail Sport.

There was a debrief of the club’s summer trip to France, where the players enjoyed a cheese and wine evening but left with mixed emotions about a visit to the bull-fighting. But the conversation focused more on what lies ahead.

England and Lions lock Chessum has become the most influential player at Welford Road and locking down his long-term future is one of the club’s biggest priorities. He is out of contract next summer but renegotiations are underway.

Huw Bevan, the head of rugby operations, joined the meeting and over a packet of Hobnobs, they outlined how the three Chessum brothers are at the heart of a three-year plan.

‘We veered off course a little bit,’ says Pinchen. ‘We talked about Dylan, Ollie’s younger brother, who lives with him and Lewis. I said: “If you’re living at home with your brothers, how great would it be to get a camera on you and do a social media video about what you’re cooking?”

England and Lions lock Ollie Chessum has become the most influential player at Leicester Tigers and locking down his long-term future is one of the club’s biggest priorities

‘I want evolvement of our game, rather than any radical changes,’ says Tigers head coach Geoff Parling

Centre Joseph Woodward makes his way out ahead of Leicester's PREM Rugby Cup group stage match against Newcastle last weekend

‘The supporters want to get to know the players and see behind the scenes. We’ve got a club-wide strategy and it’s important for the players to be part of that. We discussed the club strategy, the three-year plan and what we want to achieve. We’re all very much aligned on that.

'Ollie wants to win now but he also wants the club to win in three, five and 10 years’ time. He sees the importance of the academy, so we talked about that.

‘You want to be open and honest. We go out for dinner with the senior leadership team probably once a quarter. Myself, (head coach) Geoff Parling, (finance director) Fintan Kennedy, Joe Heyes, Jack van Poortvliet, Freddie Steward.

'Everything is on the table. “What’s the gossip in the changing room? How much of it is true? How do we get tighter?”

‘For me, it’s marrying that performance with the business. If Ollie speaks to someone from corporate sales, we want them to be talking the same language. We need to get to a sustainable position and that’s our main goal, but our ambition is to be in the top two and lifting a trophy.

'That’s not three years. That’s this year. How do we generate that income to invest back into the playing side? We want to show that picture so that everybody in the club knows what they’re working towards. Presumably Ollie will be here for five years to talk about the five-year plan… we’ll see!’

At boardroom level, there are ongoing discussions around facilities. The club’s Oval Park training ground is basic by current PREM Rugby standards. The stadium’s Crumbie Stand is still made up of dated wooden seating. There is permission to develop the land outside Welford Road.

‘The training ground is a tricky one because we don’t own it,’ says Pinchen. ‘You develop it and you want to make sure you’ve got the best facilities to train, but you’ve got to marry that with how much investment you put into a training facility you don’t own.

'We’re looking at that all the time. We’ve looked at buying a plot. We’ve looked at sharing other facilities. Everything is on the table. It’s a constant piece of work that we’re looking at.

‘With the stadium, some people look at the [Crumbie] Stand and say, “You’ve got to develop that soon, it’s a wooden stand”. It probably won’t change any time soon. When the lads are running out and everyone’s stamping their feet… you want to keep some of that tradition.

‘Then we’ve got land around the stadium, with the hotel and the plaza site. We’ve got potential for a multi-storey car park on the other side, which we’ve looked at previously.

'Those plans got put on hold because of Covid – something that would have cost £8-9million shoots up – but that may be something we can revisit.’

There is permission to develop the land around Leicester's Welford Road stadium, although the club don't plan to give its stands a face-lift

Fly-half Billy Searle has signed a new contract. The club moved quickly to secure his future, removing the threat of an offer from Saracens

The headline-making business, however, focuses on the playing group.

Fly-half Billy Searle has signed a new contract. Searle's stock rocketed last season and the club moved quickly to secure his future, removing the threat of an offer from Saracens, who remain uncertain about Fergus Burke’s future. Scrum-half Van Poortvliet is also in advanced negotiations about a new deal.

Consistency is key for Leicester, who have churned through 10 head coaches since 2013. They have not joined the wave of new PREM financial investment and their recruitment plan is built around homegrown talent.

‘We’ve been fortunate for a number of years that our two major shareholders are so supportive of us – Tom Scott and Peter Tom,’ says Pinchen. ‘They want to see the club flourish and grow. They’re not looking to make a quick bit of money.

'They’re personally and emotionally invested. There are a lot of conversations happening across the PREM with Red Bull and Dyson coming to town (at Newcastle and Bath respectively). A lot of people are suddenly looking at rugby and thinking, “This could be interesting” but our major shareholders are super supportive.

'We’re sitting in a good place. Our main goals from a commercial side are to get our data systems really singing, enabling us to fill the stadium.

‘We want to be the best and to be competing every year, but we don’t want to block our academy growth. We really want to nurture from within. When we’re looking at our recruitment pathway and depth chart for three years’ time, we don’t want to sign somebody who is going to block that pathway.

'Look at Mako Vunipola. We’ve got a history of signing more experienced, older players that has worked so well for us in the past with Mike Brown, Chris Ashton and Richard Wigglesworth. They worked so hard and shared so much. It’s about marrying that sprinkling of international experience with those real Leicester-through-and-through youths.’

Following the departures of support staff Brett Deacon, Peter Hewat and Alex Davies, Parling has been forced to shuffle his backroom team over the summer.

Rod Seib, Craig Childs, Craig Newby and Freddie Burns have all joined the club. Analyst Matt Egan was also poached by England, with Simon Barbour returning after a stint with the All Blacks under Scott Robertson.

Scrum-half Ollie Allan in action against Newcastle. First-choice No9 Jack van Poortvliet is set to sign a new contract

Former Tigers fly-half Freddie Burns, who won the Premiership in 2022, is back at the club in a coaching capacity

‘I want evolvement of our game, rather than any radical changes,’ says Parling, who invited all his new staff around to his house for a BBQ during the summer.

‘There are a few tweaks. Can we improve a few areas of our attack when we lose momentum? Can we force errors a bit more with our defence? When things aren’t going our way, can we go back to our fundamentals and wrestle back momentum?

‘In terms of the environment, we’re thinking more about how we can adapt and communicate under pressure. We’ve had guys from Sandhurst come in to look at effective communication. Finding out what they do when their communication goes wrong when they’re on the frontline.’

New mauling interpretations have been another focus point throughout the off-season. Defenders are no longer able to disrupt by ‘swimming’ up the side of the ruck, providing an advantage to the attacking team.

Leicester are traditionally one of the strongest mauling teams in the league and lock Cameron Henderson says their pack welcome the changes.

‘This is the first time playing club rugby with the new interpretations,’ says Henderson. ‘It gives a massive advantage to the attack. It means guys on the outside of the maul are now completely redundant, so if you have a very square maul, you’re more likely to score.

'Defensively, you need to be more violent early on. It doesn’t change a huge amount but it gives you a huge advantage in attack. I’d definitely say it’s something we welcome. Geoff and (assistant coach) Neil Fowkes spoke about it in pre-season. It’s an important thing for boys to get their heads around.

‘It’s been nice to come into a pre-season with continuity of head coach. It makes a huge difference in terms of knowing what’s expected of you and where you stand. The defensive system has changed and we’ve got a new attack coach but the fundamentals are the same. We’ll keep trying to evolve but we won’t go away from our identity.’

Sports.title: Martin O'Neill admits his Celtic side were taught a harsh European lesson in timid defeat to Ferencvaros
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill admits his Celtic side were taught a harsh European lesson in timid defeat to Ferencvaros

Exasperated Celtic boss Martin O’Neill insisted his side were given a European lesson as they crashed to a demoralising home defeat to Ferencvaros in their Europa League opener.

Already hurting from their bruising 3-0 Premier Sports Cup quarter-final defeat to Rangers at Ibrox last weekend, O’Neill’s men failed to lift spirits in the east end of Glasgow as they slumped to a thoroughly unconvincing loss to a side currently sitting fifth in the Hungarian top flight.

To rub salt in the wounds, one-time Celtic winger Daniel Arzani tormented his former side with an impressive display and a killer third goal shortly after the interval.

The visitors had gone in front through Bamidele Yusuf’s deflected shot but Celtic levelled in the 44th minute through Mika Baur.

However, in an all too familiar European collapse from the home side, they conceded a goal to Kristoffer Zachariassen a minute later to leave O’Neill cursing their fragility.

The Celtic manager said: ‘It’s a huge frustration, obviously, but it’s also psychologically quite damning as well.

Martin O'Neill admitted Celtic didn't take enough risks in Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros

‘Just when you’ve fought your way back into the game and you think, well if you can’t deal with the minute the fourth official puts up, at least defend it properly and we didn’t do that. That was really disappointing.

‘It’s not the start we wanted. We have seven games in which to try and get some points on the board. Tonight was I think a European lesson for us in many aspects.’

O’Neill insisted his side have to be braver – starting with Sunday’s crucial Premiership clash with Rangers at Celtic Park.

‘When we have decent possession of the ball, just don’t give it away,’ he said. ‘But also I think taking a few risks as well too — risks in the proper areas of the field.

‘We really need to concentrate now on Sunday [against Rangers]. We’ll get ourselves together. We need to re-energise ourselves as much as anything else.’

O’Neill had shaken up his team following their Ibrox defeat last weekend, with misfiring striker Kasper Hogh dropping to the bench and Camilo Duran selected to start up front.

Viljami Sinisalo and the Celtic defence react in horror after Kristoffer Zachariassen's goal

There was also a change between the sticks as Sam Johnstone – shaky in the Premier Sports Cup defeat to Rangers – was dropped for Viljami Sinisalo.

Asked by TNT Sports trackside reporter Connie McLaughlin to explain his thinking behind the decision to replace Johnstone with Sinisalo, O’Neill snapped: ‘No, I won’t talk to you about the thinking behind that there. Sinisalo was always going to play.

‘Believe it or not Connie, my job is not to explain every single situation to you, much as you are going to ask and I’m delighted you are.’

When pressed by McLaughlin over the fact supporters might want to hear his reasoning, O’Neill replied: ‘Well, why don’t I tell the fans through Celtic TV?’

Sports.title: A new star is born for Man City as Floyd Samba's double steals the show, how Allan fared on his long-awaited debut and Enzo Maresca copies from the Pep Guardiola playbook in 5-0 thrashing of Norwich
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki raced back to halfway. He'd just given former Manchester City academy graduate Daniel Grimshaw the eyes, a second home goal of the evening, and then compelled to get the tie restarted as quickly as possible.

Clearly, Cherki wanted more goals. More opportunity to make up for the lost half at Old Trafford last weekend, when he was withdrawn at the break owing to Phil Foden's red card. More opportunity to have some fun. Maybe to prove a point, if such things are possible on a straightforward Thursday night against Championship opposition, although Maresca visibly sighed at some flicks.

Fortunately for Mathias Kvistgaarden, his wits were very much about him by the time Cherki had made it back to the centre circle, hurling the ball in the Dane's direction. With impressively quick hands, Kvistgaarden just about stopped it from bursting through his fingers.

The trouble was, the majority of City's players were still celebrating up the other end after two goals in as many minutes on the half-hour had effectively secured their spot in round four here against Brighton.

And despite Cherki's efforts, the evening really belonged to a 17-year-old who first set foot on this campus as a junior.

Rayan Cherki was on the scoresheet as Manchester City beat Norwich 5-0 in the Carabao Cup

FAMILY AFFAIR

When all eyes were on JJ Gabriel of Manchester United, Floyd Samba curled home a wonderful 25-yard free kick in last May's FA Youth Cup final. A genuine moment of class. The pedigree was there for all to see.

Just four months later, he has topped that - and then some.

His mother, Theresa, was already emotional before Ruebyn Ricardo blew the first whistle. Sat next to Tyrone, the older brother also in City's ranks, she was crying as the teams lined up and spotted her son among them. To be fair, with the blonde locks, he is tricky to miss.

Samba's opener, heading in other outfield debutant Allan's cross, was reward for a tremendous bow as a senior player. Usually an attacking midfielder, Samba - son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Chris, also sat with pride in the corporate Tunnel Club - was thrown up front and linked play brilliantly.

For Cherki's goal, it was Samba dropping off the front and laying to Ayyoub Bouaddi that made the move. Intelligence City approve of. By the time Samba curled home from the edge of the box to secure a brace after half-time, a sumptuous effort, Chris was leaping in the air in much the same way as Premier League strikers had witnessed for so many years previous.

'A debut like that is mind blowing,' said an ecstatic Samba who only found out he was in the team on Tuesday. 'I couldn't believe it myself - but that's just the beginning, I've got a big career ahead of me.'

This experience must whet the appetite of another son in City's academy, Emerson, a central defender in the club's Under 13s. Samba Sr was later gladly taking the adulation from other parents behind the dugouts on yet another occasion that shows off what the youth setup has put together in these parts - especially in the context of what has happened over the road with Gabriel this week.

That two other teenagers who featured, Ryan McAidoo and Kaden Braithwaite, also starred in May's Under 18s final speaks volumes. And McAidoo's top finish in stoppage time was further testament to the ability of those coming through.

Floyd Samba had plenty to smile about after a goalscoring debut during Manchester City's win

THE KEY FOR ALLAN

City had been tracking Allan, the 22-year-old winger signed from Palmeiras last month, for some time. Director of football Hugo Viana says for the past two years and there is a belief that he can be moulded into a useful option.

Viana has instructed staff to give the Brazilian - who hails from Florianopolis, an island off the country's southern coast - the time required to adapt to life in England. They think he can operate on either side, evidenced here, but are pleading for patience.

MATCH RATINGS Man City (3-1-5-1): Rulli 7; Khusanov 7, Reis 7, Bouaddi 7; Allan 8 (Braithwaite 71, 6), Lewis 7, Cherki 8 (McAidoo 46, 7), O’Reilly 7, Ait-Nouri 7; Samba 9 Manager: Enzo Maresca 7 Norwich City (4-2-3-1): Grimshaw 5; Fisher 6, Darling 6, Alves 6 (McConville 71, 6), Yongwa 6; Wright 6, Field 5; Crnac 6 (Musaba 62, 6), Slimane 5 (Toure 71, 6), Diallo 5 (Maghoma 46, 6); Kvistgaarden 6 Manager: Philippe Clement 6 Referee: Ruebyn Ricardo 7

There is probably good reason for that - marker Darlin Yongwa occasionally more physical in duels - but the debut will go down as a triumph.

‘It was not easy for him, his first start, it's always complicated but it was important for him to see a little bit the English competition,' said Maresca post-match.

'That is a bit different from South America so overall it was good.’

Allan's instinctive half-volleyed cross for Samba's opener showed strong instincts. More of that was seen three minutes after half time, chopping from left foot to right and then squirming past Grimshaw – a goal that will do him no harm and the Etihad Stadium's south stand appeared quickly to fashion a terrace chant to the tune of 'I Predict a Riot' by Kaiser Chiefs.

Even so, there were signs that Allan may be here for other reasons too. Palmeiras have utilised him as a wing back in recent months and in his final game for the club, a 4-1 win over Vasco, he did most of his best work tracking back.

That was obvious inside five minutes of his City debut, tracking in behind right back Rico Lewis to thwart a threatening Norwich counter that had the hosts briefly scrambling for position.

'Coming to the Premier League from Brazil is a big step but we also believe that he will be an important player in that position,' Viana said.

Allan impressed for City and was also on the scoresheet during the third-round cup victory

NORWICH HAD THEIR OWN BRAZILIAN TALENT ON SHOW

Allan was not the only young Brazilian unfamiliar with the English game. Bruno Alves, a 21-year-old central defender, signed on loan from Cruzeiro in the summer and Norwich have an option to purchase at around £2million in the summer.

Alves had only featured for 70 minutes so far this season but challenges like this are seen as key in his development.

ENZO THE ECCENTRIC

It's already become clear that Maresca will not pass up the chance to lean into his tactical creativity and the sight of City's formation in the opening 20 minutes underlined some similarities with his predecessor.

Three at the back – but one of them was holding midfielder Bouaddi, with the Moroccan having to check himself a couple of times into remembering exactly where he was playing in different phases of the game.

Mateo Kovacic held midfield on his own and then the other six – including the goalscorers, Lewis, Rayan Ait-Nouri and Nico O'Reilly – ploughed forward. This could potentially be some sort of blueprint for league matches where City expect the opposition to sit in deep.

Perhaps the biggest takeaway for Maresca himself, though, was that Erling Haaland had the entire night off - not even on the bench.

Sports.title: Rory McIlroy's £9m mansion he retreats to after BMW Championship with famous neighbours
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy's £9m mansion he retreats to after BMW Championship with famous neighbours

Rory McIlroy has been competing at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth Club this week, which is a stone's throw from his luxury residence

View 7 Images Rory McIlroy can walk to his extravagant mansion from this week's event (Image: Getty Images)

Rory McIlroy wrapped up his opening round at the 2026 BMW PGA Championship and then had just a short walk back to his new £9million mansion at Wentworth.

‌



This week's tournament marks McIlroy's first appearance at Wentworth Club since moving into the exclusive gated estate with his wife Erica and their daughter Poppy. It is a substantial advantage for the Holywood-born star who typically depends on his private jet for travelling to and from tournaments.

‌



The six-time Major champion has relocated his main summer base from Jupiter, Florida. McIlroy said ahead of the tournament that playing virtually on his doorstep makes the week feel like a true home fixture.

‌



"It's always nice to be back, I guess even more meaningful now that we have a home here," he said. "It really does feel like a home event. I haven't always had the best of times around the West Course, but certainly over the last few years I've played well here, given myself some chances to win.

"I feel it's a great event. A great field is always assembled, and we always play in front of an amazing atmosphere. Honestly, it's one of my favourite weeks of the year. Looking forward to getting going again."

Shane Lowry's private text to Rory McIlroy after Irish Open champion skipped celebration READ MORE :

McIlroy launched his week on Wednesday with a stunning, flawless 12-under-par 60 to steal the show in the celebrity Pro-Am alongside teammates including Stuart Broad. The back-to-back Masters champion carded nine birdies and an eagle across a breathtaking 10-hole stretch.

‌



His impressive form carried into his opening official round on Thursday, where he completed it with a solid 3-under-par 69. Since his debut at the BMW PGA Championship in 2008, McIlroy has forged an outstanding record, claiming the title in 2014 and finishing as runner-up on three occasions.

View 7 Images The mansion in Wentworth, pictured before a makeover, which Rory McIlroy and his family bought (Image: N/A)

With him now a local resident, that record looks set to improve further. The 37-year-old snapped up the property in 2023 and it was already among the finest homes in the area before the couple embarked on a renovation project.

‌



McIlroy has completely transformed the six-bedroom mansion after leaving their £16.5m residence in Florida. Our photographs were taken prior to the golfer beginning his renovation work, while the property was still on the market in the prestigious estate.

Nevertheless, the stunning features that await the family as they settle into life in the UK are plain to see. "Straight after Augusta, we travelled over to see the house as it was going through the finishing touches," McIlroy said earlier this year. "It was fun to see and we could've stayed in it, but we wanted to get over to Holywood first."

View 7 Images The home cinema at Rory McIlroy's Wentworth home (Image: N/A)

‌



Upon stepping inside, visitors are greeted by a sweeping staircase and a welcoming fireplace, complemented by traditional artwork and an array of rugs across the floors. It's likely that McIlroy and Erica have since put their own stamp on this entrance hall with some personal interior design touches.

Moving through to the living room, the generously sized space features two sofa suites, a plush single armchair and yet another fireplace. The open-plan layout gives the new owners a clear sightline into the seating area from the kitchen.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The couple are also likely to have given the living room a makeover, with McIlroy's impressive trophy collection expected to grace the bookshelves alongside a top-of-the-range entertainment system.

Perhaps most impressive of all is a spectacular home cinema room, large enough to host a proper movie night with friends and family. A vast television dominates one wall, while the remaining walls are painted a deep red, nodding to the charm of classic old-school picture houses.

View 7 Images The bathroom at Rory McIlroy's new Wentworth property (Image: NA)

‌



Plush leather recliners fill the room, along with a small central table, perfect for resting your snacks and drinks during a film. This room, too, will undoubtedly have received the McIlroy treatment, as the family set about modernising the entire property and enhancing its overall value.

The property continues with six bedrooms and an undisclosed number of bathrooms. One bathroom featured online showcases a generous bathtub and a wet-floor shower.

The bathroom is fitted with all-white fixtures, including a floating toilet and bidet. Natural daylight streams through two windows positioned beside the bath, complementing the LED overhead lighting throughout the space.

‌



Another aquatic feature is the spectacular indoor pool, accompanied by a hot tub and floor-to-ceiling patio windows wrapping around half the room. The pool's illumination mirrors the water's shade, with deep blue tones establishing a tranquil environment where McIlroy will likely unwind after his professional commitments.

View 7 Images The entrance hall at Rory McIlroy's Wentworth property, with a grand staircase and open fire (Image: NA)

This represents one of the most contemporary spaces in the entire property and is something the golfer may opt to preserve as is. That said, he might enhance the area by incorporating a sauna or red-light therapy facilities - both popular recovery methods for modern athletes.

‌



McIlroy is believed to have invested up to £14m altogether when factoring in the costs of renovations to extend and modernise the estate. The property's exterior matches its interior splendour, with attractive trees, landscaping and immaculately kept lawns bordering the driveway leading to the residence.

With a home course at one of England's most prestigious golfing establishments, it comes as no surprise that McIlroy counts some of the UK and Europe's most recognisable celebrities among his neighbours.

View 7 Images The indoor pool at the Wentworth property bought by Rory McIlroy

‌



Four-time Major champion and former World No.1 Ernie Els was not only once a resident of Wentworth, having owned a property along the 16th hole, but was appointed the club's "world-wide touring professional" in 2005 and has overseen two major redesigns of the West course.

Back in 1992, the former Duchess of York, Sarah Ferguson, found herself at the centre of a media frenzy involving her American financier boyfriend John Bryan. This led her to seek refuge in the gated community of Wentworth and Romenda Lodge.

Few residents of Wentworth Estate are more celebrated than singer-songwriter Sir Elton John, who first moved there in the 1970s and is renowned for hosting numerous extravagant parties over the years. The cover of his 1974 compilation album Elton John's Greatest Hits was also photographed at his Wentworth home.

Article continues below

View 7 Images The living area, opening into the kitchen at the Wentworth property bought by Rory McIlroy (Image: NA)

Former Ukraine and Chelsea forward Andriy Shevchenko also possesses a £7m residence at Wentworth where, in 2012, he reportedly sought council approval to construct a six-car garage featuring remote-controlled hydraulic ramps to raise or lower vehicles from an underground car park.

His former Chelsea colleague John Terry is another avid golfer and has a property in the vicinity. Another notable Wentworth Estate resident is 2013 US Open champion and ex-World No.1 Justin Rose, who was raised 30 minutes away.

Sports.title: Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac brutally mock Spygate saga ahead of Wrexham vs Southampton
Sports.content:
Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac brutally mock Spygate saga ahead of Wrexham vs Southampton

Wrexham and Southampton meet in the Championship this weekend and the Red Dragon's Hollywood owners have made some mischievous digs over the Spygate scandal

View Image Southampton fans had mocked the Spygate saga before their team was thrown out of the play-offs (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

Wrexham co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney have dropped a video poking fun at the 'Spygate' saga ahead of this weekend's meeting with Southampton.

‌



The Saints were expelled from the Championship play-offs after beating Middlesbrough to reach the final and docked four points after an intern was found observing their opponents during a training session, with further charges brought against the club for similar offences earlier in the season ahead of games against Oxford and Ipswich Town.

‌



Wrexham were one of the teams who narrowly missed out on a play-off spot last season, finishing seventh in the Championship.

‌



This time around, the club owned by Hollywood stars Reynolds and McElhenney - now also known by just Mac - are eager to go one better and reach the Premier League - and they have already stoked the flames ahead of a big game against Tonda Eckert's side.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



In the short video, which BBC Sport claims has not been well received by senior EFL figures, Reynolds and McElhenney make quips about privacy in a skit to promote their primary sponsor, Firefox.

After emerging from behind a tree with McElhenney, Reynolds says: "Today, for no particular reason, we want to talk about the importance of privacy." McElhenny then adds: "Specifically, how to prevent spies from seeing what you're doing."

The duo go on to namedrop Oxford, Ipswich and Middlesbrough after stating privacy is "important to people everywhere" before plugging Firefox's stance on privacy.

‌



Wrexham previously aimed a jab at Southampton when the Championship fixtures were unveiled, saying "check training ground" along with an asterisk that added "for unauthorised visitors" for the September block to tie in with the fixture against Southampton.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

While Eckert is still waiting to discover his punishment for the scandal, it has seemingly not hampered Southampton's start to the new campaign, with the Saints quickly wiping out their four-point penalty. They sit ninth on 10 points after winning four of their seven games, scoring 18 goals in the process.

‌



Phil Parkinson, Wrexham's manager, insists his only focus is on getting a result with all the talk of last season's controversial season conclusion put to bed. "We're the team which obviously were affected because we were seventh, but we accepted the EFL decision on that," he said.

"Southampton got punished for it and they've had to accept their punishment and move on.

"That's all I can say on it really, it's gone. We're concentrating on what we've got to do and likewise they're the same."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney lands new job as BBC announce Man Utd legend's return
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney lands new job as BBC announce Man Utd legend's return

Wayne Rooney has been on everybody's screens as a pundit over the last year, but it now appears the Manchester United icon will be taking up a different challenge

View 4 Images Wayne Rooney will once again be a regular on the BBC (Image: BBC SPORT)

Manchester United icon Wayne Rooney will have his football knowledge put to the test in a new BBC show fronted by himself. The ex-England captain will be the protagonist of the new visualised podcast named 'Can You Beat Wayne Rooney?'

‌



It's the latest television project of the Three Lions' second highest goal-scorer, after he opened up his home to Disney's cameras for a new fly-on-the-wall documentary named 'The Real Rooneys'. Away from the streaming service, Rooney will be back with the tax-payer funded broadcaster for his latest project.

‌



He will face a new famous opponent every week in a test of football trivia with comedian Alex Brooker playing host on BBC Sport's Football YouTube channel and BBC iPlayer.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In a statement, the BBC summed up the new show by writing: "While guests will arrive convinced they can beat him, every question unlocks a story from Wayne's extraordinary journey through football, taking audiences behind the scenes of dressing rooms, title races, international tournaments and some of the sport's most iconic moments.

"Whether revisiting famous goals, legendary teammates or career-defining matches, Can You Beat Wayne Rooney? offers football fans a unique opportunity to hear the stories behind the headlines while watching Wayne's competitive side emerge as he tries to protect his reputation against a fresh challenger every week."

‌



This is not the first time he has had his own show with the Beeb, as he fronted 'The Rooney Show' but the last episode of the series aired on July 17th. It's also suggested the new show has been inspired by the time Erling Haaland challenged him to row across New York's Hudson River, after Rooney pledged to do so if Norway beat Brazil in the World Cup, which they went on to do 2-1.

4 View 4 Images Rooney rowed across the Hudson River in New York after Haaland scored twice against Brazil (Image: bbcsport/Instagram) 4 View 4 Images It appears the show was inspired by Rooney's wager with Haaland (Image: bbcsport/Instagram)

‌



Speaking about his latest television venture, Rooney also said: "Anyone who knows me knows I’m competitive, whether it’s on a football pitch, playing paddle or on a golf course and even rowing on the Hudson River.

"When Erling called me out to honour my challenge after Norway beat Brazil, there was no way I was backing out. That’s probably why I know I’m going to enjoy this series so much.

"We’ve evolved the podcast to lean into that competitive side of my personality, because I know that’s something the people love to see. Every guest will turn up thinking they can beat me and, honestly, I don’t like losing.

‌



View 4 Images Rooney had his own show on the BBC throughout the World Cup (Image: 2026 Xavier Laine)

"A single question can take you straight back to a dressing room, a match or a moment you haven’t thought about in years. We’ve got some great guests lined up, plenty of laughs and some fantastic football conversations."

Rooney has fully steered into television and punditry after enduring some difficult moments as a manager. He has not been in charge of a club since he left Plymouth Argyle in 2024, a short seven-month spell which proceeded a nightmare 83-day run as Birmingham City manager.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel's baffling World Cup regret that left England fans stunned
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel's baffling World Cup regret that left England fans stunned

Thomas Tuchel is now focusing on England's Nations League campaign, which begins with a visit from Spain on September 26

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel has one regret from the World Cup (Image: Ryan Pierse - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel regrets not eating grass from the pitch following England's win over Mexico at the World Cup. The Three Lions boss will select his Nations League squad on Friday after collecting a bronze medal in the summer.

‌



A 3-2 win against Mexico was one of England's most memorable results, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane both scoring to send Tuchel's men into the quarter-finals to face Norway.

‌



While reminiscing on the result, Tuchel has revealed that he wishes he tasted some of the pitch to keep the memory forever inside him. Speaking on the FA’s official website, the German manager said: "If you needed any proof of what it meant to these players and how they were with each other, it was the moment when Jordan (Henderson) fell over and broke his arm (after the final whistle).

‌



"Like within a second, every single player was there stopping the celebrations, building a shield, protecting Jordan, not going nowhere in full empathy. It was just so special.

"I texted a friend after the match and I just wrote that I regret that I didn’t eat some grass after the match to keep something (from the experience) in my body forever. That was the feeling. That was the moment."

Despite falling to Argentina in the semi-final, Tuchel believes the bond has now formed between himself and the players. Describing the potential success on the horizon, the 52-year-old explained: "There’s a huge bond to these players, it feels like they are my players now.

‌



"This is the beauty of it, when you have a manager and you have success and you have painful moments together. You have so much time together and you create a natural bond. I’m happy to see them, I’m happy to challenge them.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Tuchel wanted to eat some of the grass from the pitch (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



"I’m happy to push them and very proud to be a part of that. I’m excited to work with these players. I’m excited to have new young players that we can bring into camp and they can learn.

"I think we got another step closer and I think we’re there. It’s very difficult to prepare for a World Cup in the US. But I think it’s possible to prepare for a Euros.

"The target is to have another ten matches. We had ten matches in the US, eight wins, one draw, one painful loss. But that is something to build on. We have all the right to hold our heads high and go with courage and positivity into the next challenges."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Dominik Szoboszlai explains actions as star's dad makes Real Madrid claim
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Dominik Szoboszlai explains actions as star's dad makes Real Madrid claim

Today's Liverpool news sees star midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai issue a message

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister played against Spurs on Tuesday night (Image: 2026 Gaspafotos/MB Media)

Much has been made of Liverpool's midfield already this season. The Reds elected not to strengthen their engine room this summer and just one win in the Premier League from four games has thrust that decision back into the spotlight.

‌



Two of the central unit, Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister, have been ever-present this campaign. The Hungarian showed his quality again midweek with a stunning strike against Tottenham Hotspur in a 3-1 third-round Carabao Cup win.

‌



However, he has been criticised for his performances this season. Argentine Mac Allister looks to have returned to form this season after a dip last year. But he's been left to battle for his place in the first XI under Andoni Iraola.

‌



Today's latest sees Szoboszlai address his controversial celebration against Spurs. Elsewhere, Mac Allister's father has spoken out on reports that his son could be set to leave Anfield for Real Madrid in the near future.

Szoboszlai responds to critics

Liverpool vice-captain Szoboszlai has hit back at claims that his celebration against Spurs on Tuesday was in response to fans criticising him and the team after a goalless draw with Fulham last weekend.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Liverpool send clear message to Arsenal over 'genuine' plan to poach Rio Ngumoha READ MORE :

After hitting a sublime half volley, the midfielder pointed a finger towards his ear in a listening gesture. The Hungarian, part of a leadership group at Liverpool that includes Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez and Alisson Becker, however, refused to entertain that notion.

"No, [the celebration] was just for myself," Szoboszlai said post-match at Anfield on Tuesday evening. "No, I just decided before the game and I just did it.

View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai his back following his celebration against Spurs (Image: 2026 Simon Stacpoole/Offside)

‌



"Was there a criticism? I don’t know," he added. "I didn’t see [that] but thanks for telling me. You know this goal was for the people who are always next to me. Because we are also humans so we can have bad games, we can have bad days and I think never ever was a player who played every game of his life [well].

"So there will be days also and games where I am going to play badly, but I think the most important is the reaction so I think I reacted quite well today and hopefully I can keep on going on Sunday against Bournemouth."

Mac Allister's dad makes claim

Alexis Mac Allister's father, Carlos, has played down talk that the Liverpool midfielder could move to Real Madrid. The World Cup winner has been in strong form this season, despite being in and out of the team, and reiterated his importance with a goal against Spurs midweek

‌



Speaking before last week's 2-1 Champions League win over Atletico Madrid, Mac Allister, whose Anfield deal runs until 2028, confessed he was "very, very sad" that he was yet to be offered a new deal by the club.

The Liverpool star also explained that he had offers to leave Anfield this summer, amid speculation that Real were interested. Talk of a transfer to Los Blancos has been quashed by Carlos, who, in an interview with 365 Scores, said: "No-one from Real Madrid has contacted us at any point in the entire career of Alexis."

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister has openly commented about his Liverpool contract situation (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media, Getty Images)

‌



He added Liverpool have yet to ignite talks of a new contract with his son. "No-one from Liverpool's management has contacted us to renew his contract yet," Carlos said.

"We have a contract that is valid and we are committed to it with Liverpool, and if the club does not offer to renew the contract, it is their right. For now, Alexis has to give his best for the club in every game over the weekend.

"Alexis is not disappointed. This is a decision that the club makes, and we don't judge their decisions, we just prepare for what's to come."

Sports.title: Man Utd tried 11 things to convince JJ Gabriel to stay after bombshell exit announcement
Sports.content:
Manchester United were left stunned this week by the news JJ Gabriel wants to leave but they went to great lengths in an effort to keep him around. The 15-year-old now looks set to depart Old Trafford, though it remains to be seen whether he stays in England or heads overseas.

It has been claimed that United tried a number of different approaches as they sought to keep him around. Gabriel had looked set to make his senior debut against Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday but was left out of the squad after dropping that bombshell.

The Mail reports that Barcelona and Real Madrid are frontrunners for the teenager's signature. Gabriel is understood to have an EU passport, meaning he would be free to move clubs at the age of 16 - the age he will turn in October.

The same publication has pointed to some of the efforts made by the club to convince Gabriel his future should lie at Old Trafford. Here, we've got more of a rundown on the steps they took.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

1. Record-breaking opportunity

United were ready to hand Gabriel his senior debut at the age of just 15, breaking a youngest player record which has stood for 70 years. That record belongs to David Gaskell, who was 16 years and 19 days old when he made his first United appearance in October 1956 and went on to win two league titles.

Now, as the Mail notes, the youngster might be given a back seat at Under-21 level. Gabriel has scored twice in two Premier League 2 outings but didn't train on Monday or Tuesday amid the latest developments.

‌



2. Jason Wilcox and Matt Hargreaves intervened

This isn't the first time Gabriel has been linked with an exit. In the summer of 2025, director of football Jason Wilcox stepped in to convince the youngster to stick around.

View 4 Images Jason Wilcox has been credited with stopping Gabriel leaving even earlier (Image: Getty Images)

Matt Hargreaves, United's head of negotiations, was also involved in the intervention. It is believed he and Wilcox made it clear the teenager had a path to the first team.

3. Let him on the 2026 pre-season tour

That message from Wilcox and Hargreaves was emphasised when Michael Carrick included Gabriel in his squad for this summer's pre-season games. It was there that he got his first taste of men's football, featuring in a friendly against Atletico Madrid.

‌



However, those would be the only minutes he received under Carrick. He was also left out of United's 'A' list for the Champions League and is ineligible for the 'B' list, so was barred from featuring in Europe until the new year at the earlies.

4. Ruben Amorim watched footage of him

Carrick wasn't the first United boss to keep close tabs on the player. Ruben Amorim spent hours watching footage of him during United's pre-season tour to get a sense of what he was about.

Amorim left in January before having an opportunity to hand Gabriel a first-team opportunity. It is impossible to know whether things might be different had the Portuguese boss stuck around.

5. Dan Ashworth wanted to fast-track him

United's former sporting director Dan Ashworth was also an admirer of Gabriel. Indeed, the former Newcastle chief was keen on fast-tracking the wonderkid before leaving Old Trafford in late 2024.

‌



Interestingly, it was during Ashworth's time at Newcastle that the Magpies made Lewis Miley the sixth-youngest player in their history. The midfielder made 27 senior appearances before his 18th birthday, though it is unclear how big a part the sporting director played in his rise.

6. Meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson

View 4 Images Gabriel met Sir Alex Ferguson in December 2025 (Image: https://www.instagram.com/jjnr10/?hl=en)

Over the years, United have smoothed things over with young talents by allowing them to meet club legends. The approach has allowed the club to make the most of a storied history, where they remain the most decorated side in the Premier League era with 13 titles.

In December 2025, Gabriel met with iconic manager Sir Alex Ferguson. He spoke about the "honour" after being photographed with the two-time Champions League-winning boss.

‌



7. Let him have a relaxed schedule

Gabriel's schedule at Carrington wasn't what you'd expect for just any 15-year-old. The Mail reports that he was allowed to take multiple breaks during the season, something not always afforded to academy stars.

The treatment appeared to suit him well, with 26 goals last season a remarkable return. However, after taking trips to Spain last season, he could now be set to move there permanently.

8. Christopher Vivell made him feel important

United recruitment chief Christopher Vivell is another who has played a part in the efforts to make Gabriel feel special. The former Chelsea technical director is said to have aimed to make the youngster a focal point.

‌



If this was designed to show him the way forward, it appears not to have worked. Instead, a lack of minutes may have been a deciding factor despite all the efforts made elsewhere.

9. Heavy pre-season involvement

View 4 Images The teenager made his senior debut in a pre-season friendly (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

United went on a number of pre-season trips over the summer, playing friendlies in several different countries. Gabriel was involved in all but one of those, but only got eight minutes on the pitch against Atleti.

A number of other academy stars featured more in pre-season, including some who have since left Old Trafford. They include fellow forward Chido Obi, who is spending the season on loan at Dutch side Willem II.

‌



10. Carrick keeping close tabs

Michael Carrick has been on regular trips to Leigh Sports Village to watch Gabriel in action for United's age group teams. The manager was in the stands for a 5-0 win over Ipswich in August, where the youngster scored one goal and assisted two more.

Even so, Carrick urged patience when it came to a senior competitive debut. "We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy," he said. "It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really."

11. A regular in first-team training sessions

Carrick has invited Gabriel to train with the senior squad to give him a taste of what such a thing involves. Amorim did the same, saying: "If we can use every training we have to show the kids what they need to do to be here, it is important, not just for JJ but for everyone."

Arsenal prodigy Max Dowman trod a similar path before making his Premier League bow in August 2025. However, Gabriel's first taste of league football looks as though it will come away from Old Trafford.

‌

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Roy Keane gives honest verdict as out-of-work manager spotted at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Roy Keane gives honest verdict as out-of-work manager spotted at Old Trafford

Manchester United icon Roy Keane has shared his thoughts on a key issue as Michael Carrick's side look to bounce back from their Carabao Cup exit

View 2 Images Manchester United legend Roy Keane has given his verdict on an issue at the club (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Manchester United will look to return to winning ways as the team prepares for Premier League action this weekend. Michael Carrick will hope to see an immediate response from his side against Fulham on Sunday, with the club reeling from their Carabao Cup exit to Brighton.

‌



United appeared on course to sail into the next round after going 2-0 up in the opening 10 minutes against the Seagulls. However, Brighton successfully mounted a comeback to claim a 3-2 victory at Old Trafford, heaping pressure on Carrick’s position as manager.

‌



Teenage sensation JJ Gabriel was not named in United’s matchday squad for the cup tie following his request for the club to cancel his registration. The 15-year-old has made waves in United’s academy and looked to have a first team pathway, with club icon Roy Keane sharing his thoughts on Gabriel’s stance.

‌



Meanwhile, former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna, who was previously part of United’s coaching staff watched the recent Carabao Cup clash from the stands. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding United.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Roy Keane gives honest verdict

United legend Keane has urged Gabriel to be patient for his first-team debut. The 15-year-old, who featured for the club during pre-season, is yet to be named in a matchday squad so far this term, and Keane believes it is the wrong time for the youngster to be thrown into Carrick’s team.

‌



Giving his verdict on Gabriel’s situation, Keane said on the Stick to Football podcast: “Are you telling me he can’t wait? If you are 15 years of age and you’re talking about playing for Man United’s first team, just wait. Can you wait another six weeks if United get through the cup?

“Carrick’s under pressure. Obviously, [Sir Alex] Ferguson would throw young lads into the first team. But United, they need wins [right now].

“I don’t think United are in a position where they go, ‘We can write off a cup game tonight and play a couple of young lads. We need to get momentum into the season. If some 15-year-old is spitting his dummy out, we’ll deal with that.’”

‌



View 2 Images Kieran McKenna has been out of work since leaving Ipswich Town at the end of last season (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Out-of-work manager spotted at Old Trafford

Former Ipswich boss McKenna watched United’s plight in the Carabao Cup from the directors’ box at Old Trafford. The 40-year-old, who has been out of work since June, previously worked alongside Carrick as part of United’s coaching staff before beginning his managerial career with Ipswich in December 2021.

Article continues below

During his time in charge, McKenna’s side were twice promoted to the Premier League before choosing to leave this summer. United were previously linked with appointing the Northern Irishman as manager two years ago, but opted to extend Erik ten Hag’s contract.

Upon stepping down as Ipswich boss, McKenna said: “I now look forward to taking a break from management and dedicating some time to my family, who have been with me every step of my career so far.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
