For her part, the first lady, who was Special Guest of Honour, said the Tinubu government had been working to reposition the economy and establish foundations for sustainable national development.

She said, “Since the inception of this administration, Mr. President has worked tirelessly to reposition our economy and lay a solid foundation for sustainable national development.

“Nation-building is a continuous process, and the gains already recorded must be consolidated for the benefit of present and future generations.”

Mrs Tinubu also welcomed the forum’s endorsement of Tinubu for a second term, saying the support carries particular significance because it comes from former legislative leaders familiar with the demands of governance and the difficulties associated with major policy decisions.

She stated, “I especially acknowledge and appreciate your endorsement of President Bola Tinubu, for a second term in office. Coming from men and women who have themselves presided over legislative institutions, your endorsement carries special significance.

“You understand the demands of governance, the difficulty of making critical decisions, and the courage required to pursue reforms in the national interest.

“On behalf of Mr. President, I thank you for this expression of confidence, support and goodwill.”

The first lady also charged the former speakers and deputy speakers not to withdraw from public service simply because they had left elective office, saying the country still requires their institutional experience and networks.

“Leaving political office should never mean leaving public service. Nigeria still needs your wisdom, experience, and networks,” she said.

She urged them to use the forum to preserve institutional memory, mentor younger legislators, promote democratic stability, and continue contributing to development in communities where they had served.

Mrs Tinubu expressed hope that the summit would strengthen cooperation among members and create a platform for continued contributions to national unity and democratic development.

“May this Summit strengthen the bonds among you and open a new chapter of meaningful contribution to our nation, promote national unity and strengthen our democracy,” she said.

The former Speakers and Deputy Speakers of Houses of Assembly also unanimously endorsed Tinubu for a second term and resolved to launch a nationwide grassroots mobilisation for his re-election in 2027.

To this end, members of Forum of Former Presiding Officers of State Houses of Assembly of Nigeria (FOPSHAN) promised to mobilise across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), explaining the administration’s policies and programmes and canvassing support for the president.

The ex-legislative leaders also endorsed the administration’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy, stating that the immediate difficulties associated with the measures should be weighed against their anticipated long-term benefits.

The resolutions were adopted at FOPSHAN’s National Summit in Abuja, with former Senate President, Senator Anyim Pius Anyim, chairing the session, while the forum’s national chairman, Senator Wasiu Eshilokun Sani, hosted the gathering.

According to its resolutions, the forum declared its support for what it described as the administration’s “bold economic reforms”, particularly petrol subsidy removal, saying the policy should be viewed within the broader objective of securing long-term economic prosperity.

It thereafter announced a unanimous endorsement of Tinubu’s second-term bid.

It stated, “In recognition of the president’s colourful, visionary leadership and commitment to national development, FOPSHAN unanimously endorses President Bola Tinubu, for a second term in office in the 2027 general elections.”

The forum resolved to move beyond the endorsement by deploying its membership across the country to build grassroots support for the administration.

On party affairs, the forum reaffirmed its commitment to the unity and progress of All Progressives Congress (APC), urging members to close ranks and support the administration at the federal and sub-national levels.

World.title: Liverpool player set for Zimbabwe debut in AFCON qualifiers
World.content:
Liverpool and Zimbabwe defender Isaac Mabaya. Image: This Is Anfield

A Liverpool player could make his Zimbabwe debut when the Warriors begin their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign against Sierra Leone next week.

Isaac Mabaya has been included in Ramón Catalá’s final Warriors squad for the opening qualifiers, giving the 21-year-old an opportunity to make his senior international debut for Zimbabwe.

Zimbabwe face Sierra Leone away on 24 September before hosting the Democratic Republic of Congo in Harare four days later.



From Liverpool’s academy to the Warriors

Mabaya was born in Preston, England, to Zimbabwean parents and joined Liverpool’s academy when he was just six years old.

The right-back progressed through the club’s youth system and signed his first professional contract with Liverpool in 2021.

Interestingly, he did not begin his career as a defender.



Liverpool said Mabaya was initially deployed as a wide midfielder before being moved to full-back, where his ability to attack from the position became one of his notable qualities.

That versatility has remained an important part of his development.

Mabaya has already played for Liverpool’s first team

Although the upcoming match could be his Zimbabwe debut, Mabaya has already made a senior appearance for Liverpool.



He came off the bench against Plymouth Argyle in the FA Cup in February 2025 after Joe Gomez suffered an injury.

His senior experience at club level remains limited, but his progression through one of England’s biggest football academies has kept him on the radar.

According to This Is Anfield, the attacking full-back is registered in Liverpool’s Premier League and Champions League squads because he qualifies as both homegrown and club-trained.



Mabaya also featured prominently around Liverpool’s first-team environment during his development and appeared for the club during pre-season.

The Liverpool man previously represented England

Mabaya’s international career has also included England youth teams.

He represented England at Under-15, Under-16, Under-18 and Under-19 level, making him one of several players with the option of representing Zimbabwe despite being born in England.



His decision to play senior international football for Zimbabwe now gives Catalá another option at right-back.

Liverpool’s academy profile describes Mabaya as a player who can operate from full-back after his positional switch from midfield.

Zimbabwe’s AFCON qualifiers

The Warriors will begin their 2027 AFCON qualifying campaign against Sierra Leone on 24 September.



They will then return home to face the Democratic Republic of Congo at the National Sports Stadium on 28 September.

Mabaya has been named among the defenders in Catalá’s 23-man squad for the two matches.

For the Liverpool youngster, the fixtures could mark the beginning of a new chapter in his career.

World.title: El Niño broke a record by doing… nothing
World.content:
El Niño is intensifying toward what forecasters now call a genuinely historic strength, and one of its strangest effects has nothing to do with a storm at all.

Through 10 September 2026, normally the peak of the Atlantic hurricane season, not a single Atlantic hurricane had formed this year, marking the latest season start since satellite tracking began in the 1960s.

WHAT’S ACTUALLY DRIVING THE SILENCE

Why has the Atlantic gone quiet?



El Niño typically increases wind shear over the Atlantic basin, tearing apart storms before they can properly form.

Where the opposite is happening is the Pacific.

The 2026 Pacific hurricane season has been hyperactive instead, with named storms in the northeastern Pacific running roughly 40% above average for this time of year.



Who is confirming just how strong this El Niño has become?

NOAA’s Climate Prediction Center.

On 14 September, the Niño 3.4 Relative Oceanic Niño Index reached 2.0°C above average, the official threshold for a “very strong” event.



The Niño 1+2 region off north-western South America, which typically warms first, was already running 3.7°C above average in the same period.

WHY THIS EVENT KEEPS BREAKING RECORDS

When did forecasters start taking this seriously?

The World Meteorological Organization has described the event as “supersizing before our eyes,” projecting it could become the strongest El Niño on record.



The Washington Post reports water temperatures are projected to peak around 4.1°C above average in December, roughly a full degree hotter than the previous record set during the 2015 El Niño.

How confident are forecasters that this continues?

The WMO now puts the likelihood of El Niño persisting through February 2027 at nearly 100%, the first time a WMO update has been this unequivocal.



NOAA separately estimates a greater than 90% chance the event stays “very strong” through the Northern Hemisphere’s fall and winter.

WHAT THE IMPACTS ALREADY LOOK LIKE

Where has El Niño already caused real damage?

Panama has been hit hard, with torrential rain and severe flooding affecting more than 15,600 people in its Caribbean and northern regions.



At the same time, a rainfall deficit in Panama’s central and metropolitan areas has caused water stress across eleven watersheds.

Globally, the UN’s World Food Programme has separately warned that nearly 50 million more people in vulnerable communities could be pushed into acute hunger because of the strengthening pattern.

I find this quiet-Atlantic detail genuinely fascinating.



It’s a reminder that a single climate pattern can produce wildly different, almost contradictory effects depending entirely on where you’re standing.

Have you noticed any unusual weather patterns where you live this year?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: Cyril Ramaphosa was NOT poisoned at BRICS Summit in India
World.content:
India’s Ministry of External Affairs has dismissed claims that Cyril Ramaphosa became ill after attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. Image: File

India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has dismissed viral claims that South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other world leaders became ill after attending the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

The ministry’s fact-checking unit labelled the claims misleading and warned social media users against what it described as malicious posts.

The BRICS Summit was held in New Delhi on 12 and 13 September under the theme Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.



The summit concluded with the adoption of the New Delhi Declaration.

Fake Alert!!! 🚨🚨🚨



We caution against such malicious posts on social media platforms! pic.twitter.com/NRu6Dfk7Yj — MEA FactCheck (@MEAFactCheck) September 17, 2026

Cyril Ramaphosa illness fuels online rumours

The claims gained traction after Ramaphosa’s office confirmed that the South African president had been booked off from public engagements.



He was advised by his doctors to rest and recover, although his office did not disclose the nature of his illness.

Social media posts subsequently attempted to link Ramaphosa’s health to an alleged food poisoning incident at the BRICS summit.

However, India’s MEA has rejected the suggestion that world leaders fell ill because of food served at the event.



The ministry’s fact-checking account on X directly addressed the claims, describing them as misleading and urging people to be cautious of unverified information circulating online.

Claims about Xi also dismissed

Separate social media claims suggested that Xi had fainted or had left India early because of health concerns.

Those claims are also disputed by available information.



Xi attended the second session of the BRICS Summit alongside Cyril Ramaphosa and other leaders on 13 September, before completing his scheduled engagements.

There has been no verified evidence presented linking Xi’s health, or Ramaphosa’s subsequent medical leave, to food served at the summit.

The New Delhi meeting brought together leaders of the BRICS grouping as discussions focused on cooperation, economic development, resilience and other international issues.



Officials urge caution over social media claims

The latest rumours highlight how quickly unverified claims can spread when they involve prominent political figures.

In this case, Ramaphosa’s confirmed absence from public engagements was used online as the basis for claims about an alleged mass food-poisoning incident.

India’s MEA has now publicly rejected that narrative.

World.title: Rejected Afrikaner refugee applicants reveal criminal convictions
World.content:
Refugee applicants have shared why they were rejected. Image via Canva

Several Afrikaner refugee applicants have shared the criminal charges that have led to them being rejected from the resettlement programme.

This comes amid an increase in the number of applicants who have received ineligibility letters.

To date, figures have revealed that over 13 000 ethnic minorities, predominantly white South Africans, have resettled under the US under the President Donald Trump administration.



The programme is open to South Africans who face “racial persecution” or a fear of future persecution to apply for resettlement in the United States.

AFRIKANER REFUGEES ON WHY THEY WERE TURNED DOWN

Speaking to The Guardian this week, several refugee applicants shed light on why they were rejected from the resettlement programme.

The applicants, mostly Afrikaner people who spoke on condition of anonymity, said they were distraught after receiving their eligibility letters. Some of them had packed up and sold off their belongings in South Africa and were now faced with “starting over”.

A man in his 60s told the publication that he was rejected as his partner, whom he had jointly applied to the programme with, had a marijuana conviction brought up. The couple had completed the screening process last year and received a rejection letter in June.

He said, “I cried like a baby. It was something I actually believed was attainable. I believed the hype.”

Another couple shared that they had sold all their possessions when they received a rejection letter in July. The husband shared that he had been convicted of trespassing in 2014, for which he had paid a fine and did not go to court. Despite this, he was granted multiple temporary visas to work on farms in the US between 2011 and 2024.



Another man, also in his 60s, admitted to shooting a black person in his job as a security personnel in 1995. The man claimed that he had been investigated by authorities and was not charged, as he was found to have acted in self-defence.

The man applied for a Freedom of Information (FOI) request, and was notified that the reasons behind his rejection were “crime involving moral turpitude” and “commission of acts of torture or extrajudicial killing”.

CAN REJECTION LETTERS BE APPEALED?

Applications have been rejected, and some individuals have had their status revoked for the following reasons:

The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) can revoke applications based on the following:

Fraud and misrepresentation

Ineligibility

Security and terrorism concerns

Criminal history

The UCIS has stated that it is under no obligation to grant an appeal to a rejected refugee applicant.

However, in rare cases, the application may be reviewed if evidence is missing or a factual error is found. This is entirely discretionary.

‘DO NOT MISLEAD OR LIE’

According to US YouTuber and intel expert Chris Wyatt, many cases of rejection stemmed from applicants who had not been forthcoming about their past during the screening process.

He said in a video: “I’ll tell you why people are getting denied. Criminal activity, criminal convictions, lying to investigators, and drug offences and drug use.

“Over the past year, I’ve repeatedly said that an act of omission is an act of commission. Do not mislead or lie”

Wyatt explained that this also applied to those who intentionally failed to disclose expunged crimes from their past.

“You’re a liar in their eyes. Expunged doesn’t mean that the record is gone. It just means that you don’t have a personal criminal record. It doesn’t mean the government doesn’t retain records of it. They consider that a lie. You’ve made yourself ineligible”.

World.title: Confirmed: Former Kaizer Chiefs midfielder joins Stellenbosch again
World.content:
Matsheke previously represented the Stellenbosch FC during the 2023/24 season. He was part of the squad that lifted the Carling Knockout trophy.

The midfielder played a key role in the final against TS Galaxy. He scored the winning penalty as the Maroons secured the trophy after a penalty shootout.

Matsheke made 12 appearances across all competitions during his first spell in the Winelands.



MATSHEKE’S JOURNEY BACK TO STELLENBOSCH

Born in Chiawelo, Soweto, Matsheke began his professional breakthrough within the youth structures of Kaizer Chiefs. He was promoted to the senior team during the 2020/21 season.

The midfielder then spent loan spells with Uthongathi FC and Moroka Swallows to gain more competitive experience. After leaving Kaizer Chiefs permanently, Matsheke joined Stellenbosch FC on a free transfer in October 2023.

His first spell at the club proved memorable on the pitch. He helped Stellenbosch FC win the 2023 Carling Knockout trophy after scoring the decisive penalty against TS Galaxy in the final shootout.



However, his time at the club ended abruptly in March 2024. Stellenbosch FC terminated his contract following an internal code of conduct transgression.

Matsheke subsequently moved through spells with Pretoria Callies and Kruger United before returning to top-flight football with Marumo Gallants during the 2025/26 season.

His stay at Marumo Gallants was short-lived. The midfielder eventually parted ways with the club by mutual agreement after falling out of the head coach’s long-term plans.



Now back at Stellenbosch FC, Matsheke has another opportunity to revive his career at the highest level of South African football.

MATSHEKE TARGETS MORE SUCCESS

Matsheke admitted that his return to Stellenbosch FC came as a surprise, but said he was delighted to be back. “It feels great to be back at Stellenbosch FC,” Matsheke said. “It was unexpected, but I am really happy to be here.”

The midfielder thanked the club and coach for giving him another opportunity. “I want to pick up where I left off on the field and help the team compete for more,” he added.



“I missed out on the opportunity to play in Africa last time, so there’s a bit of unfinished business, but this is a second chance for me to do more and achieve those goals.”

Matsheke will wear the No. 31 jersey during the new season. The midfielder could make his second Stellenbosch FC debut this weekend. The Maroons are scheduled to face Kruger United in the Betway Premiership.

World.title: Richards Bay appointing Africa’s most wanted nomadic tactician
World.content:
Local football reports indicate that Richards Bay have reached an agreement with Pantev. The remaining details are reportedly being finalised before the coach travels to South Africa to take charge of the Natal Rich Boys.

The Natal Rich Boyz are searching for a new coach following the resignation of Ronnie Gabriel. His departure came after a difficult run of results, which included a heavy 5-1 defeat.

Pantev could now be handed the responsibility of turning around Richards Bay’s fortunes in the Betway Premiership.



PANTEV BRINGS AFRICAN EXPERIENCE

The reported move would see the club bring in a coach with considerable experience outside his native Bulgaria. Pantev has worked in Europe and across several African leagues during his managerial career.

The 50-year-old coach has also built a reputation for winning league titles in Africa.

Pantev first made his name in Bulgaria, where he spent a significant part of his early coaching career in futsal. He guided Grand Pro Varna to five consecutive Bulgarian futsal league titles between 2011 and 2016.

He also had a spell with the Bulgaria national futsal team before eventually moving into 11-a-side football.

His coaching career later took him to Palestine before he moved to Africa. Pantev joined Victoria United in Cameroon and guided the club to the 2023/24 Elite One title, the first top-flight championship in the club’s history.

The Bulgarian then moved to Botswana, where he coached Orapa United before taking charge of Gaborone United. His time at Gaborone United proved particularly successful. Pantev guided the club to the 2024/25 Botswana Premier League title.



That success earned him a move to Tanzanian giants Simba SC in October 2025. However, his time at the club was brief before the two parties parted ways.

Pantev has since continued his coaching career in Africa. His reported move to Richards Bay would now bring him to the South African top flight for the first time.

The club will hope his experience of working in different African leagues can help stabilise the team and improve their results.

World.title: RIP: Motorsport South Africa mourn tragic death of Robert Wolk
World.content:
Robert Wolk, the 41-year-old touring car driver was killed in an alleged road-rage incident on Wednesday evening, 16 September, while traveling to OR Tambo International Airport.

According to South African Police Service spokesperson Colonel Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi, the incident occurred at the intersection of Camwood Street and Portland Drive in Kempton Park.

Wolk was en route to catch a flight to Cape Town for an upcoming race weekend when he was involved in a reportedly minor traffic accident.



Emergency services pronounced him dead at the scene beside his Audi after he was shot at point blank range in a shocking incident at the scene of the accident.

Wolk was a dominant force on local circuits, renowned for his remarkable skill in the Global Touring Cars (GTC) series and his back-to-back victories at the prestigious Simola Hillclimb in Knysna.

Police have opened a murder investigation, though no arrests have been made as authorities continue searching for suspect details.

Tributes pour in for Robert Wolk

Motorsport South Africa and fans across the country have expressed profound shock and grief, remembering him as a fierce competitor and a beloved ambassador for the sport.

“Motorsport South Africa is deeply saddened by the tragic passing of Robert Wolk,” a statement read.

“Robert was a hugely respected figure in South African motorsport, with a career spanning almost three decades and success across karting, single-seaters, touring cars and other forms of circuit racing.



“His list of achievements is extensive, including SA Junior GP Karting Championship titles in 1995 and 1997, multiple Formula Ford championships, the 2013 SA Formula Volkswagen Championship, the 2015 SA Formula 1600 Championship, the 2021 and 2022 SA GTC Championships and the 2024 SA Touring Cars Championship.

“He was awarded South African Junior Protea Colours in 1998 and later received his Senior Protea Colours in 2022.

“Robert continued to add to that remarkable career in 2026. In May, he won his second Simola Hillclimb King of the Hill title, and in June he returned to South African Touring Cars with a victory at Aldo Scribante.

“Robert’s passion for racing remained clear right to the end. He was still competing at national level and was due to race at Killarney this weekend.

“His passing leaves a profound void in South African motorsport. Robert will be remembered not only for the championships and victories he achieved, but for the passion, commitment and sportsmanship he brought to the sport throughout his career.

“Our thoughts are with Robert’s family, friends, team members, colleagues and everyone across the motorsport community who knew him.

“Rest in peace, Robert Wolk.”

Shocking incident

Initial reports indicate the conflict began after a minor vehicle collision at the corner of Camwood Street and Portland Drive in Esther Park.

Wolk reportedly pulled over in his Audi, apparently to exchange insurance information and to inspect the damage. An argument is said to have broken out between the drivers, during which Wolk attempted to disengage and leave the scene.

Video footage circulating on social media shows Wolk pleading with the gunman before turning to walk back toward his vehicle, at which point he was shot in the back. The shooter is seen retrieving an item from the ground before fleeing in the vehicle.

SAPS continues to appeal to anyone who may have witnessed the collision or the surrounding movement of vehicles in Esther Park on Wednesday evening to contact local authorities or Crime Stop.

World.title: Body of MAN discovered north of Johannesburg
World.content:
Police in Gauteng have opened a murder investigation after the body of a man was discovered in Victory Park in Linden, north of Johannesburg. Image: Wikimedia Commons

Police in Gauteng have opened a murder investigation after the body of a man was discovered in Victory Park in Linden, north of Johannesburg.

The body was found on Thursday with visible injuries, according to police.

READ | Kempton Park serial killer? Profiler weighs in on Ekurhuleni killings



Circumstances unknown

Gauteng police spokesperson Colonel Dimakatso Nevhuhulwi said the circumstances surrounding the man’s death remain unknown at this stage.

“The body had visible injuries, and the circumstances surrounding the incident are unknown at this stage, pending police investigations,” Nevhuhulwi said.

Police have not yet released the identity of the deceased or provided details about how he died.

Police appeal for information

Investigators are now working to establish the circumstances leading to the man’s death and are appealing to members of the public who may have information to come forward.

Police urged anyone with information that could assist with the investigation to contact Crime Stop on 08600 10 111.

Anonymous information can also be submitted through the MySAPS application.



“Police investigations continue,” Nevhuhulwi said.

World.title: Police launch manhunt after two EC cops killed
World.content:
MTHATHA - Police have launched a manhunt after two Eastern Cape police officers were killed in Libode, near Mthatha, in the early hours of Friday morning.

The officers, aged 30 and 52, were from the Mthatha National Intervention Unit and the Mthatha Public Order Policing Unit. They were responding to reports of an attack on a spaza shop when they came under fire.

READ | Three EC police officers killed in shooting

It is alleged that armed suspects were attacking the shop and demanding money from the operator. The officers responded to a call for assistance and were later found with gunshot wounds.

Their service pistols were also reported missing.

Police are investigating two counts of murder, two counts of attack on police, two counts of robbery of police firearms and one count of attempted business robbery.

World.title: UPDATE: Zolani Tete murder accused denied bail
World.content:
MDANTSANE - Two men alleged to have played key roles as the mastermind and middleman in the murder of former boxing world champion Zolani Tete have been denied bail.

Uzozole Goqwana and Sinebongo Qase appeared in the Mdantsane Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where their bail applications were denied.

READ | Zolani Tete family chooses forgiveness as accused killers await bail ruling

The pair are among four men facing eight charges linked to Tete’s murder. The two men accused of carrying out the shooting have already abandoned their bail applications.

Tete was gunned down outside his home in Mdantsane last month. Another person was wounded in the shooting.

World.title: Australian athlete who soiled herself apologises for continuing Hyrox race
World.content:
BEIJING - An Australian athlete who sparked an outcry when she kept competing despite soiling herself midway through an event in Beijing apologised Friday and forfeited her points from winning.

Joanna Wietrzyk finished the Hyrox indoor fitness race last weekend with excrement on her legs and shoes, continuing to use the mats and equipment.

It sparked backlash about potential health hazards posed to other competitors and went viral on social media.

"I want to offer my sincere apology to the people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the Hyrox organisers for what happened during the race in Beijing," Wietrzyk said on Instagram.

"I felt completely fit and healthy at the start of the race, with no reason to expect any illness.

"Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track. I recognise that I should have made a different choice."

The 23-year-old world record holder said she had retroactively withdrawn from the race and would hand back the points earned from competing.

"I am learning from this experience and will carry those lessons with me, including remembering that there is more to life than racing and knowing when it is right to step away," she added.

"I will be taking some time to recover, reflect and look after myself and my family away from the noise."

Hyrox, a popular fitness competition launched in Germany and held worldwide, features a mixture of treadmill running and strength exercises, such as lunges and rowing.

Co-founder Moritz Furste apologised on Monday to "all who were directly or indirectly involved" as intense criticism swelled over its health and safety standards.

"Hyrox made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race," added Furste. "In the end it is my job to foresee these potential incidents, and I did not."

It has since updated its rules.

They now state that if a "racer's blood, vomit, urine, or faeces poses a welfare or contamination risk to the racer or to other racers, a race director may withdraw the racer from the race on medical grounds".

World.title: Princess Diana's brother makes new explosive claims against Charles
World.content:
LONDON - Princess Diana's brother has unleashed a string of criticism against King Charles III in his new book, alleging the monarch was "giddily elated" the night his ex-wife died in a car crash, as Buckingham Palace issued a rare rebuke of the startling claims.

Charles Spencer wrote that the then-prince "sounded giddily elated, like a lottery winner" on the night Diana died three decades ago, in the latest extract of his book published by the Daily Mail on Thursday.

In another extract released earlier, Spencer claims that days after her death, the future king told him: "Rest assured, we'll forget her soon enough."

Buckingham Palace took the unusual step of strongly pushing back against the allegations earlier Thursday, with UK newspapers splashing the war of words between Spencer and the king, who was married to Diana for 15 years.

"His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgement and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss," a palace spokesperson said, adding that they do not normally comment on books.

Spencer's book, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister and set to be published next week, is being serialised in the Daily Mail.

In the latest extracts, Spencer claims, "there were others in the Palace, I already knew, who were relieved, indeed, pleased, that she had gone".

He also alleges Charles subjected him to a "stream of anger" after he insisted Diana would not have wanted her sons, princes William and Harry, then aged 15 and 12, to walk in her funeral procession.

World.title: Ekurhuleni murders | Technology a welcomed ally in search for perpetrators - Analyst
World.content:
Editor's Note: Please note that the following interview may contain graphic visuals and content.

JOHANNESBURG - The Gauteng Premier has praised the province's investment into technology and cameras in fighting crime.

Footage is being analysed to help trace perpetrators in the deaths of nine women in the East Rand over two months.

A ninth body of a woman was discovered in Dawn Park in Boksburg naked and covered in a sheet on Thursday.

Prof Dee Khosa from Unisa's School of Criminal Justice says CCTV footage has an important role to play in the case.

"While most of the women appear to have been killed somewhere and dumped elsewhere, the footage will likely show vehicles and movements," she says.

This means license plate recognition, footage from the roads leading to the various sites, cross-checked with cellphone records could go far in the cases.

"Cameras only deter where people believe someone is actually watching," says Khosa.

In the wake of the various bodies of semi-naked women found across the Ekurhuleni, police have increased their visibility.

Khosa says such visibility will only deter offenders in that particular area.

"It cannot be a main strategy for crimes that happen in isolated spaces away from patrolled roads, for instance," she says.

Municipalities need to come to the party of crime fighting by fixing street lights, cut overgrown fields and secure abandoned sites including construction sites.

Khosa calls on the police to treat reports of missing women as urgent in the first hour.

World.title: Russians begin voting in controlled election as war drags on
World.content:
MOSCOW - Polling stations opened early Friday in Russia's Far East, kicking off a three-day election that President Vladimir Putin's party is all but guaranteed to win in the fifth year of war with Ukraine.

It will be Russia's first parliamentary election since Moscow sent troops to Ukraine in February 2022. The conflict has since killed hundreds of thousands.

Only parties that support Putin and the Kremlin's dragging military campaign have been registered to run. Moscow has also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.

While few in Russia doubt Putin's United Russia party will sail to victory again, the vote is an opportunity for the Kremlin to gauge public support for the Ukraine war, the effects of which have hit home more than ever this year.

In a grim reminder of the fighting, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said on Friday that Russia destroyed dozens of Ukrainian drones bound for the capital overnight.

"More than 350 UAVs flew towards the Moscow region between 8:00 pm (1700 GMT) on 17 September and 7:00 am on 18 September," he said on Telegram, adding that most were destroyed at an outer defensive perimeter and some 64 were shot down as they were approaching the sprawling city.

The vote to renew the 450 seats in the Duma, Russia's lower house of parliament, will run until 1800 GMT on Sunday.

Russia's Kamchatka peninsula and Chukotka, on the Pacific, are the first of Russia's 11 time zones to begin voting.

Putin has ruled Russia since New Year's Eve 1999, and his United Russia party has dominated Russian politics since the early 2000s.

Moscow has banned criticism of its Ukraine campaign and the Russian elections, tightly controlled by the Kremlin, are bringing few surprises.

- 'Emotionally important to Putin' -

United Russia is only facing parties who back most of Putin's policies and the war in Ukraine: the Communist Party, the nationalist LDPR, A Just Russia and New People.

Yabloko, which called for an end to fighting, was barred from running shortly before the vote. One of its main figures, Lev Shlosberg, was imprisoned for criticising the war.

World.title: Ekurhuleni deaths highlight policing failures, says activist Saths Cooper
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A week of despair in Ekurhuleni has renewed concerns about safety, policing and the state of the country's criminal justice system.

The discovery of nine bodies in the Ekurhuleni metro has left communities grappling with fear and grief.

Anti-apartheid activist and clinical psychologist Professor Saths Cooper says the killings are evidence of deeper problems within the country’s democracy and criminal justice system.

“We have a failure in our democracy to make our streets and our communities safe because of the sheer lack of visible policing, the sheer lack of caring and intentionality to preclude this kind of event.”

Cooper says the killings highlight what he describes as a breakdown in the criminal justice system, particularly within the police service.

He argues that communities are being left vulnerable when there is not enough visible policing or effective intervention to prevent violent crime.

“It just declares the entire society in terms of criminal justice vulnerable. It shows us that there's a breakdown from the top in the criminal justice system and particularly the police.”

Cooper also questioned whether promises from authorities can provide reassurance to communities that have already experienced repeated violence.

He says statements made after murders occur can feel inadequate to families and communities who want to know why preventative measures were not taken earlier.

“How are you going to protect us now?”

For Cooper, the deaths in Ekurhuleni should serve as a serious warning to leaders at both national and local government levels.

“This is a serious wake-up call to our leadership at national and local levels that we are failing our population because all the indices show that this country is one of the most violent without war.”

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Madlanga probes capture of public service
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Madlanga Commission is continuing its probe into the alleged capture of the public sector.

The inquiry is expected to hear from Public Service Commission Chairperson Somadoda Fikeni.

The Public Service Commission is responsible for monitoring and investigating public administration to promote ethical, efficient and accountable governance.

READ | Madlanga Commission hears how prison gangs link to crime outside

Meanwhile, the inquiry has also heard testimony about the growing influence of gangs inside correctional facilities.

Correctional Services National Commissioner Makgothi Thobakgale testified about prison operations and how gangs have allegedly turned some prisons into hubs for recruiting and training inmates to become future gang leaders.

World.title: From 55bob contribution to presidential bid: Why Sifuna has been sued

World.title: Ruto faults Uhuru for undermining his government
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto join traditional dancers in Homa Bay on September 17, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has renewed his public criticism of former President Uhuru Kenyatta, accusing his predecessor of undermining the government and urging him to withdraw from active political mobilisation.

Ruto said he had supported Uhuru throughout their political partnership and expected reciprocal support when he sought the presidency.

“I stood by you through four elections; I stood by you, helped you, took care of you, and worked for you.”

Ruto claimed the two had discussed an arrangement in which each would serve as president for ten years. He accused Uhuru of failing to honour that understanding, saying:

“When the time came for you to help me, after you said ‘ten years for you, ten years for me,’ not even for a single day did you support me.”

Ruto also appealed to Uhuru to respect the position of former President and withdraw from political activities that he said were aimed at destabilising his administration.

“A former president! Surely, my brother, you are lowering the dignity of the office of the former president. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” Ruto said.

Ruto made the remarks on Thursday, September 17, 2026, in Sindo, Homa Bay County, as he concluded a four-day development tour of Nyanza.

The tour covered Kisumu, Siaya, Migori and Homa Bay and focused largely on roads, markets, housing, water and other development projects. The Star+1

The latest confrontation adds another chapter to the complicated political relationship between the two leaders.

Ruto served as Uhuru's deputy from 2013 to 2022, after the two politicians formed a political alliance that won the 2013 and 2017 presidential elections.

Contemporary accounts describe their original arrangement as involving support for Kenyatta for two terms, followed by support for Ruto's presidential ambitions. The Washington Post

The President nevertheless acknowledged Uhuru's democratic right to oppose his government but urged the former president to respect the office he once held.

“You are running schemes to sabotage the government. You are a retired president respect your office, go and relax. Let us plan for this country of ours, Kenya,” he said.

His criticism centred instead on what he described as continued political mobilisation against his administration.

He said his administration had stabilised the economy and pointed to investments in education, housing, markets and infrastructure. During the Homa Bay leg alone, the government highlighted a Sh3.5 billion plan for 21 modern markets.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: Egypt bans social media accounts for under-13s and mandates “safe mode” for ages 13-15
World.content:
Egyptian authorities declared a major digital crackdown on Thursday, barring children under the age of 13 from holding independent social media accounts and slapping strict mandatory restrictions on users under 15.

In a joint decree issued by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation (SCMR) and the National Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (NTRA), social media platforms operate under a tough new mandate designed to shield children and young teenagers from digital risks. Under the newly unveiled regulations, platforms are strictly forbidden from allowing children under 13 to create or activate independent personal accounts.

For young teens aged 13 to under 15, personal accounts will still be permitted—but with a heavy catch. Platforms must automatically and mandatorily activate “Safe Mode” on these accounts, and the setting cannot be unilaterally disabled by the underage user as long as they remain in that age bracket.

To ensure the rules are not easily skirted, the decree compels tech platforms to deploy effective age-verification protocols and actively prevent users from manipulating age boundaries. Companies must audit existing accounts and take immediate action against any profile confirmed or suspected to belong to a user under 15. However, a formal appeals process must be provided to correct any legitimate age-verification errors.

Officials frame the sweeping measures as a direct response to directives from President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi aimed at safeguarding youth from the dangers of social media misuse and forging a safer online ecosystem.

Underscoring the broader vision, Khaled Abdel Aziz, Chairman of the SCMR, emphasized that digital child safety has become “a shared responsibility between the state, the family, society, and digital platforms.” He insisted that the objective is not to strip technology away from children, but rather to guarantee its safe, responsible, and age-appropriate use.

Echoing this stance, NTRA Chief Executive Mohamed Shamroukh explained that the framework operates on the principle of “age- and risk-proportionate protection,” delivering varying tiers of security based on a user’s developmental age and exposure to online hazards.

Tech firms have been put on a strict clock: platforms must bring their operations into full compliance within three months of the decree taking effect, and must submit a comprehensive operational blueprint and technical timeline detailing their execution strategy within the next 30 days.

World.title: Sisi warns against mounting conspiracy to destabilize Egypt
World.content:
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi warned Thursday that persistent schemes to destabilize the state remain an ongoing threat, declaring that the unrest witnessed between 2011 and 2013 “has not ended” and that underlying plots “have not stopped.”

Speaking during an address at the Egyptian Military Academy, President Sisi emphasized that while methods may evolve, the push to dismantle the state persists, underscoring public awareness as the nation’s primary defense against continuous challenges.

Reflecting on regional volatility, Sisi noted that while several neighboring nations suffered catastrophic destabilization during that period, Egypt miraculously survived.

He described the nation’s survival as a divine blessing, asserting that events across the region were systematically orchestrated and planned, imposing a heavy responsibility on Egypt to safeguard its stability—particularly given its finite national resources.

The President stressed that protecting the state is a collective civic duty rather than a mandate tied to any single authority or leadership figure. Framing national preservation around the institution of the presidency, he cautioned, distorts the true purpose of state resilience, which rests on the joint responsibility of the government, institutions, and the Egyptian public.

World.title: Egypt to witness gradual drop in temperatures over next few days
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority announced a noticeable shift in the weather across Egypt, as the country experiences a gradual drop in temperatures ranging between 3 to 5 degrees Celsius in most areas, starting Friday, and continuing through next Tuesday.

This drop comes after a heatwave that swept the country over the past few days, bringing temperatures back to seasonal averages for this time of year.

Moderate to warm and humid weather will prevail in the early morning, turning hot and humid during the day across the north of the country down to Greater Cairo and North Upper Egypt, while remaining extremely hot in South Upper Egypt.

Maximum temperatures in Greater Cairo and the Nile Delta are expected to reach around 33°C on Friday, dropping to 32°C on Saturday and Sunday, while in South Upper Egypt, temperatures will decrease from 43°C down to 39°C by the beginning of next week.

Meteorologists warned of dense morning fog forming at times between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM on roads to and from northern Egypt, Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, and Central Sinai.

There are also chances of light to occasionally moderate rain over parts of the northern coasts and the northern Nile Delta. Winds will pick up across most areas at speeds between 30 and 40 km/h, helping to cool the atmosphere, with a chance of kicking up sand and dust in parts of the Western Desert.

World.title: New Princess Diana documentary featuring confidential audio tapes
World.content:
Nearly three decades after her death, Princess Diana remains a compelling subject for arts and literature, most recently featuring in the new three-part documentary series “Diana Unheard”, which presents previously unreleased audio recordings of the late royal.

Global rights to the three-part series have been acquired by Cineflix Rights from the independent British production company Love Monday TV, known for producing royal programs for ITV and Channel 5.

The series features “the People’s Princess” reflecting on her life, personal relationships, and the royal family.

Producers gained access to secret conversations recorded in 1991 between Diana and her close friend, Dr. James Colthurst—tapes that served as the primary source for Andrew Morton’s groundbreaking biography, “Diana: Her True Story”.

Both Colthurst and Morton appear in the documentary alongside Diana’s audio tracks, where she discusses Prince Charles (his title at the time), Camilla, and Prince Andrew.

Speaking to Deadline, Kieran Barfield, Creative Director at Love Monday TV, stated: “With this series, we wanted to challenge the long-standing narrative depicting Diana, Princess of Wales, merely as a victim of her circumstances. Here, we do not see Diana as a passive victim of events, but as a woman taking control of her own narrative and risking everything to make her voice heard.”

“Diana Unheard” is set to premiere at the MIPCOM trade market in Cannes, France, nearly 30 years after the Princess died in a Paris car crash at age 36 in August 1997. The debut comes amidst a public rift between Buckingham Palace and Diana’s brother, Earl Spencer, over his new memoir, “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister”, which examines his sister’s life and tragic death.

World.title: Egyptair plans Sydney flights in major Asian expansion
World.content:
Egyptair is preparing to relaunch flights from Cairo to Sydney via Singapore in 2027, marking a potential return to the Australian continent after a nearly 25-year hiatus. According to Sydney Airport officials and industry reports from Aviation Week, the route remains subject to regulatory approvals.

Crucially, the flag carrier is seeking “Fifth Freedom” traffic rights, which would allow it to sell tickets independently for the Singapore-Sydney leg alongside its primary Cairo connections.

Simultaneously, Egypt is accelerating its diplomatic and tourism push into Southeast Asia. It has officially granted Vietnamese citizens visas upon arrival at Egyptian airports to boost bilateral travel and trade ties, a decision highlighted by Deputy Foreign Minister Ambassador Mohamed Abou Bakr Saleh during Vietnam’s National Day celebrations in Cairo.

Complementing these policy changes, Egyptian carrier Air Cairo is exploring direct commercial flights to Vietnam to capitalize on growing Asian tourist demand. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism officials welcomed the initiative, framing Egypt as a key North African gateway to expand reciprocal travel and cultural exchange.

World.title: Pakistan calls for implementing “Mecca Agreement” to safeguard Saudi security amid Houthi attacks
World.content:
Pakistani Defense Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif affirmed that the time has come to implement the “Mecca Agreement,” amid escalating tensions and attacks launched by the Houthis toward the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

During statements to the local Pakistani channel Geo News, Asif emphasized his country’s commitment to Saudi Arabia’s security and the protection of holy sites, stressing that Pakistan does not need a formal treaty to fulfill its responsibility toward safeguarding the sanctities, as Islamabad considers it a binding “duty.”

Diplomatic channels and messages to Tehran

Asif confirmed that Pakistan will continue its diplomatic efforts to contain the escalation and prevent the conflict from spreading to new fronts, underscoring the importance of maintaining regional stability. The Pakistani Defense Minister also revealed that his country relayed a Saudi message to Iran, which detailed growing concerns regarding the attacks carried out by the Houthi group.

The strategic scope of the Mecca pact

The Mecca Joint Defense Agreement is a collective defense pact signed in August 2026 by Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey that enshrines a mutual defense framework committing each nation to treat an attack against one as an attack against all. Expanding upon a prior 2025 bilateral defense deal between Riyadh and Islamabad, the agreement aims to bolster regional security cooperation and deter foreign aggression targeting the signatories’ territories and holy sites.

Historical ties and mediation

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia share deep-rooted defense and security ties, with Islamabad historically pledging to protect the Kingdom’s territorial integrity and the Islamic holy sites in Mecca and Medina against external threats. Pakistan has frequently acted as a diplomatic bridge between Saudi Arabia and Iran to reduce regional friction, utilizing its military and diplomatic channels to de-escalate proxy conflicts in the Arabian Peninsula.

Escalating threats from Yemen

Over the past few days, tensions escalated significantly following a series of long-range drone and missile attempts launched from Yemen targeting Saudi Arabia’s western region. These intercepted strikes close to the Holy City raised sharp international alarm and prompted widespread condemnation across the Islamic world regarding the security of Mecca’s sacred sites.

World.title: Saudi Arabia accuses Huthis of ‘red line’ attack on Mecca as rebels face outrage from Muslim world
World.content:
Saudi Arabia said it shot down a Huthi drone near Mecca, Islam’s holiest city, on Tuesday, drawing swift regional condemnation of the Iran-backed Yemeni rebel group.

Turki al-Maliki, spokesperson for the Saudi-led Coalition Forces, accused the group of targeting the city, saying it was the first time in almost a decade that the Huthis had targeted Mecca.

The security of the holy site is “a red line,” he said, adding that the kingdom “will not hesitate to take the necessary and deterrent measures” against the Yemeni group.

The claim was strongly denied by the Huthis, who follow the Zaydi branch of Shiite Islam and also revere Mecca as a sacred city.

The group’s military spokesman, Yahya Saree, said early Wednesday that its targets were Saudi oil facilities and military bases “far removed from the holy places.”

“The fabrications and lies propagated by the criminal Saudi regime regarding targeting Mecca cannot deceive anyone,” Saree said. “There is no threat whatsoever from Yemen to the holy sites.”

Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed the drone “before it entered” Mecca’s restricted airspace, without specifying how close it was to the city.

The rebel group’s swift advance in Yemen and attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia in recent weeks have put the kingdom in an increasingly difficult position, facing the prospect of being drawn into a wider conflict as the US-Iran war drags on.

Mecca is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. All Muslims worldwide are required, if they are able, to make the pilgrimage to the holy city at least once in their life, with millions making the journey each year.

“This hostile attempt will also remain a black mark in the record of violations by the extremist terrorist Huthi militia, as a deliberate act intended to provoke the feelings of millions of Muslims,” al-Maliki said in a post on X.

A ‘dastardly and heinous’ act

The Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), a 57-member body representing 1.5 billion Muslims, also condemned the incicdent, saying the strikes “violate the sanctity of holy sites and mosques” and “instill fear in innocent civilians.”

The prime minister of Pakistan, which recently signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia, called it a “dastardly and heinous” act. While Shehbaz Sharif did not mention the Huthis in his statement, he affirmed his country’s support for Saudi Arabia.

The interception comes amid heavy fighting. The Huthis launched ballistic missiles and drones at several Saudi cities earlier this week, including Khamis Mushait, Abha and Taif, injuring 13 civilians. On Sunday, they claimed responsibility for an attack on a Saudi military base. And on Wednesday, the Huthis said they attacked a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu, a port city on the Red Sea.

In response, Saudi forces launched airstrikes across Huthi-held areas of Yemen last Saturday and this Tuesday, according to the Huthis.

The Huthis have recently stepped up their fighting against Yemen’s Saudi-backed government and have expanded their area of control. Last week, they captured a Red Sea port city in Yemen and an island near an important waterway that has, for months, acted as a backup to the Strait of Hormuz, allowing for the export of Saudi oil and refined products.

Over the weekend, Saudi Arabia suspended oil loadings at Yanbu, its primary Red Sea export terminal, after it came under attack from militant groups within Iraq.

No date has been given for its resumption, Ashley Hikmet, head of crude at Axis Limited, a trading subsidiary of the Onyx Capital Group, told CNN. Satellite tracking indicates no Saudi crude has left the Red Sea ports since Saturday, he said.

On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia also cut supplies to Europe with immediate effect, Hikmet said, adding that Aramco notified some customers that supplies would be halted until mid-November. The supply disruptions to Europe were first reported by Reuters.

CNN has reached out to Aramco for comment.

The Huthis’ tightening grip over shipping in the Red Sea has fueled fears that the main escape valves for the region’s oil are slamming shut, as Iran and the US continue battling for control of the Strait of Hormuz.

Oil prices climbed back above $100 per barrel last week following further US strikes on Iranian oil tankers in the Persian Gulf and the fighting in Yemen, sparking protests around the world as people demand government action and economic relief.

CNN’s Nadeen Ebrahim and Thomas Gould contributed reporting.

World.title: Gaza building collapse kills more than 20, dozens remain trapped under rubble
World.content:
More than 20 people, including several children, have died after a war-damaged residential building in Gaza City collapsed early Wednesday, local authorities said, with dozens more feared trapped under layers of rubble.

Dr. Mohammed Abu Salmiya, the director of al-Shifa hospital, told CNN at least 21 people have been killed in the disaster, including 11 children, and that many others have been injured.

Search and rescue operations are underway at the site of the collapsed al-Sa’ada building in the city’s Rimal neighborhood, where around 100 people are missing, according to Gaza’s Civil Defense agency.

The building, which is six stories high with four apartments on each floor, was targeted by Israeli airstrikes at the beginning of the war in Gaza, the Civil Defense agency said. The Israeli strikes followed the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attack on Israel.

Around 80 percent of all structures in Gaza have been damaged since the conflict began, with two-thirds of them destroyed, according to the United Nations. The destruction has left Palestinians struggling to find safe shelter amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and the threat of unexploded ordnance.

The demand for shelter is high, especially as winter approaches. Around 1.9 million Palestinians in Gaza — or about 90% of the population — have been displaced during the war, the UN said. Many people in the territory have been displaced several times.

Rescue workers remove the bodies of victims from the rubble of a collapsed building in Gaza City on Wednesday. Saeed M. M. T. Jaras/Anadolu/Getty Images

Hamas’ media office in Gaza said the building fell onto “dozens of displaced families who had been forcibly driven to seek shelter there, amid the complete absence of alternative and safe places of refuge.”

It accused Israel of obstructing rescue efforts by “maintaining its categorical refusal to allow the entry of sufficient equipment, machinery and rescue supplies needed to respond to such disasters.” Israel restricts the entry of what it calls “dual-use goods” into Gaza, including heavy equipment, which it says Hamas could repurpose for military use.

Ramiz Alakbarov, the UN’s humanitarian coordinator for occupied Palestinian territory, called for “urgent approvals” to be granted for the entry of heavy machinery, engine oil and fuel into Gaza.

“No one should have to risk their life simply to find a safe place to shelter,” he said Wednesday.

‘A tragic, painful scene’

Gaza’s Ministry of Housing said Wednesday that about 3,000 buildings in the territory have been classified as “dangerous” or at risk of collapse, after previous Israeli strikes caused structural damage and cracks.

It said the damage poses a “direct threat to the lives of thousands of families” and called for an immediate regional and international response.

“Since midnight in Gaza City, a tragic, painful scene has unfolded: a brutal humanitarian event, as you can see in front of you under this residential building, where dozens of innocent people were trapped,” Civil Defense spokesman Mahmoud Basal said Wednesday.

“People woke up at 3 a.m. to screams and the crying of children who were inside after the building completely collapsed on them,” he added. “We warn of further collapses like this incident in the Gaza Strip, in the areas where citizens are now sheltering.”

No significant reconstruction has taken place in Gaza since a fragile ceasefire deal was agreed last October between Hamas and Israel. The UN reported in late August that the percentage of damaged buildings in the territory has continued to increase since the ceasefire.

Meanwhile, substantial progress from US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, created to advance the US-brokered ceasefire agreement, remains elusive following recent criticism from Israel.

This is a developing story and will be updated.

World.title: Beyond the $1B Milestone: Liberians React to Historic Revenue Gains, Demand ‘Real Impact’
World.content:
Monrovia – Over the past few days, FrontPage Africa reporters have traveled across Liberia — from the market corridors of Monrovia and Paynesville to the trading cities of Kakata in Margibi County and Gbarnga, Bong County — sampling the views of ordinary Liberians on the government’s announcement that domestic revenue has crossed US$1 billion for the first time in the country’s 179-year history.

By Selma Lomax, Francis G. Boayue and Jaheim T. Tumu.

It is a number the Boakai administration has treated as a historic achievement, and by the raw arithmetic, it is. Revenue has climbed from about US$612 million in 2023 to US$699 million in 2024, US$848 million in 2025, and now past the billion-dollar mark this year, with the government targeting US$1.3 billion by year’s end.

Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan on Tuesday delivered the news in Harper, Maryland County, while President Joseph Nyuma Boakai followed with a special national address titled “One Billion, One Liberia,” crediting Liberia Revenue Authority Commissioner General James Dorbor Jallah and a newly digitized tax system for the surge.

But numbers announced in a presidential address travel slowly, if at all, into the daily lives of the people meant to benefit from them. That is the gap FrontPage Africa set out to measure directly — not through additional statistics, but through conversations with the market vendors, business owners, single mothers and commuters who make up the tax base the government is now celebrating.

What they described, almost without exception, was a billion dollars they cannot see, cannot spend, and in several cases, do not entirely trust the framing of. Even Minister Ngafuan himself seemed to anticipate this reaction, telling communities in the Southeast that revenue should be judged not by what enters a government’s account, but by what enters the life of the citizen.

President Boakai, in his own address, went further, insisting the milestone must translate into support for market women, salary relief for civil servants, functioning classrooms for students, and steady medicine supplies for public hospitals.

That is a high bar for any government to set for itself, and it is precisely the bar Liberians are now holding the administration to. Health workers have already moved from words to organized demands — the Liberia Nurses Association is calling for a minimum monthly salary of US$500, and the Liberia Midwives Association has voiced similar hopes for greater investment in maternal health.

Minister Ngafuan has responded by urging patience while acknowledging the pressure is fair, telling those he met that scarcity must never be allowed to excuse indifference, even as the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning begins the delicate work of drafting the 2027 national budget under the weight of these expectations.

Outside the halls of government, however, the reaction has been less about competing budget priorities and more about a basic, recurring question: where, exactly, has this money gone?

From Kakata to Paynesville, the Liberians FrontPage Africa spoke with described an economy that looks unchanged by the announcement — prices that haven’t moved, exchange rate gains that haven’t translated into savings, and public services, from schools to hospitals, that remain as strained as ever. Their voices, gathered in their own words below, offer the clearest picture yet of how the billion-dollar milestone is actually landing across the country.

Yanga King, a businesswoman in Kakata, Margibi County, said her skepticism was sharpened by comments Ngafuan made suggesting the government had already been spending the revenue well before the public announcement — a detail she believes explains the timing and tone of the government’s messaging.

“The Government of Liberia announced about US$1 billion in revenue, but I think we, the Liberian people, are not feeling the impact or benefiting from this money. I listened to the Finance Minister today, and he said the government has been using this money since January of this year. That is just frustrating for us as Liberians.

“I believe the Finance Minister is a smart man. I think he is making this clarification that the money has been used to avoid future embarrassment, because people might say, in time to come, that when he served as Finance Minister, the government collected and announced this money, but the people did not feel its impact.

“Look at the situation in the schools, for example. Parents are unable to register their children because they do not have the money. The government says primary education is free, but there are not enough public primary schools here to accommodate all the students. As a result, parents are forced to send their children to private schools, even though they do not have the money to afford the cost.”

King’s account from Kakata was mirrored, almost point for point, by traders and residents interviewed in Monrovia and Paynesville — different towns, different circumstances, but the same underlying complaint about a milestone that has yet to reach the ground.

At Parker Paint Junction in Monrovia, Edith Wilson, a vendor, responded to news of the billion-dollar figure with a question of her own rather than a statement: “Who are they giving the $1 billion to?” she asked. Wilson said the cost of living keeps rising and prices of local goods continue to climb, describing conditions as no different from years when the national budget was in the hundreds of millions rather than the billions. “No improvement,” she said. “It’s from worse to worst.”

Patricia Sumo, a single mother, described the disconnect in the smallest possible terms — the difference between buying rice by the cup and buying it by the bag. “I’m not feeling nothing, no chance for me,” she said. “I’m still buying rice by the cup L$70, L$80 because I can’t even afford a bag of rice.”

Musu Gorlormator, a market seller in her 50s, said her living conditions are getting worse, not better, and tied her frustration to a personal loss — the death of her husband, which she attributed to inadequate care at the government-run John F. Kennedy Medical Center. “Citizens sick in the hospital and nurses are telling you no bed,” she said.

In Paynesville, Jerry Toe, a seller along the commercial corridor, focused his frustration on the exchange rate specifically, arguing that a stronger Liberian dollar means little if prices at the store never follow it down. “You drop the US exchange rate while prices in the stores remain the same,” he said. “What’s the difference?”

That same exchange-rate frustration was laid out at greater length by Fuku Joshua, another resident who has been closely watching the disconnect between currency movement and everyday costs.

“My take on the situation is that no commodity has been affected by the reduction in the exchange rate. The only thing that has changed is the value of the money itself. The rate has dropped, but nothing else has changed. Prices of goods and services are still the same. The price of gas is still the same, and other materials are also still the same. So, I really don’t understand why the reduction in the U.S. dollar exchange rate is not affecting the prices of other commodities.

“My recommendation to the government is that whenever the exchange rate goes down, we should also see a corresponding reduction in the prices of goods and services. If the rate is down, we should see the prices of basic commodities going down as well.

“Regarding the $1 billion reportedly raised by the Liberia Revenue Authority through taxes from January to September, I recommend that some of that money be used to empower ordinary Liberians. There are people who need support, including access to loans, to enable them to start businesses or pursue individual economic activities. This would help people become more self-reliant rather than depending entirely on government support.

“When it comes to spending the revenue on education, health, and job empowerment, I believe all three areas are very important. Education is important because in some parts of the country, students have to travel for three or four hours just to get to school. These are challenges that need to be addressed. Health is also important. When someone becomes sick, people sometimes have to travel for several hours to access medical care. Situations like these are very discouraging for our country. Therefore, the government needs to invest in education, healthcare, and job empowerment to improve the lives of the people.”

Peter Flomo questioned the emphasis placed on the US$1 billion milestone, arguing that Liberia’s natural-resource base gives the country potential to generate substantially more revenue.

He said the significance of the announcement should ultimately be measured by improvements in areas such as education, salaries, employment and basic living conditions.

Flomo also questioned the relationship between the revenue announcement and the government’s spending, noting that Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan has clarified that the revenue is not sitting in a single account awaiting expenditure but is being used to finance government operations and programs.
