B3 is evaluating taking its event contracts to retail investors, Finsiders Brasil reported from a panel on 15 September, investors. Two days later, Estadão reported that the finance ministry had drafted a measure to ban online casino apps.

What B3 Has Already Built

B3 is Brazil’s only stock and derivatives exchange, based in São Paulo. A forerunner product on rate decisions dates from 2020.

The event-contract line itself began on 27 April 2026, when six contracts started trading. Those six reference the Ibovespa index, the United States dollar and bitcoin.

Contracts on the IPCA inflation index and on quarterly GDP followed. Luiz Masagão is B3’s vice-president for products and customers; he said the launch followed the evolution of prediction markets abroad.

Masagão said the contracts deliver a simplified experience for investors. He added that they keep the safety parameters of B3’s regulated environment.

The exchange publishes the product list on its own website. Twelve contracts across seven underlyings are listed there now, including ether and solana.

How an Event Contract Works

Each contract asks one question with a yes or no answer. An example is whether the dollar closes above a set level that day.

Prices move between R$0 and R$100, so the ceiling is about US$19.41. A holder who is right receives R$100 and a holder who is wrong receives nothing.

The price therefore reads as a probability. A contract at R$70 implies a seventy per cent chance in the market’s view.

Jerson Zanlorenzi, a partner at BTG Pactual, made that point at the B3 Week event. He said a contract at 70 cents in a hundred shows the probability directly.

Zanlorenzi called it a lower-risk entry point for people new to futures. He said the gain and the loss are both known in advance.

That differs from a futures contract, which needs margin and daily settlement. The event contract simply pays a fixed sum or nothing.

The Rule That Draws the Line

Brazil’s National Monetary Council issued Resolution 5,298 on 24 April 2026. It took effect on 4 May.

The rule bans derivatives referenced to sporting, political, electoral, cultural or entertainment events. It allows those tied to economic and financial variables.

Permitted references include interest rates, exchange rates, price indices, commodities and listed securities. The CVM may bar further underlyings at its discretion.

The ban also reaches offers made into Brazil from abroad. Law firm Machado Meyer read it as covering indirect access arrangements.

That wording pushed Polymarket and Kalshi outside the Brazilian perimeter. It left B3’s economic contracts inside it.

The CVM has separately limited these products to professional investors. That means R$10 million in financial assets, about US$1.9 million, or a regulator’s certification.

Why B3 Now Wants the Retail Investor

The pitch was made at B3 Week 2026 in São Paulo on 15 September. Finsiders Brasil reported the panel the next day.

Estadão, reporting the panel on 16 September, headlined its account on how the exchange hopes to avoid an efeito bet. The phrase is the newspaper’s own.

Silvia Bugelli, then B3’s legal director, had put the commercial case in March. She said that without a broad market there is no liquidity.

Bugelli added that without liquidity a contract does not form a price. That is the exchange’s core argument for widening access.

Daniel Maeda, B3’s superintendent for legal affairs, spoke at Rio Innovation Week on 4 August. He said B3 had discussed the target audience with the CVM.

João Accioly, a CVM director, said removing the audience barrier is the watershed for this market. He also said the bureaucrat needs educating alongside the investor.

B3’s Own Words on Bets

B3 runs an education portal called Bora Investir. It published an explainer on prediction markets and bets in December 2025.

The portal says that in prediction markets people bet against other people, not against the house. That is the exchange’s own framing of the difference.

It adds that a betting firm sets the odds itself and profits when bettors lose. Prediction market operators instead earn fees per transaction.

The portal also notes that a position can be traded before the event settles. A sports bet cannot be resold in the same way.

Thiago Godoy, who runs the Papai Financeiro education project, sounded a warning on the same panel. He described users trading hundreds and then thousands of times in short periods.

Godoy said technology can track how often someone trades and how much they stake. He argued that such monitoring should come with retail access.

The Measure Against Betting Apps

Estadão reported on 17 September that the finance ministry had drafted a provisional measure. It said the text was under review at the Planalto palace.

The report said publication was expected within days, before the first round of the October election. A provisional measure takes effect on publication and then needs congressional approval.

The draft targets online casino games rather than sports betting. Estadão reported that sports wagers and club sponsorship would stay outside it if the current design holds.

The government is studying a clause delaying the ban by 180 days. That would force Congress to vote before any prohibition started.

President Lula said on 14 September that betting is a disease and not a game. He said the government would announce a drastic decision soon.

Estadão said the finance ministry and the Casa Civil did not comment. Nothing has been published in the official gazette as of 18 September.

What a Ban Would Cost the State

Industry figures cited by Estadão put online casino games at about 80 per cent of operator revenue. A ban would therefore hit most of the sector’s income.

Each licensed company paid R$30 million, about US$5.8 million, for a five-year authorisation. Estadão reported that the state would have to refund part of that money.

Brazil’s fiscal responsibility law also requires compensation for forgone revenue. That is a second budget problem for the same measure.

The Receita Federal collected R$8.747 billion from gaming and betting between January and July 2026. That is about US$1.7 billion, and roughly 77 per cent more than a year earlier.

The levy on gross gaming revenue was 12 per cent until March and 13 per cent from April. A separate 15 per cent income tax applies to bettors’ net prizes.

Bettors deposited R$88.4 billion, about US$17.2 billion, in licensed sites in the first half of 2026. Estadão counted 31,821,805 unique bettors across almost 119 million accounts.

Football’s Sponsorship Problem

Eight clubs signed a joint manifesto against a ban on 17 September, and a dozen more published the text. Flamengo, Vasco, Fluminense, Botafogo, São Paulo, Santos, Palmeiras and Cruzeiro signed it.

The São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro state federations signed as well. Lance reported that betting firms pay Série A clubs more than R$1 billion a year.

That is about US$194 million at current rates. Reported individual deals run from around R$100 million a year at Palmeiras to far more at Flamengo.

The manifesto argued that the money also reaches smaller clubs and lower divisions. It said no other sector could immediately replace that investment in the interior.

The sector’s own estimate of the loss to football is around R$1 billion. Those figures come from clubs and industry bodies, not from an audited filing.

Betting associations have warned that demand would move to unlicensed sites. The sector estimates the illegal market already matches the legal one in size.

What the Household Data Shows

Brazil’s central bank published a technical study on the betting market in September 2024. It used Pix instant payment receipts from betting companies as its base.

That study found monthly transfers of R$18 billion to R$21 billion, roughly US$3.5 billion to US$4.1 billion. It counted about 24 million individuals sending at least one payment.

The CNC, Brazil’s trade confederation, put monthly spending at R$30 billion for March 2026. That is about US$5.8 billion, drawn from its own consumer debt survey.

The CNC used a difference-in-differences method comparing the periods before and after regulation. Its chief economist, Fabio Bentes, linked the outflow to weaker retail sales.

A study by the Made centre at the University of São Paulo landed on 15 September. It estimated that betting cut economic activity by R$120 billion to R$141 billion in 2025.

That range equals about US$23.3 billion to US$27.4 billion, or 0.9 to 1.1 per cent of output. The finance ministry works with a smaller estimate of around R$60 billion, near US$11.6 billion, a year.

What It Means If You Invest or Live in Brazil

Retail investors cannot buy these contracts today. Access still depends on a CVM rule change that has no published timetable.

Anyone offering contracts on football matches or elections to Brazilian residents sits outside Resolution 5,298. That applies to offshore platforms marketing into the country.

B3 itself trades in São Paulo under the ticker B3SA3. Event contracts are a small line next to its equities and futures business.

Investors holding Brazilian media or football-linked assets face a different question. Sponsorship income would be exposed if the measure widened to sports betting.

Every dollar figure here uses R$5.1521 to the dollar. That is the Banco Central PTAX selling rate for 17 September 2026.

The real has moved little this month against the dollar. Readers converting older reais figures should check the rate for the date concerned.

What Is Not Yet Known

The text of the provisional measure has not been published. Everything about its scope comes from reporting, not from an official document.

It is not confirmed that sports betting and club sponsorship will be spared. Earlier reports described a broader prohibition under discussion.

The CVM has not opened a public consultation on retail access to event contracts. No B3 executive has given a launch date for a retail product.

The size of any licence refund is unclear. Some 188 brands appear on the regulator’s authorised list, though company counts differ by source.

Estimates of household betting outflows vary widely by method. Deposits, losses and gross gaming revenue are three different measures and are often conflated.

Whether Congress would approve a ban is untested. A provisional measure lapses if deputies and senators do not vote it through.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is a B3 event contract? It is a binary derivative that pays R$100, about US$19.41, if a stated economic outcome occurs. It pays nothing if the outcome does not occur. Can ordinary Brazilians buy them? Not yet, because the CVM limits them to professional investors with R$10 million, about US$1.9 million, in assets. B3 said on 15 September that it wants that widened. What would the provisional measure ban? Estadão reported that the draft targets online casino games rather than sports betting. The text has not been published, so the scope is not confirmed. How much tax does betting pay in Brazil? The Receita Federal collected R$8.747 billion, about US$1.7 billion, from gaming and betting between January and July 2026. That was roughly 77 per cent more than the same period of 2025.

World.title: Peru Clears Pichincha to Buy Diners Club and Keeps Velarde at Central Bank
World.content:
Peru · Economy

Key Facts — What happened. The SBS cleared Banco Pichincha to buy up to all of Diners Club Peru. — The paperwork. Resolution SBS 02290-2026 was disclosed to the market on 17 September. — The price. About US$6.96 million, for up to 100 percent of the shares. — The catch. The resolution is an authorisation, not a completed purchase. — The other vote. The Senate kept Julio Velarde at the central bank until 2031. — The rate. The BCRP reference rate has stood at 4.25 percent for a year.

Two institutions moved on Peru’s financial system in the same week, and both moves point the same way. One reshuffles a card business, the other locks in the man who sets interest rates.

The Central Reserve Bank of Peru in Lima. The Senate ratified Julio Velarde for another five-year term (Photo: Ovruni, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Banco Pichincha told Peru’s market regulator on 17 September 2026 that the SBS had cleared it to buy Diners Club Peru. The day before, the Senate voted 40 to 12 to keep Julio Velarde as central bank president until 2031.

What the SBS Actually Approved

The Superintendencia de Banca, Seguros y AFP is Peru’s banking, insurance and pensions regulator. Its decision is recorded in Resolution SBS 02290-2026, according to Banco Pichincha.

The bank disclosed it on 17 September 2026 in a Hecho de Importancia to the market regulator, the SMV. That filing route is the standard way a Peruvian issuer reports a material event.

The resolution allows the bank to acquire up to 100 percent of the shares of Diners Club Peru S.A. The stated purpose is that Diners Club Peru becomes a subsidiary of the bank.

RPP, citing the resolution, put the total consideration at S/23,474,937. At the BCRP banking-system selling rate of S/3.372 per US dollar on 16 September, that is about US$6.96 million.

How the Deal Got Here

The transaction did not appear this week, and the resolution sets out its history. Pichincha’s board agreed on 20 January 2026 to buy at least 94.77 percent of the shares.

On 26 May 2026 the same board ratified the decision and widened it to as much as 100 percent. The S/23.47 million figure, about US$6.96 million, attaches to that widened agreement.

The two companies were already partners before any of this. They formed a consortium in 2015 to run the credit card business together, Infobae reported.

Moody’s Local Peru put the bank’s share of that Diners consortium portfolio at roughly 27 percent. The rating agency noted the bank books 100 percent of the portfolio on its balance sheet regardless.

Why a Regulator Has to Sign Off

Peru does not let a bank buy a financial company quietly, and this is the mechanism. Law 26702, the General Law of the Financial System, governs what a bank may own.

It lets banks acquire shares in firms providing complementary or auxiliary services. It also requires prior SBS authorisation before a bank sets up a subsidiary.

The SBS reviewed the file and found the paperwork met the established procedure. The same law lists card issuance and administration among permitted banking activities.

That is the legal hook the regulator used, according to RPP’s account of the resolution. The SBS opened a separate public consultation on 15 September on procedures for buying more than 10 percent of a bank.

Who Banco Pichincha Is in Peru

The bank is older than its current name suggests, and the history explains its scale. It was constituted in 1964 as Financiera y Promotora de la Construccion, known as Finanpro.

It was authorised to operate as a bank in 1986 under the name Banco Financiero del Peru. Ecuador’s Banco Pichincha group entered the shareholder register in 1994 and built up control.

It bought NBK Bank in 2001 and America Financiera in 2011, Infobae reported. The SBS approved the change of name to Banco Pichincha in 2018.

Moody’s Local Peru reported gross loans of S/8,063 million at 30 June 2025, about US$2.39 billion. The agency affirmed the bank at A- with a stable outlook on 26 March 2026.

Mas Finanzas reported net profit of S/19.46 million in the first five months of 2026, about US$5.8 million. That was 8.16 percent below the S/21.19 million, about US$6.3 million, booked a year earlier.

The parent, Banco Pichincha C.A., is Ecuador’s largest private bank, Moody’s Local said. Grupo Pichincha held about US$31 billion in assets across eleven financial firms in six countries, Gestion reported in 2024.

What Diners Club Peru Brings

Diners Club Peru is a card issuer rather than a bank, and it sits in a narrow segment. It is supervised by the SBS and trades on the strength of the Diners Club brand.

Its card base and its latest profit figures were not disclosed in the filings reviewed for this article. The consideration of about US$6.96 million is small against a bank of Pichincha’s size.

Infobae reported that the resolution sets out no changes to the Diners Club brand. It also sets out no changes to current products or to the conditions on existing cards.

The Senate Keeps Velarde

The second decision came from the legislature rather than a regulator. The Senate plenary approved the report ratifying Julio Velarde on 16 September 2026.

The vote was 40 in favour, 12 against and no abstentions, Congress said in its own release. The term runs five years, to 2031, matching the constitutional period.

The executive had already designated him by Supreme Resolution 258-2026-PCM on 21 August 2026. Velarde has led the BCRP since September 2006, Gestion reported.

He has been ratified under Garcia, Humala, Kuczynski, Castillo and now Keiko Fujimori. Senator Patricia Juarez said Peru has had low regional inflation under his conduct of the bank.

Opponents from Juntos por el Peru questioned the distributional effect of the bank’s decisions, La Republica reported. The commission report found the candidacy met the conditions with no legal impediment, though its chair recorded his own opposition.

The board is still incomplete, and the Senate must elect three more directors. La Republica reported evaluations scheduled for 22 to 24 September and a final report by 7 October.

Peru Has a Senate Again

A foreign reader may be surprised that Peru has a Senate at all. The bicameral Congress was installed on 25 July 2026, the official gazette El Peruano reported.

It has 60 senators and 130 deputies, serving the 2026 to 2031 term. The change ended 33 years of continuous single-chamber legislature, El Peruano said.

The reform was approved through Law 31988, which restored the two chambers. Ratifying the central bank president is one of the powers the Senate now exercises.

Where Monetary Policy Stands

The man the Senate kept is running a policy that has not moved in a year. The BCRP held its reference rate at 4.25 percent on 11 September 2026, Forbes Peru reported.

Central bank series confirm the rate at 4.25 percent through August 2026. That is twelve consecutive months without a change, Infobae reported.

Inflation is not where the bank wants it. Lima metropolitan prices rose 4.44 percent in the year to August 2026, INEI said on 1 September.

The national twelve-month rate was 4.06 percent, Forbes Peru reported from the same release. The BCRP target band is 1 to 3 percent, and inflation has sat above it since March.

Inflation expectations stood at 3.01 percent in July, just above the band, Infobae reported. The bank linked the overshoot mainly to fuel prices and their effect on transport costs.

The sol has been steady through the month. The BCRP banking-system selling rate was S/3.372 per US dollar on 16 September 2026.

Consolidation and Concentration

Peruvian banking is already concentrated, and this deal does little to change that. Nineteen private banks operate in the country, La Republica reported from SBS data.

The four largest hold more than 80 percent of loans, deposits and equity, PeruCheck found using SBS figures. Those four are BCP, BBVA, Scotiabank and Interbank.

System profits reached S/14,147 million in 2025, about US$4.2 billion at the 16 September rate. That was 37 percent above the S/10,325 million, about US$3.06 billion, earned in 2024.

The same four banks took S/11,800 million of it, about US$3.5 billion, or 83 percent. BCP alone earned S/6,478 million, about US$1.92 billion.

Arturo Garcia, an economist at ESAN, told La Republica in February what high concentration does. He said entities with greater participation have greater influence in determining market rates.

He argued the SBS must be active in promoting the entry of more financial entities. The SBS has separately signalled more structural change, flagging possible fully digital banks and pension-arm absorptions.

What It Means If You Hold a Peruvian Card or Account

If you carry a Diners Club card in Peru, nothing in the resolution changes your terms. Infobae reported that the brand, the products and the card conditions are untouched by the document.

That is the position today, not a permanent commitment by the buyer. Watch the tarifario, the published fee schedule, which any issuer can revise with notice.

If you are a depositor at Banco Pichincha, the deal is small relative to the bank. About US$6.96 million is a modest outlay for a lender with roughly US$2.39 billion in gross loans.

If you borrow on cards in Peru, the concentration numbers matter more than this transaction. The average credit card rate was 74.8 percent a year, La Republica reported from SBS data.

If you hold soles, Velarde’s continuation is the more consequential of the two decisions. It signals policy continuity at an institution that has held its rate for twelve months.

If you are an investor, the Senate’s remaining three board picks are the open variable. A central bank president sets direction, but the board votes on the rate each month.

What Is Not Yet Known

Several things stayed unanswered after both decisions. The exact date the SBS signed Resolution 02290-2026 was not stated in the filings reviewed here.

Peru Retail reported the authorisation as dated 16 September and published the following day. Banco Pichincha disclosed it on 17 September, and that date is firm.

Diners Club Peru’s card base, its portfolio size and its latest results were not disclosed. Nor was any timetable given for closing the share purchase itself.

Whether the Diners Club brand survives in the medium term is not addressed anywhere in the resolution. The three outstanding BCRP directorships are also unresolved, with the process running into October.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Banco Pichincha already bought Diners Club Peru? Not yet. The SBS authorised the purchase, and the bank still has to complete it. Will my Diners Club card change? The resolution sets out no changes to the brand, the products or the card conditions. Gestion and Infobae both reported that position. How long has Julio Velarde run Peru’s central bank? Since September 2006, according to Gestion. The Senate vote extends that to 2031. Why does a Senate vote on the central bank? Peru restored its bicameral Congress on 25 July 2026. Ratifying the BCRP president is one of the Senate’s powers.

World.title: Ecopetrol Hands Its Board to a Campaign Strategist as Output Falls
World.content:
Colombia · Energy

Key Facts — What happened. Ecopetrol’s board elected Carlos Augusto Suarez Rojas as its chairman on 17 September 2026. — Who he is. He is a lawyer who ran President Abelardo de la Espriella’s 2026 campaign strategy. — The catch. Eleven analysts tracked by Stock Analysis rate the New York listing a sell. — The state’s grip. The finance ministry holds about 88.5 percent of Ecopetrol’s shares. — Production. Group output fell 6.6 percent to 705,800 barrels of oil equivalent daily. — What comes next. Ecopetrol still has no permanent chief executive after two departures this year.

Ecopetrol has changed board chairman twice since July, and its chief executive seat is empty. The newest chairman ran President Abelardo de la Espriella’s campaign strategy.

Ecopetrol’s headquarters in Bogota. The board elected a new chairman on 17 September (Photo: EEIM, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Ecopetrol’s board elected Carlos Augusto Suarez Rojas as its chairman on 17 September 2026. He had joined the nine-member board only two days earlier, at an extraordinary shareholders’ meeting.

What The Board Decided

The nine directors met on 17 September 2026 and chose Suarez to chair them. Claudia Margarita Lafaurie Taboada was elected vice chair at the same meeting.

El Tiempo reported the choice first, and Investing.com carried it to English-language markets that day. Suarez replaces Luis Felipe Henao Cardona, who had held the chair since late July.

Henao stays on the board and now chairs its corporate governance and sustainability committee. He has described his own spell in the chair as a transitional presidency.

The Ministry of Finance nominated Suarez to the board as an independent member. Ecopetrol had not published a statement from Suarez about his plans by 18 September.

The Exploration and Production segment engages in the exploration and production of oil and gas. The Transport and Logistics segment is involved in…

Who Carlos Suarez Is

Suarez is a lawyer trained at the Universidad Externado de Colombia in Bogota. He holds specialisations in public management, fiscal control and criminal law.

He founded Estrategia y Poder, a consultancy working in political communication and crisis management. El Colombiano described him as the main architect of De la Espriella’s 2026 electoral and digital strategy.

He is also listed as a co-founder of Defensores de la Patria, the president’s movement. His earlier public sector work includes a post at the Cundinamarca comptroller’s office.

Colombia One reported that he is a personal friend of the president. Gustavo Petro’s own campaign manager, Ricardo Roa, ran the company from 2023 until July this year.

The Shake-Up He Inherits

Ecopetrol announced on 23 July 2026 that directors Angela Maria Robledo and Tatiana Roa had resigned. Semana reported the two were among the board members closest to then-president Gustavo Petro.

Ricardo Roa’s departure as chief executive was confirmed in the same round of changes. Luis Felipe Henao took the chair and Hildebrando Velez Galeano became vice chair.

Velez notified his resignation on 14 September, effective the following day. Juan Carlos Hurtado Parra quit as acting chief executive on the same day.

El Tiempo had published an audio recording that it said involved Hurtado and a Catalan businessman. Henao told El Tiempo he would ask Hurtado for his irrevocable resignation.

Chief financial officer Camilo Barco took the interim presidency on 15 September. No criminal charges against Hurtado have been reported in connection with the recording.

How Bogota Controls The Vote

Colombia’s finance ministry holds about 88.5 percent of Ecopetrol, Semana reported on 15 September. That stake makes any contested shareholder vote a formality.

The extraordinary meeting on 15 September opened with 88.8 percent of shares present. Participation rose to 92.69 percent within two hours, Semana said.

The government’s single slate of nine directors passed with 99.65 percent support. Shareholders also amended Article 20 of the bylaws, which governs board composition and election.

The Ministry of Finance proposed that amendment. About 277,000 minority shareholders hold the rest of the company.

Where The Company Stands

Ecopetrol reported second-quarter net income of 6.1 trillion pesos on 3 August 2026. That is about US$1.9 billion, and it was 235 percent above the same quarter of 2025.

Group earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation reached 17.7 trillion pesos, about US$5.6 billion. Revenue was 40.2 trillion pesos, or about US$12.8 billion, up 35 percent.

Peso figures here use the Banco de la Republica market rate for 18 September 2026. That rate was 3,151.73 pesos to the dollar.

Production fell 6.6 percent to 705,800 barrels of oil equivalent a day. Gross debt was two times EBITDA at group level, and 1.3 times excluding the ISA transmission unit.

Cash stood at 11.3 trillion pesos, about US$3.6 billion, at the end of June. Proved reserves were 1,944 million barrels of oil equivalent at the close of 2025.

The company put reserve life at 7.8 years and the replacement ratio at 121 percent. Refining throughput rose 6.1 percent to 438,500 barrels a day in the quarter.

The Exploration Argument

Petro said in October 2024 that he would not sign new oil and gas exploration contracts. He said signing new contracts would expose children and grandchildren to the total death of the human species.

Abelardo de la Espriella took office on 7 August 2026 with the opposite position. In March 2026 he told an industry audience he would open the door fully to fracking.

Mines and Energy Minister Maria Nohemi Arboleda says Colombia needs more barrels and more gas molecules. Infobae reported on 9 September that the government wants output back at one million barrels a day.

National output was 730,966 barrels a day at the time of that report. The plan starts with unblocking about 270 contracts that already exist.

An intersectoral hydrocarbons committee was due to be activated in late September. Henao put the case bluntly, saying an oil company that does not explore liquidates itself slowly.

What Analysts Say

Alejandro Sanchez of Aval Asset Management spoke to Bloomberg Linea on 17 September 2026. He said the market will watch several pending decisions from the new governance, beyond oil prices.

His list starts with the 2027 investment plan and its exploration spending. It also covers the company’s stance on ISA, staff retention and cost efficiency.

Stock Analysis records eleven analysts with a consensus sell rating on the New York listing. Their average target is US$13.91, well below the 17 September close.

What It Means If You Hold The Shares

Ecopetrol’s Bogota-listed shares closed at 2,730 pesos on 17 September 2026, down 3.7 percent. That is about US$0.87 at the 18 September market rate.

The New York listing, ticker EC, closed at US$17.38 the same day. Each American depositary receipt represents twenty ordinary shares.

The 52-week range for the receipts runs from US$8.57 to US$18.38. Trailing dividends of US$0.65 per receipt give a yield near 3.7 percent.

Dividend policy is set at the shareholders’ meeting, where the state decides the outcome. Holders outside Colombia therefore carry the peso exchange rate and Bogota’s politics together.

What Is Not Yet Known

Ecopetrol has no permanent chief executive, and no appointment date has been set. Bloomberg Linea named Joaquin Gutierrez as a leading candidate on 17 September.

The 2027 investment plan has not been published. The company has not said whether it will sell or keep its ISA stake.

Henao has spoken of a forensic audit into past contracting at the company. Its scope, cost and timetable have not been made public.

Whether fracking proceeds depends on regulation and the courts, not on the board alone. Suarez has not set out a public agenda for his chairmanship.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Carlos Suarez? He is a Bogota lawyer and political consultant who founded the firm Estrategia y Poder. He ran the 2026 campaign strategy for President Abelardo de la Espriella. Why was the Ecopetrol chair vacant? Luis Felipe Henao held it from late July 2026 in what he called a transitional role. A new nine-member board was elected on 15 September and had to choose its own chair. How much of Ecopetrol does the Colombian state own? The finance ministry holds about 88.5 percent of the shares, Semana reported on 15 September 2026. That leaves roughly 277,000 minority holders with the remainder. What does this mean for New York-listed holders? Each depositary receipt covers twenty ordinary shares, so Bogota price moves pass straight through. The receipts closed at US$17.38 on 17 September 2026, against an average analyst target of US$13.91.

World.title: Chile Has Mined 7% Less Copper So Far in 2026 Than Last Year
World.content:
Chile · Economy

Key Facts — What happened. Chile mined about 2.9 million tonnes of copper from January to July. — The number. That is 7.1% less than a year earlier, the weakest since 2003. — The catch. Cochilco still forecasts a full-year fall of only 2.6% for 2026. — Who is short. El Teniente fell 26.5% and Escondida 9.3% over those seven months. — The price. London three-month copper closed at US$14,083.50 a tonne this week. — The budget. Chile’s 2027 budget assumes copper at US$5.37 a pound, below spot.

Chile is the source of about a quarter of the world’s mined copper. Seven months of 2026 data show the smallest haul for that period since 2003.

The Chuquicamata copper mine in northern Chile. Output for the first seven months is the weakest in years (Photo: Pierre cb, public domain via Wikimedia Commons)

Chile produced roughly 2.9 million tonnes of copper between January and July 2026, about 7.1% below the same months of 2025. The figures come from the statistics institute INE and the state copper commission Cochilco, published on 31 August.

What the Seven-Month Data Show

INE reported 403,424 tonnes of mined copper in July 2026. That was 9.4% below the 445,322 tonnes recorded in July 2025.

The agency blamed weather in the north and maintenance at large operations. Its mining production index fell 7.2% year on year in the same month.

Adding July to the first half leaves about 2.9 million tonnes for seven months. Actualidad Juridica put the shortfall at about 223,000 tonnes against 2025.

The Actualidad Juridica report described it as the lowest January-July total since 2003. Both attribute the underlying data to INE and Cochilco rather than to a private house.

How the Official Forecast Still Adds Up

Cochilco published its revised outlook on 11 August 2026. It expects 5.27 million tonnes for the full year, a fall of 2.6%.

That implies 2025 output of roughly 5.41 million tonnes. Seven months at 2.9 million tonnes leaves about 2.37 million for August to December.

The same five months of 2025 yielded roughly 2.29 million tonnes. So the official number requires a gain of about 3% in the closing stretch.

It would follow declines in six of the seven months, June being the exception. Cochilco also sees 5.55 million tonnes in 2027 as new tonnes arrive.

Where the Tonnes Went Missing

Cochilco’s mine-level figures, reported by CNN Chile, name the main gaps. El Teniente produced 148,900 tonnes in seven months against 202,600 a year earlier.

That is a drop of 26.5%, the steepest among the large divisions. Escondida, controlled by BHP, fell 9.3% to 721,400 tonnes.

Teck’s Quebrada Blanca was the clear gainer, up 16.8% to 132,000 tonnes. Collahuasi was broadly flat and Los Pelambres slipped 3.7%.

In July alone, Escondida fell 22.1% to 89,400 tonnes. Collahuasi rose 12.3% that month to 38,400 tonnes.

Codelco’s Own Position

State miner Codelco produced 564,000 tonnes in the first half of 2026. That was 11% down on the 634,000 tonnes of a year earlier.

Pre-tax profit still rose to US$1.97 billion from US$429 million, Reuters reported. The realised price climbed to 653.2 cents a pound from 461.7 cents.

Direct cash costs rose 7% to 231.6 cents a pound. Chairman Bernardo Fontaine said the 1.33-1.36 million tonne target looked difficult to achieve.

On 16 September, Reuters reported the company’s restructuring plan may slip to year-end. Four sources told the agency job cuts could reach 5% to 20% of about 77,000 staff.

Structural Causes and One-Off Ones

Two very different problems are running at the same time. The structural one is ore grade, the share of copper in the rock.

BHP reported Escondida concentrator feed grade at 0.90%, down from 1.02%. It guided fiscal 2027 group copper output to 1.65-1.80 million tonnes.

The prior year came in near 1.95 million tonnes. Permitting is the second slow constraint, and the new framework law aims to cut delays.

The one-off causes are weather and the El Teniente accident of July 2025. Storms in July and August 2026 halted operations and disrupted ports.

How the El Teniente Setback Works

El Teniente is an underground block-cave mine over a century old. Ore is undercut and allowed to break under its own weight.

That method makes the rock mass seismically active as voids grow. Codelco suspended the Andes Norte expansion on 4 August 2026 for two years.

Fastmarkets reported the decision followed geological studies flagging seismic risk. El Teniente produced 310,100 tonnes in 2025, down 13% on the prior year.

The same month, ministers let Codelco retain US$2.422 billion of 2025 profits. Mining Minister Daniel Mas said the aim was to safeguard the credit rating.

What the Price Is Doing

Copper has been strong all year despite the volume losses. The London Metal Exchange showed a three-month closing price of US$14,083.50 a tonne.

That quote was day-delayed and dated to 16 September 2026. The same contract closed at US$14,708 on 8 September, after an all-time high the same day.

Comex December copper hit a record US$6.8730 a pound that week. The metal was up roughly 22% on the year at that point.

The Banco Central de Chile’s copper indicator read US$6.36 a pound on 17 September. Morgan Stanley expects 2026 to bring the first drop in global mine supply since 2017.

What It Means for the Budget and the Peso

Copper ores and refined copper made up about half of Chile’s 2025 exports. Trade data put total exports above US$107 billion in 2025, with mining the largest single block.

The finance ministry’s expert committee set the 2027 reference price at US$5.37 a pound. That is up from US$4.38 a pound used for the 2026 budget.

The committee also fixed trend non-mining growth at 2.6%. Volumes matter because a reference price cannot mine tonnes that do not exist.

Central bank data showed August copper exports at US$4.62 billion. That was 14% below July and 3.2% below August 2025, Bloomberg reported.

The Exchange Rate and the Arithmetic

The Banco Central de Chile’s last published dolar observado was 957.53 pesos, on 15 September 2026. All peso figures here use that dated rate.

At that rate a tonne of copper at US$14,083.50 is about 13.5 million pesos. The peso has weakened even as the metal has held near records.

It stood near 926 pesos to the dollar on 10 September, central bank data show. Lower export volumes are one plausible reason, though the bank has not said so.

Chile’s July Imacec activity index fell 1.5% year on year. Mining within that index was down 9.3%.

What Officials and the Industry Say

Mining Minister Daniel Mas set a goal of returning to about 6 million tonnes a year. He pointed to framework law 21,770, which is meant to cut permit times.

The government says simplifying mining permits could unblock about US$24 billion of investment. Sonami president Jorge Riesco was more bullish in January 2026.

He projected national output of 5.5 to 5.7 million tonnes for the year. Cochilco’s own August revision put the figure at 5.27 million tonnes.

The gap between those two numbers is the story of 2026 so far. Neither body has publicly revised its position since the July data landed.

What It Means If You Live or Invest in Chile

Exporters and mining suppliers face lower volumes but higher unit revenue. Contractors are the exposed group if Codelco’s restructuring cuts deep.

Codelco says contractors account for about 80% of its jobs. Chile’s unemployment rate was 9.5% in July 2026.

For residents paid in pesos, a weaker currency raises imported costs. For dollar earners, the same move cuts the local cost of living.

Investors should watch the August and September output prints closely. Those two months decide whether the 5.27 million tonne forecast survives.

What Is Not Yet Known

Cochilco has not published a further revision since 11 August. August output figures were not available at the time of writing.

Codelco has not given a firm number for job reductions. The company said it was too early to speculate about decisions.

No analyst house has been identified publicly forecasting a 7% full-year fall. The 7.1% figure describes the seven months already recorded, not the year.

The El Teniente restart date for Andes Norte remains a two-year estimate. Whether the peso keeps weakening against a record copper price is untested.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has Chile’s copper output really fallen 7%? Yes, for January to July 2026 against the same months of 2025. The full-year forecast from Cochilco is a smaller fall of 2.6%. Why is the copper price high if Chile is producing less? Lower supply from a quarter of the world’s mines tightens the market. Demand from grids and data centres has stayed firm. What does this do to Chile’s budget? Copper is about half of exports, so volumes and price both matter. The 2027 budget uses a reference price of US$5.37 a pound. Is El Teniente back to normal? No, its seven-month output was 26.5% below last year. Codelco has also paused the Andes Norte expansion for two years.

Sources: INE, industrial production release for July 2026, Reuters via Kitco, Chile’s July copper output down 9.4%, Mining.com, Cochilco sees 2026 output at 5.27 million tonnes, Actualidad Juridica, January-July output lowest since 2003, CNN Chile, Cochilco mine-level figures to July 2026, Reuters via Kitco, Codelco first-half results, Reuters via Mining.com, Codelco restructuring may slip to year-end, London Metal Exchange, LME Copper price page

World.title: Colombia Quits the Global LGBTI Rights Coalition It Was Co-Chairing
World.content:
Colombia · Politics

Key Facts — What happened. Colombia withdrew from the Equal Rights Coalition on 17 September 2026. — The timing. It left while co-chairing the coalition with Spain, part-way through the term. — The catch. Colombian law does not change, because court rulings and statutes stay in force. — The stated reason. The foreign ministry said membership was not a priority for this government. — The reaction. Caribe Afirmativo called the exit a snub to the international community. — Still open. Neither Spain nor the coalition has published a response to the departure.

Colombia gave up a seat its own co-chair says took years to secure, and gave no reason. The rights themselves sit in court rulings that a diplomatic note cannot touch.

Colombia’s foreign ministry in Bogota, which sent the withdrawal note on 17 September (Photo: Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0)

Colombia’s foreign ministry withdrew the country from the Equal Rights Coalition on 17 September 2026. The note gave no reason, and took effect the same day.

What the Foreign Ministry Did

The withdrawal went out as diplomatic note S-DVAMCP-26-024300, reported by the outlet Mi Oriente. It came from the vice-ministry for migration, consular affairs and international protection.

The text told the coalition’s executive committee that the government had decided to leave. The operative line says the national government has decided the withdrawal of the Republic of Colombia, effective from today.

Infobae reported that the ministry also informed the government of Spain, Colombia’s partner in the chair. Nothing in the note set out a reason for the decision.

The Reason the Government Gave Later

A day after the note, the vice-minister Pedro Agustin Roa recorded a video statement. He said Colombia has a very robust body of rights protected by the constitution, public policy and a set of rules.

He added that rulings of the Constitutional Court protect minorities on grounds of sexual orientation. El Heraldo quoted the ministry saying the exit does not in any way mean a step backwards on LGBTI rights.

El Universal reported the ministry’s position that taking part in the coalition was not a priority for this government. Caribe Afirmativo told El Espectador its own sources put the decision down to the membership being seen as a legacy of the previous government.

What the Equal Rights Coalition Is

The coalition was founded in 2016 at the Global LGBTI Human Rights Conference in Montevideo. Uruguay and the Netherlands led its creation, according to the coalition’s own history page.

El Tiempo described it as an intergovernmental body dedicated to protecting the rights of LGBTI people. Its own pages carry both 43 and 44 member states, and Colombian outlets used both this week.

Colombian outlets used both numbers this week, and one agency report said 45. The work runs through five thematic groups covering diplomacy, national law, donor coordination, humanitarian protection and the 2030 agenda.

How the Chair Works and What Colombia Held

Two member states and two civil-society organisations share the chair for two-year terms. Colombia and Spain held the government seats, with Caribe Afirmativo and Fundacion Triangulo alongside them.

The coalition’s site lists that pairing under the 2024 to 2026 period. El Espectador dated the start to 17 December 2024 and said the term ran to February 2027.

Other outlets described the term as running from 2025 to 2027, so the end date is not settled in the reporting. Noticaribe reported that Colombia joined under Gustavo Petro, after years of groundwork under Juan Manuel Santos and Ivan Duque.

El Espectador said no member state had previously left the coalition while holding the chair. No public record of an earlier withdrawal by any other member state was found this week.

How Civil Society Responded

Caribe Afirmativo held the civil-society half of Colombia’s chair and was not consulted in advance. Its director Wilson Castaneda told El Tiempo the move was an unfortunate decision.

He said it was the clearest decision this government has taken against LGBTI rights, with an international impact. He added that it leaves Colombia in a bad position internationally, signalling no recognition of protection for LGBTI people.

Speaking to La Silla Vacia, he said it would have been healthier to at least wait for the end of the chair. Noticaribe quoted the organisation calling the exit a snub to the international community and a break with the leadership Colombia had built.

The group said it had counted 24 government actions in 40 days that it argues weaken LGBTI rights. The NGO Temblores said the government must publicly explain why it took the decision.

The Ombudsperson and Other Critics

Colombia’s ombudsperson, Iris Marin, responded publicly to the withdrawal. She said LGBTIQ+ people need the backing of the state, and the state cannot stop giving it.

She cited 68 killings of trans women between 2024 and April 2026, and 148 killings of LGBTI people during 2025. El Universal reported the first as an attorney general’s figure and the second as the forensic institute’s; the anthropologist David J.

Luquetta told La Silla Vacia that public discourse determines what a society treats as tolerable, suspect or undesirable. Semana reported that politicians from several sectors spoke against the decision, without naming them in the piece reviewed.

What Colombian Law Still Says

A withdrawal from an intergovernmental coalition does not amend Colombian law. The coalition has no treaty, no binding obligations on members and no enforcement power.

Same-sex marriage rests on Constitutional Court ruling SU-214 of 2016, issued on 28 April that year. Adoption by same-sex couples rests on ruling C-683 of 2015, issued on 4 November 2015.

That ruling held that the sexual orientation of a person cannot be confused with a lack of suitability to adopt. It read the children’s code as covering same-sex couples who form a family.

Law 1482 of 30 November 2011 added article 134A to the penal code, punishing acts of discrimination. Sexual orientation is named among the protected grounds, with 12 to 36 months and a fine, as amended in 2015.

The Wider Policy Direction Since 7 August

Abelardo de la Espriella took office on 7 August 2026 and has moved quickly on foreign policy. On 10 August his government recognised Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights, the second state to do so.

It also restored ties with Israel and recognised Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara, MercoPress reported. Colombia joined the United States anti-drug initiative known as Shield of the Americas.

El Universal reported 85 extraditions in the government’s first 40 days. During the campaign the president said a child needs a father and a mother, and opposed adoption by same-sex couples.

What It Means If You Live or Invest in Colombia

For residents, nothing in the civil registry, marriage, adoption or criminal law changed on 17 September. Notaries and judges continue to apply the same rulings they applied the week before.

For employers, the anti-discrimination provisions of the penal code are unaffected by this decision. Company policies written to Colombian law need no revision because of this decision.

The change is diplomatic, affecting where Colombian officials sit and which joint statements they sign. Any shift in domestic entitlements would require Congress or the Constitutional Court, not the foreign ministry.

What Is Not Yet Known

Spain has not published a public response, and neither has the coalition’s secretariat. It is unclear who will complete the government half of the chair for the remainder of the term.

The ministry has not said whether Colombia will keep taking part in the coalition’s working groups as an observer. No figure has been published for what membership cost the Colombian budget.

Rights groups have asked publicly for the reasoning, and raised concern over the foreign ministry’s 2027 budget. The ministry had not answered that request at the time of writing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does this change marriage or adoption rights in Colombia? No. Those rights come from Constitutional Court rulings SU-214 of 2016 and C-683 of 2015, which are unaffected. What reason did the government give? The note gave none. The vice-ministry later said membership was not a priority and that constitutional protections already cover the population. Who was Colombia’s partner in the chair? Spain held the other government seat for the term. Caribe Afirmativo and Fundacion Triangulo were the civil-society co-chairs. Has any other state left the coalition? No earlier withdrawal is on public record. El Espectador said this is the first exit by a state while it held the chair.

World.title: Yucatan Monitors 180 People After Rare Amoeba Death in Merida
World.content:
Mexico · Health

Key Facts — What happened. A wakeboard instructor in Merida died on 8 September after a rare amoeba infection. — The numbers. Some 180 people remain under watch, down from 361 first listed as exposed. — The site. The artificial lake at Plaza La Isla in northern Merida is closed. — The catch. Surveillance is precautionary, and officials say no second infection has been reported. — The science. Infection happens when contaminated water enters the nose, never from drinking it. — The odds. The United States logged 180 cases in total between 1937 and 2025.

A wakeboard instructor died in Merida after a rare amoeba infection traced to an artificial lake. State health officials say 180 people remain under watch until early October.

Merida, Yucatan. Health officials say the alert is confined to one closed lake in the north of the city (Photo: Eden, Janine and Jim, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Yucatan’s health authorities confirmed on 14 September 2026 that Naegleria fowleri killed a water sports instructor. Mexico’s federal reference laboratory also found the amoeba in the lake where he worked.

What the Health Authorities Confirmed

The Instituto de Diagnostico y Referencia Epidemiologicos confirmed the case on 14 September 2026. InDRE is the federal reference laboratory of Mexico’s health ministry.

The patient was a wakeboard instructor aged 34, according to the state health secretariat. He was admitted to an IMSS hospital in Merida on 2 September.

He died on 8 September, six days after he was admitted. The cause was primary amebic meningoencephalitis, the disease this amoeba causes.

It is the first case ever officially registered in Yucatan. State health secretary Miguel Alberto Alcocer Gamboa says no other infection has been reported.

The Lake at Plaza La Isla

The exposure is linked to an artificial lake at Plaza La Isla in northern Merida. The lake sits at a shopping centre and is used for wakeboarding.

Samples taken from the water tested positive for the amoeba. Officials put the index case’s exposure window between 4 and 15 August 2026.

The lake has been shut since the investigation began. The state ratified that suspension once the laboratory result arrived.

Reopening requires laboratory proof that the water meets Mexican standard NOM-245-SSA1-2010. A fresh inspection and new sampling must follow before any decision.

How the Infection Actually Happens

Naegleria fowleri is a free-living amoeba that lives in warm fresh water and soil. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention calls it a single-celled organism.

It is found in lakes, rivers, ponds and hot springs worldwide. It is popularly known as the brain-eating amoeba, a label doctors avoid.

Infection begins when contaminated water is forced up the nose. The amoeba then travels along the olfactory nerve to the brain.

The resulting illness is primary amebic meningoencephalitis, or PAM. First symptoms usually appear about five days after exposure.

The CDC gives a range of one to 12 days. Early signs are headache, fever, nausea and vomiting.

Later come a stiff neck, confusion, seizures, hallucinations and coma. Death usually follows about five days after symptoms begin.

Why Drinking Water Is Not a Route

You cannot catch this infection by swallowing water that contains the amoeba. That is the plain wording of the CDC guidance.

The organism has to reach the nasal passages to cause disease. The infection also does not pass from one person to another.

Alcocer Gamboa repeated both points when he set out the surveillance plan. He also said there is no generalised risk to the public.

What the Authorities Have Ordered

The state government announced the alert after the laboratory confirmation. Health workers traced everyone known to have entered the water.

A total of 361 people were listed, and 180 remain under watch. Surveillance runs to 4 October 2026, counted from the last day of exposure on 3 September.

That covers two full surveillance periods after anyone last entered the water. Those on the list were given telephone numbers to report symptoms.

The warning signs are fever, severe headache, nausea, vomiting and dizziness. Officials say the detection was limited to samples from that single lake.

How Rare These Infections Are

The disease is very rare, and the numbers are small everywhere. The CDC recorded 180 cases in the United States between 1937 and 2025.

That works out at about two cases a year. Annual totals have ranged from zero to eight.

Fewer than 10 infections occur in a typical American year. More than 97 percent of recorded patients have died of it.

The CDC sets that against thousands of drowning deaths each year. A 2026 review in Infectious Disease Reports examined 66 published cases worldwide.

Those reports covered the years 2000 to 2024 and about 20 countries. Ten of the patients with a recorded outcome survived, the review found.

Mexico’s Own Record of Cases

Mexico has recorded cases since the late 1970s, mostly in the north. The health ministry’s epidemiology manual dates the first to Mexicali in 1978.

A cluster of five cases was confirmed in Mexicali in 1990. The same manual records six cases in 2002 and six in 2005.

Irrigation canals and warm standing water were the usual settings. Yucatan had never registered a case before this one.

What It Means If You Are Travelling to Yucatan

The risk to visitors stays very low on the evidence published so far. The amoeba was found in one closed lake, not in the wider water system.

Officials say that lake is not linked to cenotes or to the drinking water network. Drinking tap water and ice carry no risk, because swallowing does not transmit it.

Properly chlorinated pools and salt water do not carry the risk. The one tap-water route recorded anywhere is water forced up the nose, as in nasal rinsing.

No cenote has been closed and none has tested positive. Officials say the Merida drinking-water network is not implicated.

The precautions that matter concern the nose, not the mouth. Hold your nose or wear a nose clip when jumping into warm fresh water.

Keep your head above water in naturally hot springs. Avoid digging in or stirring up sediment in shallow fresh water.

What Is Not Yet Known

The source of the contamination in the lake has not been established publicly. The sanitary assessment of the water treatment system is still being prepared.

No date has been given for any decision on reopening. Officials have not said how long the alert will stay in force.

Whether any company faces sanctions over the lake is also unclear. No such finding has been announced by the state or by prosecutors.

The surveillance period ends on 4 October, and no second case has emerged. Health officials have not said what happens to the alert after that date.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I still swim in Yucatan’s cenotes? No cenote has been closed and none has tested positive for the amoeba. Officials say the contaminated lake is not connected to them. Is it safe to drink the water in Merida? The infection cannot be caught by swallowing water, according to the CDC. Officials also say the lake is not linked to the drinking water network. How long does the monitoring last? Surveillance runs to 4 October 2026, two full periods counted from the last day of exposure on 3 September. The current group is 180 people. How dangerous is this infection? More than 97 percent of recorded patients have died, the CDC says. It is also extremely rare, with fewer than 10 US cases most years.

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Daily Brief for Friday, September 18, 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro — A mild Friday between 17°C and 25°C, with afternoon showers likely and around three millimetres of rain forecast. Carry something light and waterproof rather than an umbrella you will regret.

The city is in the middle of its first Semana de Arte do Rio, which runs to 27 September with more than 400 attractions. A large share of the programme is free, including three events today.

Flamengo reached the Copa Libertadores semi-finals last night at the Maracanã. The club drew 1-1 with Independiente del Valle and advanced 3-1 on aggregate.

Sunset falls at 5.48 in the afternoon. Plan the outdoor part of the day for the morning and the indoor part for after four.

Weather & What to Wear

FOUR-DAY OUTLOOK

FRI 18 25°C 55% rain SAT 19 26°C 5% rain SUN 20 28°C 63% rain MON 21 33°C 55% rain

Friday sits between 17°C and 25°C with cloud and scattered afternoon showers. Forecasters differ on how much rain arrives, with estimates from a light 16 percent chance to a firmer 55 percent.

Saturday is the driest day of the four and the best one for the beach. Sunday brings a storm warning and Monday is the hottest, reaching 33°C with thunderstorms in the afternoon.

Dress for a warm afternoon rather than a cold one. A thin waterproof layer covers today, and Monday will need nothing more than sunscreen.

02

Day at a Glance

SNAPSHOT

Free at 12.30 — the XXI RioHarpFestival plays the Museu da Justiça in Centro, with no ticket required.

the XXI RioHarpFestival plays the Museu da Justiça in Centro, with no ticket required. Free at 6pm — harpist Luis Castro performs at the Centro Cultural Justiça Federal, also in Centro.

Quarteto Kalimera plays a live score to Nosferatu at the Sala Cecília Meireles in Lapa, 7pm. From R$75, about US$15 — Angra perform Holy Land in full at Vivo Rio, 7pm.

Angra perform Holy Land in full at Vivo Rio, 7pm. Metro fare — a single journey costs R$7.90, roughly US$1.54, on Lines 1, 2 and 4.

Three of today’s six main events cost nothing at all. That is the direct result of the Semana de Arte programme, which subsidises a large part of its calendar.

The free events cluster in Centro rather than the Zona Sul. A single metro ticket covers all three if you time them properly.

03

What to See & Do

FRIDAY IN RIO

The first Semana de Arte do Rio runs from 16 to 27 September and brings together more than ten separate festivals. Its organisers count over 400 attractions across the twelve days.

The Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil is free and open from nine in the morning until eight at night. It is showing Vik Muniz’s A Olho Nu until 12 October and Amazônicas, a survey of women’s work from the Amazon, until 16 November.

The CCBB is also hosting the FIL 2026 language festival from 17 to 27 September. The Cinemateca do MAM programme runs there in parallel.

The Jardim Botânico charges R$40 for residents and R$80 for foreign visitors, about US$8 and US$16. Half price applies to students, under-21s, over-60s and visitors with disabilities, not to residency alone.

The Museu do Amanhã opens Thursday to Tuesday from ten until six, with last entry at five. The Museu de Arte do Rio opens eleven until six, costs R$20 or about US$4, is free on Tuesdays and closes on Wednesdays.

Looking ahead to the weekend, the MIMO Festival plays two free nights at the Circo Voador on 19 and 20 September. It is the largest free music event of the month.

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

A single metro journey costs R$7.90, roughly US$1.54, across Lines 1, 2 and 4. A planned rise to R$8.20, about US$1.60, was slated for April and suspended.

The three free concerts today are all in Centro, within walking distance of Cinelândia and Carioca stations. The Vivo Rio show is in the Flamengo park, a short walk from Cinelândia.

Rain is forecast for the afternoon, which lengthens journeys and raises ride-hailing prices. Leaving twenty minutes earlier than usual is the cheapest response.

The city has opened a women-only intake for urban train driver training. It is a small change but a notable one for a network that has been almost entirely male.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

The Centro lunch trade runs from noon to about half past two and empties quickly afterwards. If your afternoon is built around the free concerts, eat before the RioHarpFestival rather than after.

Lapa is the natural choice for dinner before the Sala Cecília Meireles show. It is also the part of the centre that stays busy well after the concert ends.

In the Zona Sul, Botafogo and Humaitá have absorbed most of the new openings this year. Both are twenty minutes from Cinelândia by metro.

Friday bookings fill from about seven in the evening. A table before then is usually available without a reservation, even in the busier streets.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Sunset is at 5.48 in the afternoon. Beach light effectively ends around five, which is earlier than most visitors expect in September.

The CCBB closes on Tuesdays and the Museu de Arte do Rio on Wednesdays. Neither affects today, but both catch people out on a longer stay.

Card payment is universal in Centro and the Zona Sul, and instant bank transfer is accepted almost everywhere. Cash is worth carrying only for street vendors.

Rain in Rio arrives suddenly and passes quickly. A light jacket beats an umbrella on a day with wind.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

The Semana de Arte is the easiest week of the year to meet people without paying for it. Free concerts in Centro draw a mixed crowd of residents rather than a tourist one.

Portuguese is more useful at the free events than at the ticketed ones. Staff at the CCBB and the Justiça Federal centre generally speak some English.

Newcomers often underestimate how much of Rio’s culture is publicly funded and free. The Palácio Capanema concerts are a good introduction to that habit.

The city’s cultural calendar thins sharply after the first week of October. September and late November are the months to use.

08

Game Day

THE WEEKEND ROUND

Flamengo drew 1-1 with Independiente del Valle at the Maracanã last night and advanced to the Copa Libertadores semi-finals 3-1 on aggregate. Djorkaeff Reasco scored for the visitors and Giorgian De Arrascaeta equalised in the 82nd minute.

Jorginho was sent off in the 64th minute and Flamengo held on with ten men. They face Estudiantes in the semi-finals, with first legs from 13 to 15 October.

Fluminense are also through, after losing 2-1 at Platense on Tuesday but advancing 3-2 on aggregate. They meet Palmeiras in the other semi-final.

Vasco reached the Copa Sudamericana semi-finals by beating Santa Fe 2-0 at São Januário on Monday. Their opponents are Boca Juniors.

There is no Brasileirão football today. Round 28 falls on Sunday, when Flamengo host Red Bull Bragantino at the Maracanã at half past six.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

The Ibovespa closed Thursday at 185,992 points, up 0.24 percent, after falling more than one percent during the session. The dollar ended at R$5.1289, down 0.48 percent.

The central bank cut the Selic to 13.75 percent on Wednesday, its fifth consecutive quarter-point reduction. The United States Federal Reserve raised its own rate the same day.

The index has traded sideways through September without testing either edge of its range. That is a market waiting for the 4 October election rather than one taking a view on it.

For residents the practical effect is on credit rather than shares. Five consecutive cuts should start reaching mortgage and consumer rates over the coming quarter.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

The MIMO Festival plays two free nights at the Circo Voador tomorrow and Sunday. It is the single largest free event of the Semana de Arte programme.

Flamengo host Red Bull Bragantino at the Maracanã on Sunday at half past six. The league then pauses for two weeks for the international window and the election.

The Semana de Arte runs until 27 September, with the CCBB language festival ending on the same day. Vik Muniz at the CCBB continues until 12 October.

The first round of the presidential election falls on Sunday 4 October. Expect transport changes and shorter opening hours across the city that weekend.

11

Today’s headlines September 18, 2026

Flamengo Hold On With Ten Men to Reach the Libertadores Semi-Finals

Flamengo drew 1-1 with Independiente del Valle at the Maracanã on Thursday night and advanced 3-1 on aggregate. The kick-off was at half past nine in Rio, half past midnight in London.

Djorkaeff Reasco put the Ecuadorians ahead in the 30th minute. Giorgian De Arrascaeta equalised in the 82nd, by which point Flamengo had been down to ten men for eighteen minutes.

Jorginho was sent off in the 64th minute. The first leg in Quito on 10 September had finished 0-2 to Flamengo, with goals from Bruno Henrique and Léo Pereira.

Flamengo meet Estudiantes in the semi-finals. The other tie is an all-Brazilian affair between Fluminense and Palmeiras.

Montevideo City Torque Overturn Two Goals to Complete the Sudamericana Four

Montevideo City Torque beat Cienciano 3-0 at the Estadio Centenario on Thursday to reach their first continental semi-final. They had lost the first leg 2-0 in Peru.

It was the last quarter-final of the Copa Sudamericana to be decided. The result completes a semi-final line-up of Boca Juniors against Vasco da Gama and Atlético Mineiro against Torque.

Atlético Mineiro had qualified on Wednesday, beating Santos 4-2 after extra time at the Arena MRV and 3-1 on penalties. The tie finished 4-4 on aggregate after Santos won the first leg 2-0 at the Vila Belmiro.

Vasco went through on Monday, beating Santa Fe 2-0 at São Januário after a goalless first leg. The semi-finals are scheduled for 13 and 14 October with second legs on 20 and 21 October.

Latin America Sports Daily — Friday, September 18, 2026 Photo: Rafael Henrique Serra, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons

Thirty Medal Events on the Busiest Day of the South American Games

The thirteenth South American Games are running in Rosario, Santa Fe and Rafaela until 26 September. Friday is the heaviest day of the programme with thirty medal events.

Athletics, sprint canoe, track cycling, fencing, artistic and rhythmic gymnastics, shooting, weightlifting and wrestling all decide medals today. Fifteen nations are competing across 43 sports and 60 disciplines.

Brazil leads the medal table. The games opened on 12 September at the National Flag Memorial in Rosario.

The full programme covers 465 events across the two weeks. Events are also being staged in Paraná, Vicente López and Mar del Plata.

The SP Open Reaches Its Quarter-Finals in São Paulo

The SP Open, a tour-level women’s tournament, reaches its quarter-finals today at Parque Villa-Lobos in São Paulo. The final is on Sunday 20 September.

Leylah Fernandez is the top seed. The field also includes Paula Badosa, Yulia Putintseva, Tereza Valentová and Solana Sierra. Total prize money is US$283,347.

Ground passes cost R$30, about US$6, from today through the final. That is unusually cheap for a tour event and reflects a deliberate pricing decision by the organisers.

The main draw began on 14 September. It is the only tour-level women’s event in Brazil this season.

Qualifying ran on 12 and 13 September and was free to attend with a reservation. Ground passes were R$50, about US$10, from Monday to Thursday before dropping for the weekend.

Liga MX Opens Round Nine and Argentina Starts Its Tenth

Puebla host Atlante at the Estadio Cuauhtémoc this evening at seven o’clock local time. Juárez play Tigres in the second Friday fixture, with the kick-off time not published.

Toluca lead the Mexican table on nineteen points after winning a rescheduled match at Puebla. Chivas are on seventeen and América on sixteen, with two games still pending across the division.

In Argentina, the tenth round of the Clausura opens today. Central Córdoba play Defensa y Justicia at six and Racing meet Sarmiento at quarter past nine, with San Lorenzo hosting Boca on Sunday.

There is no Brasileirão football today. Round 28 falls on Sunday, with Flamengo hosting Red Bull Bragantino at the Maracanã and Palmeiras meeting Grêmio.

Around the Region

Flamengo lead the Brazilian league on 57 points from 27 matches, one ahead of Palmeiras. Athletico and Bahia share third place on 46.

Colo-Colo lead the Chilean Primera División on 54 points from 23 matches, twelve clear of the field. It is the largest lead in any major league on the continent.

Lionel Messi’s farewell match for Argentina is set for 6 October against Benin at the Monumental in Buenos Aires. It falls inside the October international window.

There is no Formula One race this weekend. The championship resumes in Azerbaijan from 24 to 26 September.

Mexican wrestling marks its biggest night of the year today. The CMLL 93rd Anniversary show is staged at the Arena México in the capital.

Saturday brings a full Argentine programme. River Plate host Huracán at seven, Unión meet Independiente at quarter to five and Instituto play Talleres at quarter past nine.
