The Philippine Coast Guard said the ship had been carrying out a mission intended to support Filipino fishermen operating in the area.





China's embassy in Manila had not immediately responded to a request for comment on the incident.

Tensions remain high in disputed waters

The latest confrontation adds to a series of incidents between Manila and Beijing in contested areas of the South China Sea.

In July, the Philippines accused China of using water cannon against its government vessels near Scarborough Shoal.

Manila also alleged that a Philippine Navy staff member was struck on the head with a wooden baton during an encounter near Second Thomas Shoal.

The two countries have repeatedly confronted each other over competing claims in the South China Sea, with the Philippines maintaining that its vessels have the right to operate in areas within its claimed maritime zone.

World.title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.

The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.

A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.

The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.

Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.





He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.

On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.

Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.

Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.

On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.

Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.

Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.

World.title: FSSAI flags Nestle infant products over false promotional claims, biotin levels
World.content:
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) on Friday initiated legal action against Nestle India over alleged non-compliance involving its NAN Excella Pro Stage 1 and Lactogen Pro 1 infant nutrition products.

FSSAI said it examined the products and their promotional material available on e-commerce platforms. In the case of NAN Excella Pro Stage 1, the regulator flagged claims relating to â5 HMOsâ and âWhey Proteinâ. For Lactogen Pro 1, it raised concerns over a claim that the productâs âWhey Proteinâ was easy to digest.

According to FSSAI, both products were found to be in contravention of Regulation 4(2) of the Food Safety and Standards (Foods for Infant Nutrition) Regulations, 2020.

The provision restricts promotional claims and material intended to increase the saleability of infant foods. The regulator also cited Section 3 of the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods (Regulation of Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 1992, which prohibits their  and promotion.

FSSAI said it had sought clarifications from Nestle India regarding the claims.

Separately, a sample of a follow-up formula manufactured by Nestle India was found to be sub-standard for its biotin content during laboratory analysis.





The sample was sent for re-analysis, but the referral laboratory also found it non-conforming with the prescribed biotin requirement under the 2020 regulations.

In view of the alleged violations, FSSAI said three separate adjudication cases have been filed against Nestle India in relation to the products. The action covers both promotional claims and the laboratory finding concerning biotin content.

World.title: Blast rips through mosque during Friday prayers in northwest Pakistan; 16 killed, dozens injured
World.content:
At least 16 people were killed and dozens injured in a powerful suicide blast during Friday prayers (September 18, 2026) at a mosque near police lines in Kohat district in northwest Pakistan, officials said.

The blast occurred at the mosque located near the old Police Lines in Kohat district, around 60 kilometres southwest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's capital Peshawar, they said.

At least 16 people, including five police personnel and 11 civilians, were killed in the suicide blast at the Kohat Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province during Friday prayers, provincial Police Chief Zulfiqar Hameed said.

No group or individual has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Citing District Headquarters Hospital's MS Tahir Ali Shah, Geo News reported that 15 bodies were brought to the hospital along with over 50 injured following the blast.

Most of those wounded were worshippers, police said, adding that the blast caused a crater outside the mosque.

According to Rescue 1122 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa spokesperson Bilal Ahmad Faizi, rescue teams reached the site shortly after receiving the information and launched a rescue operation.

He said several of those injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for initial medical treatment.

The spokesperson said rescue teams were present at the scene and assessing the situation.

World.title: Kuppam’s flowers now wilt by 8 a.m.: El Niño scorches Andhra’s flower basket, cuts output by 40%
World.content:
For 30 years, Munemma’s day began at 4 a.m., among the kanakambara (Crossandra infundibuliformis) plants on her acre at Rallabaduguru village. This March, she woke to a heat that had already settled over the field, and to flowers that had given up before the day had begun.

“The delicate flowers wilted on the plants themselves, unable to bear the intense heat,” says Munemma, 56, a small farmer in Shantipuram mandal, in Andhra Pradesh’s flower basket at the tri-junction with Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. “Usually, kanakambara, delicate as it is, holds its freshness on the plant till 11 a.m. But this year, since March, the flowers started wilting by 8 a.m.,” she says.

Kuppam, at the southern tip of Andhra Pradesh, sends flowers to four cities in three States every day of the year. This year, traders say, the tonnage is down by at least 40%, the blooms are smaller and lighter, and growers are being paid less for them.

Munemma is one of 3,000 small and marginal farmers spread across 2,000 acres in the core flower belt of Kuppam revenue division. The belt covers several village clusters: Mallanur, Nadimur and Chinnagandlapalle in Kuppam mandal; Shantipuram, Syamarajupuram, Dandikuppam and Thummanapalle in Shantipuram mandal; Gudupalle and Amudagondi in Gudupalle mandal; forested hamlets in Ramakuppam mandal; V. Kota, Kadiriobandlapalle and Pothur in V. Kota mandal; and Pathikonda on the Palamaner fringe.

Kuppam mandal got 100.8 mm of rain between June 1 and September 18, against a normal of 400.1 mm, a shortfall of 75%, according to the State’s water resources portal, Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Information and Management System (APWRIMS). Gudupalle was 74% short and V. Kota 68%. Every district in the State is short of rain this monsoon.

Monsoon rain fell short across the flower belt

Mandal / area Rain, June 1 to Sept. 18 (mm) Normal (mm) Shortfall (%) Kuppam 100.8 400.1 75 Gudupalle 104.4 397.4 74 V. Kota 124.2 384.7 68 Ramakuppam 199.1 314.3 37 Shantipuram 241.4 378.0 36 Chittoor district 179.9 392.4 54 Andhra Pradesh 252.4 504.4 50

Source: APWRIMS

Chittoor is among 315 districts mapped by the Centre as vulnerable to El Niño, with four Rayalaseema districts flagged as high-risk. The heat has stayed high in Kuppam since March. March highs averaged 32.8 to 33.6 degrees Celsius and lows 19.3 to 20.1 degrees. April and May sustained highs of 34.8 to 35.5 degrees, with lows of 23.9 degrees, and a heat index of 40 to 45 degrees. June highs were 30 to 32.6 degrees; July and August, 29 to 31.1 degrees. With humidity holding at 63% to 68% through the heat, fungal rot has spread across the region.

March and April together brought 3.7 mm against a normal of 37.6 mm. May was wet, 113.7 mm against a normal of 90.6 mm, but July brought 5.8 mm against 82.5 mm.

Horticulture scientists at Dr. Y.S.R. Horticultural University say a flower crop needs a diurnal range of 15 to 18 degrees, the gap between day and night temperatures, in December and January for flower bud initiation. In Kuppam division, the gap came late in January, and the March heat set in early. Flowering was delayed by four weeks, and the blooms lost weight, fragrance and shelf life.

Normally, Kuppam farmers send out over six tonnes a day, in varieties such as jasmine, kanakambara, marigold, chrysanthemum and polyhouse rose, to Bengaluru, Chennai, Coimbatore and Vijayawada by the express trains that halt at Kuppam, with larger consignments going by road from Kolar.

“The figure is about 180 tonnes a month, with the Dasara outflow crossing 800 tonnes. This year, the tonnage is down by at least 40%,” says Krupa, 38, a flower merchant from Ambur in neighbouring Tamil Nadu, who buys from several growers in Kuppam.

The dry monsoon has followed a falling water table. In Chittoor district, groundwater stood 16.64 metres below ground on September 18, 4.2 metres deeper than a year earlier, the APWRIMS portal shows. It is deeper than a year ago in every Rayalaseema district.

The water table has fallen across Rayalaseema

District Depth on Sept. 18, 2026 (m) Deeper than a year earlier (m) Sri Sathya Sai 21.65 10.85 Annamayya 18.97 8.49 Ananthapuramu 16.26 5.88 Nandyal 10.61 5.40 Chittoor 16.64 4.20 Kurnool 9.27 3.55 YSR Kadapa 13.92 3.42 Tirupati 10.12 1.94 Rayalaseema average 14.68 5.47 Andhra Pradesh 11.27 3.26

Source: APWRIMS

Business at the Kuppam flower market yard averages ₹9 crore a month. Prices rise by 60% to 200% during festival seasons, as they did in August 2025.

This year, under the shadow of El Niño, marigold fetched ₹120 a kg wholesale at Kuppam and sold at ₹400 retail in Bengaluru; kanakambara ₹3,000 against ₹6,000 in Chennai; jasmine ₹800 to ₹1,200 against double that in the metros; and polyhouse rose ₹8 a flower locally against ₹40 in the metros.

Gudupalle mandal recorded 4 mm of rain this August, against a normal of 106.5 mm and 161.8 mm last August, the APWRIMS data shows.

Rajesh, a farmer from Gudupalle, says he sold his half-acre yield of several flower varieties for ₹23,000 in August. “The same month last year, the yield fetched me ₹58,000. The buyer says the flowers are small, so the rate is low. What can we do if the sun itself burns them?” he asks.

World.title: Walgreens to set up Global Capability Centre in Chennai, create over 250 jobs in first year
World.content:
Tamil Nadu’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem continues to attract companies, with Walgreens, one of the leading healthcare and pharmacy companies in the U.S. setting up a new GCC in Chennai. An MoU regarding this was signed with Walgreens India Private Limited on Friday (September 18, 2026), in the presence of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and Industries Minister S. Keerthana.

The proposed GCC will focus on technology and business services and is expected to create more than 250 employment opportunities in its first year, with further expansion planned over the coming years.

The centre will be located at DLF Downtown, Taramani, in Chennai’s emerging GCC ecosystem. The investment comes on the heels of the State government announcing the Tamil Nadu Global Capability Centres Corridor and Development Programme in the Assembly recently, covering key employment corridors across Chennai and aimed at enabling the next generation of GCCs to establish, expand, and scale in the State.

According to a statement, the centre will enable Walgreens to build critical technology and business capabilities from Chennai to support its enterprise operations, while creating high-value employment opportunities for the State’s skilled workforce.

World.title: Holiday for three education institutes in Tirthahalli on account of CM’s visit to discuss K. Kasturirangan report on Western Ghats
World.content:
The Tirthahalli taluk administration has declared a holiday on September 19 for a few local education institutions citing a visit by Karnataka’s Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and his cabinet colleagues to the town for a public discussion on the K. Kasturirangan report on the Western Ghats.

The tahsildar’s official memo announced that the Government Pre-university College, U.R. Ananthamurthy High School, and the Government First-grade College in Tirthahalli will remain closed on September 19. This decision was taken to ensure the safety of children, given the anticipated heavy traffic in the town.

As per the CM’s tour plan, he will depart Mangaluru by helicopter at 9.30 a.m. on September 19 and arrive at the helipad at the Government First Grade College in Tirthahalli at 10 a.m. There, he will meet people, elected representatives, and representatives of various organisations regarding the K. Kasturirangan report.

After the meeting, he will leave for Balehonnur in N.R. Pura taluk of Chikkamagaluru district at 12.30 p.m. At Balehonnur, he will listen to the views and grievances of people on the K. Kasturirangan report. He is expected to leave for Bengaluru by 4 p.m.

The CM will be accompanied by Deputy CM G. Parameshwara, Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy, and Minister for School Education Madhu Bangarappa.

World.title: Surendra Koli, accused in Nithari killings, found dead in his Haridwar tea shop
World.content:
Surendra Koli, the man at the centre of the sensational Nithari killings who was subsequently acquitted in all 13 cases, was found dead in his tea stall in Haridwar, Uttarakhand on Friday (September 18, 2026), police said.

Koli, who worked as a domestic help at the Noida house of businessman Moninder Singh Pandher, appears to have ended his life, police said.

Sub-Inspector at the Haridwar Kotwali police station Vikram Bisht told PTI that the Saptarishi police outpost received information that a man had been found dead in a tea shop on Sapt Sarovar road. The deceased was identified as Koli, a resident of Mangrukhal in Almora.

Shishupal Singh Negi, circle officer, city, told PTIVideos that Koli was living in Haridwar for some time and running a tea stall on rent.

"Police received information this morning that a person had been found dead. Our forensic team reached the spot. At present, it appears to be a case of suicide. The body is in police custody, and the panchanama and post-mortem proceedings are underway," he said.

The Nithari case came to light in 2006 when skeletal remains, skulls and bones were discovered from the backyard and drains near a bungalow belonging to Pandher in Sector 31, Noida.

The gruesome findings, unearthing the disappearance and killings of several children and women, had triggered nationwide outrage and terrorised the local community.

Pandher, a co-accused in the case, was also in jail for years but was released on October 20, 2023 following his acquittal in the case.

Koli, the only convict in the sensational 2006 Nithari mass killings case, was acquitted by the Supreme Court in 2025 in the last such case.

It was the 13th case in the Nithari killings in which Koli was acquitted. He was earlier acquitted in the 12 other related cases.

Allowing Koli's curative petition challenging his conviction in the case related to the alleged rape and murder of a 15-year-old girl in Nithari, the apex court had said criminal law does not permit conviction on conjecture or on a hunch.

A bench comprising Chief Justice B R Gavai and Justices Surya Kant and Vikram Nath had said the offences in Nithari were heinous and the suffering of the families was beyond measure.

"It is a matter of deep regret that despite prolonged investigation, the identity of the actual perpetrator has not been established in a manner that meets the legal standards," the bench had said.

It said that suspicion, however grave, cannot replace proof beyond a reasonable doubt, and the courts cannot prefer expediency over legality.

"The presumption of innocence endures until guilt is proved through admissible and reliable evidence; and when proof fails, the only lawful outcome is to set aside the conviction even in a case involving horrific crimes," the bench had said.
